returned_results.slogan: A sparse vector can be exactly recovered by solving a minimization problem under certain conditions. The recovery is guaranteed if the restricted isometry constant is less than a specific bound. This bound depends on the sparsity level, a maximum sparsity parameter, and a value between zero and one. Two different functions yield distinct bounds for the restricted isometry constant.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.1

returned_results.slogan: Given a matrix U covered by a sparsity pattern with l levels and ratio constant, if its RIP constant is below a specific bound, then any solution to the l1 minimization problem approximates a vector x from noisy measurements. The error in the l1 norm is bounded by a constant times the best s-term approximation error plus a term proportional to the noise level. The error in the l2 norm is similarly bounded, with constants depending on the RIP constant and the sparsity pattern parameters. The constants in the bounds depend solely on the RIP constant.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.4

returned_results.slogan: The theorem considers functions with sparse coefficient vectors and a measurement matrix with a bounded restricted isometry constant. Under given conditions on parameters, with high probability, a sum over indices exceeds half the total count for all relevant tuples. This implies that, with the same high probability, two inequalities hold simultaneously for more than half of the indices. The first bounds a function norm by the coefficient vector norm, and the second provides upper and lower bounds on an inner product in terms of a coefficient subvector norm.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4

returned_results.slogan: A matrix with restricted isometry properties and sparse columns must satisfy a lower bound on its column sparsity. The sparsity parameter s times the logarithm of m divided by s times k is at least on the order of the logarithm of n divided by k. This holds when the matrix satisfies the RIP-1 condition with sufficiently small error. The result relates the dimensions and sparsity of the matrix to its restricted isometry properties.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5 (\cite{N10})

trajectory.query: for fixed sparse vector subsampled Gaussian circulant absolute values concentration sqrt(pi/2) l1 to l2 expectation

returned_results.slogan: For a fixed subset I, consider a random circulant matrix A generated by a Gaussian vector. If the size of I is sufficiently large relative to parameters s, N, kappa, and eta, then the supremum of the norm of A times any s-sparse vector x, normalized by the square root of m, is bounded by 1 plus kappa. This bound holds with probability at least 1 minus eta.

returned_results.slogan: A randomly subsampled Gaussian circulant matrix allows for stable sparse recovery using L1 minimization. The result holds with high probability when the number of measurements m meets a certain bound relative to sparsity s, dimension N, and failure probability eta. The recovery error is bounded by the best s-term approximation error plus a noise term. The bound on m depends on s, N, and eta through several logarithmic factors.
returned_results.name: Corollary 6.1

returned_results.slogan: A constant C exists such that for any subset of sparse vectors with bounded p-norm, the expected supremum of the inner product with a Gaussian matrix is bounded. The bound depends on the Gaussian complexity of the subset and the expected dual norm of a Gaussian vector. It also includes terms involving the dimension n and sparsity s, scaled by logarithmic factors. The result holds for all sparsity levels between 1 and n.

returned_results.slogan: The expected value of the L1 norm of a vector with independent standard Gaussian entries is at least the square root of two d over pi times the expected value of its L2 norm.

returned_results.slogan: The expected value of the L1 norm of a vector with independent standard Gaussian entries is at least the square root of two d over pi times the expected value of its L2 norm.

returned_results.slogan: The theorem establishes uniform concentration bounds for the average of certain matrices under a sparse Gaussian model. It provides a high probability bound on the deviation of a specific submatrix from its expected value. The result holds for matrices defined with sparsity parameter s between 1 and K-1. The bound involves constants related to the Gaussian distribution and the matrix dimensions.
returned_results.name: Lemma A.1

returned_results.slogan: A randomly subsampled Gaussian circulant matrix scaled by a constant satisfies the RIP1,2 property with high probability under given conditions. Another matrix formed by appending a vector also satisfies an effective RIP1,2 property under different assumptions. Both results hold with probability at least one minus a small parameter. The conditions depend on sparsity, dimensions, and tolerance parameters.

returned_results.slogan: For an s-sparse vector and a matrix with independent Gaussian rows, the average of certain quadratic forms concentrates around a specific matrix. This holds with high probability when the number of measurements exceeds a constant times the support size times the logarithm of the dimension ratio. The deviation is bounded by a small fraction of the squared norm of the vector. The result applies to any subset containing the true support and not exceeding a given size.
returned_results.name: Lemma B.1

returned_results.slogan: A symmetric matrix with Gaussian entries has its projection onto a sparse pattern bounded in terms of vector norms. The bound depends on the standard deviation, the sparsity parameter, and logarithmic factors. The inequality holds when the expected number of entries is sufficiently large relative to the dimension. The result applies to vectors independent of the specific row and column sampling.

returned_results.slogan: A random partial circulant matrix A satisfies an expected restricted isometry property. The expected deviation between the squared norm of Ax and the squared norm of x is bounded by a constant alpha. This holds uniformly for all k-sparse vectors x. The required number of rows m grows proportionally to k times log squared k times log squared n divided by alpha squared.

returned_results.slogan: The expected supremum of the deviation between the norm of BAx and the Frobenius norm of B times the norm of x over sparse vectors in a scaled ball is bounded by a constant times the operator norm of B multiplied by a term involving the radius, sparsity, and the logarithm of the dimension ratio. The result holds for Gaussian random matrices and sparse vectors within a closed ball.

returned_results.slogan: The expected supremum over a set of vectors with bounded norms is at most a constant times the sum of the first norm bound and the square root of the sparsity times the second norm bound, multiplied by the square root of the logarithm of the dimension divided by sparsity.
returned_results.name: Lemma 8.1

returned_results.slogan: The expected supremum of the norm of a random sum over sparse subsets is bounded by a constant times the sum of two supremum norms. The constant depends on the entry bound and the sparsity parameter. This result extends a fundamental lemma by Rudelson and Vershynin. It applies to vectors with uniformly bounded entries.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.3

returned_results.slogan: With high probability, the supremum of the norm of a sparse linear combination of random vectors is bounded. The bound depends on the maximum norm of the vectors and a term involving the sparsity and sample size. The probability of this bound holding is at least one minus a constant divided by a power of the sample size. The constants in the bound depend on absolute values and parameters related to the distribution.

The inequality relates the sum to the operator norm of a covariance matrix and the norm of another vector. This result occurs with high probability.

returned_results.slogan: The supremum of the absolute inner product between a noise vector and a design matrix applied to sparse vectors is bounded. This bound depends on the noise standard deviation, the vector norm, a constant, and the square root of a logarithmic term. The inequality holds with high probability. The probability is at least one minus an exponentially small term in the minimum of the sample size and a sparsity-dependent logarithmic factor.

The result applies to all sparse vectors in a specified set.

returned_results.slogan: The universal stable manifold consists of pairs of curves and metrics satisfying a gradient flow equation converging to a critical point. A submersion maps each such pair to the starting point of the curve. This mapping is a submersion away from the constant curve at the critical point. It is a submersion everywhere if the Morse index of the critical point is zero.

returned_results.slogan: On a closed manifold with a Morse function and a gradient-like vector field, the flow from any point converges to critical points as time goes to positive or negative infinity. Each unstable manifold is diffeomorphic to a Euclidean space of dimension between zero and the dimension of the manifold.

returned_results.slogan: For p=2, a smooth solution of the flow equation converges smoothly to a critical point of the energy functional as time goes to infinity, up to reparametrization. returned_results.slogan: The solution to the gradient flow equation with initial data in a specific function space and a parameter value of at least two exists for all time. The maximal time of existence is infinite. The solution does not blow up in finite time.

returned_results.slogan: On a compact Riemannian manifold with a Morse-Bott function, every gradient flow line converges to a critical point as time goes to infinity. returned_results.slogan: An unstable minimal hypersurface with finite total curvature in Euclidean space has a Morse index I. There exists an I-dimensional family of ancient mean curvature flows. These flows are asymptotic to the hypersurface as time approaches negative infinity.

returned_results.slogan: A closed, smoothly embedded minimal submanifold with finite Morse index in a Riemannian manifold gives rise to an I-parameter family of ancient mean curvature flows defined for all negative times. These flows are uniquely determined by their configuration at time zero. They converge exponentially fast to the original minimal submanifold as time goes to negative infinity.

The limit of the associated measures forms a Brakke flow that converges to an equatorial sphere and the Clifford torus at positive and negative infinity, respectively.

returned_results.slogan: A gradient flow line converges to critical points of the function as the parameter tends to positive or negative infinity.

returned_results.slogan: On a compact boundaryless manifold with a Morse function, the gradient flow trajectories have well-defined limits as time goes to positive and negative infinity. These limits are critical points of the function.

returned_results.slogan: On a compact Riemannian manifold with a Morse-Bott function, every gradient flow line converges to a critical point as time goes to infinity. The convergence is exponential, meaning the speed of the flow decays at an exponential rate. The same behavior occurs as time goes to negative infinity.

returned_results.slogan: For a smooth Morse pair generating a Morse-Smale gradient flow, every point in the unit cotangent bundle excluding the stable set approaches the unstable set as time goes to negative infinity. Similarly, every point excluding the unstable set approaches the stable set as time goes to positive infinity. This convergence is measured by the distance function on the unit cotangent bundle. The result describes the asymptotic behavior of the lifted flow on the cotangent bundle.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.6

returned_results.slogan: Assume a Morse vector field on a Banach manifold has a Lyapunov function. Let x and y be rest points such that the closure of the intersection of their unstable and stable manifolds is compact. Consider a sequence of points in this intersection and the flow lines through them, including the endpoints. A subsequence of these sets converges in Hausdorff distance to a broken flow line connecting x to y.

returned_results.slogan: On a complete Riemannian manifold, consider a smooth proper function bounded from below. If the negative gradient flow of the function exists for all negative time, then every backward orbit accumulates in the critical set. Specifically, for any point and any sequence of times going to negative infinity, a subsequence of the flow converges to a critical point.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.28

returned_results.slogan: A continuous flow exists on the unstable manifold with a unique stationary point at x. Near x, this flow coincides with the original flow for negative times. Every point in the unstable manifold converges to x in negative time. For non-stationary points, the positive time limit lies in the boundary of the unstable manifold, and this limit depends continuously on the initial point.
returned_results.name: Theorem 7.1

returned_results.slogan: The flow of a vector field defines stable and unstable manifolds at critical points of a function. The unstable manifold consists of points whose backward flow converges to the critical point. The stable manifold consists of points whose forward flow converges to the critical point. These manifolds are open submanifolds diffeomorphic to Euclidean spaces whose dimensions depend on the Morse index.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.7 (Stable Manifold Theorem)

returned_results.slogan: The omega-limit set of any point under the gradient flow of a Morse-Bott function on a Riemannian manifold is a single critical point. Every solution of the gradient flow converges to an equilibrium point.

This function is defined as the integral of a positive twice-differentiable test function against a certain measure, minus a term linear in time. The linear term depends on the initial energy bound and the maximum norm of the test function. The result holds for all nonnegative times.

returned_results.slogan: The total energy functional decreases over time for solutions of the projected Allen-Cahn equation. The derivative of the total energy with respect to time is non-positive. This implies the energy does not increase as time progresses.

returned_results.slogan: The energy of the solution to the Allen-Cahn equation decreases over time due to dissipation. The total energy at any time plus the dissipated energy equals the initial energy. This holds for all times within the considered interval. The initial data is assumed to be bounded between negative one and one.
returned_results.name: Lemma 8 (Energy dissipation equality for bounded weak solutions)

returned_results.slogan: The Allen-Cahn equation with a general positive mobility is energy dissipative. The rate of change of the energy is negative and given by two integral terms. These integrals involve the time derivative of the trajectory and the spatial derivative. The energy itself is defined by an integral combining a gradient squared term and a potential function.

returned_results.slogan: The Allen-Cahn equation in Lagrangian coordinates follows an energy dissipation law. The rate of change of the total energy equals the negative of a dissipation integral. This integral involves the time derivative of the position and the gradient of the initial data. The dissipation term is always non-positive, indicating energy decreases over time.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.1

returned_results.slogan: An initial function with finite energy leads to a weak solution of the Allen-Cahn equation. The solution satisfies an energy dissipation identity, where the energy at time T plus an integral of the time derivative squared equals the initial energy. The second spatial derivatives and the derivative of the potential are square-integrable over space and time. This regularity allows testing the equation with the gradient of the solution.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.3

returned_results.slogan: Given an initial function with finite energy, a weak solution to the Allen-Cahn equation exists. This solution satisfies an energy dissipation inequality over time. The second spatial derivatives and the gradient of the potential are square integrable. This regularity allows testing the weak equation with second derivatives.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.3

returned_results.slogan: The sequence defined by minimizing a certain functional leads to unconditional energy stability. Each iterate has energy less than or equal to that of the previous iterate. This holds for the energy functional associated with the Allen-Cahn equation. The result ensures non-increasing energy throughout the minimization process.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.1

returned_results.slogan: The energy of a solution to the parabolic PDE decreases over time. The time derivative of the energy equals the negative integral of the squared time derivative of the solution. This implies that the energy is non-increasing. The result holds for the given energy functional.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.1

returned_results.slogan: The energy functional decreases over time. The integral of the squared L2 norm of the time derivative plus the energy at time t equals the initial energy. The time derivative of the squared L2 norm of the solution is negative twice the Nehair functional.

There exists a family of diffeomorphisms parameterized by negative time. The pullbacks of the metric and three-form under these diffeomorphisms converge to the original soliton data. Otherwise, the convergence is at a polynomial rate proportional to one over the square root of time.

returned_results.slogan: Every trajectory of the negative gradient flow of f converges to a unique limit point. If the limit lies in the principal orbit-type stratum or the isotropy group remains constant, the convergence is exponentially fast. Otherwise, the convergence rate is at most a constant times t to the negative one-half. The map sending each point to its limit under the flow is a deformation retraction onto the critical set.

returned_results.slogan: The negative gradient flow of the squared norm function converges to a critical point for any initial condition. The flow is defined on a space with a group action and a map. The limit exists as time goes to infinity. The result holds under the assumptions of the referenced theorem.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.6

returned_results.slogan: A gradient flow line converges exponentially fast to a limit point if it eventually stays in a neighborhood of that point and has a sequence approaching it. The convergence rate is bounded by an exponential decay function. The constants in the bound are independent of the specific flow line. A similar result applies for sequences tending to negative infinity.

returned_results.slogan: An ancient, embedded, and weakly convex solution to mean curvature flow converges exponentially fast in smooth topology to a unique equator as time goes to negative infinity.

returned_results.slogan: A critical point without Killing fields has a neighborhood where the negative gradient flow from any nearby initial condition converges smoothly to a critical point. The convergence occurs exponentially fast in any C^k norm.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1

returned_results.slogan: When m equals three, each ancient solution from a specific family develops a type I singularity at a finite negative time. The rescaled metrics converge as time approaches the singularity. The limit is a Riemannian product of an Einstein metric and a Euclidean space.
returned_results.name: Theorem 25

returned_results.slogan: A gradient flow line converging to a Morse critical point has all its derivatives decaying exponentially fast. This decay occurs for all orders of derivatives after a sufficiently large time. The exponential rate is uniform, and the bound constants depend on the derivative order. A similar result applies for convergence in negative time.

returned_results.slogan: A strong solution to a gradient flow in a Hilbert space converges in norm if the energy functional satisfies a Lojasiewicz-Simon inequality. The inequality bounds the gradient norm from below by a power of the energy difference relative to a critical point. This bound ensures the time integral of the velocity norm is finite. Consequently, the solution converges to a limit in the Hilbert space as time goes to infinity.

returned_results.slogan: A critical point of the energy functional satisfies a Lojasiewicz-Simon inequality. The inequality bounds the energy difference by the gradient norm near that point. This holds for functions sufficiently close in the Sobolev norm. The exponents and constants depend on the specific critical point.

returned_results.slogan: A smooth critical point of a specific energy functional is considered. If a gradient flow starts sufficiently close to this point in a high-regularity norm and the energy remains above the critical value under certain conditions, then the flow exists globally. The flow converges smoothly, after reparameterization, to another critical point with the same energy value.

This holds when the energy functional is proper, semiconvex, and lower semicontinuous. The result assumes the energy satisfies the Kurdyka-Lojasiewicz-Simon inequality near that limit point. The convergence occurs in the topology associated with the energy functional.

returned_results.slogan: A continuously differentiable function solving the equation converges in norm to a stationary point of the energy functional, provided its trajectory closure is compact and the energy satisfies a Lojasiewicz gradient inequality near stationary points. The convergence rate depends on the Lojasiewicz exponent at the limit point. If the exponent is one-half, convergence is exponentially fast. If the exponent is between zero and one-half, convergence follows a polynomial rate.

returned_results.slogan: A function with compact superlevel sets and isolated critical points ensures that every solution to the gradient flow equation converges to a critical point as time goes to infinity.

The limit is a critical point of the given energy functional. The energy of the limit does not exceed the initial bound.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.5

returned_results.slogan: A regular closed curve with constant speed initial data gives rise to a family of curves solving a gradient flow equation in a weak sense. The curves maintain constant speed parametrization for all time. As time goes to infinity, a subsequence of these curves, when translated, converges to a critical point of the energy functional. If V star V is in the commutant of A and V A V star is a subset of A, then the map delta_V from A to A is an endomorphism. Additionally, V star to the k times V to the k is in the commutant of A for every positive integer k.

If A contains the identity and both V V star and V star V are in the commutant of A, then several conditions are equivalent. These include V star V being a projection, V V star being a projection, and the maps defined by conjugation with V or V star being morphisms.

This holds when T times A times S is contained in A, and the product S T lies in the commutant of A. The conditions ensure that alpha preserves the algebraic structure.

returned_results.slogan: Given a dynamical system with a C-star algebra and an action by extendible endomorphisms, certain maps define a partial-isometric covariant representation. The associated homomorphism is an isomorphism onto a specific corner of a crossed product algebra. This isomorphism preserves the structure of the representation maps. The partial-isometric crossed product is a full corner in the larger crossed product algebra.

returned_results.slogan: An endomorphism alpha on A and an ideal J in A define J-covariance for a representation when J is contained in the set where SS star pi of a equals pi of a. The C star algebra C star of A, alpha, and J is generated by j A of A and j A of A times s, where j A and s are universal for such representations. If alpha is extendible, then s lies in the multiplier algebra, and the algebra is also generated by j A of A and s times j A of A. Isomorphisms relate this algebra to other crossed product and endomorphism C star algebras for different choices of J.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.26

returned_results.slogan: An extendible endomorphism alpha of a C-star algebra A satisfies a relation with a non-degenerate homomorphism pi into a multiplier algebra and a partial isometry v. The condition pi of alpha of a times v equals v times pi of a for all a, and v times v conjugate equals the extension of pi applied to the extension of alpha of the unit, holds if and only if pi of alpha of a equals v times pi of a times v conjugate for all a. Additionally, v conjugate times v times pi of a must equal pi of a times v conjugate times v for all a.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.3

returned_results.slogan: Given a covariant faithful representation of a C-star algebra with an endomorphism, there exists an extension of the representation to the coefficient algebra. This extension is an isomorphism onto the C-star algebra generated by the iterated adjoint actions of the representation. The extended representation remains covariant and faithful with respect to the extended endomorphism and its inverse. The covariance conditions relate the extended representation to the unitary operator through conjugation.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.10

trajectory.query: Stacey crossed product multiplicity one isometric representation A-covariant endomorphism

returned_results.slogan: Given an Exel system and an ideal J contained in a specific inverse image, there exists a unique isometry V in the multiplier algebra of a certain C*-algebra. This isometry satisfies a covariance relation and induces an endomorphism on the core algebra. The endomorphism is injective, extendible, and its range is characterized by a projection. The pair consisting of the identity map and V forms a covariant representation that yields an isomorphism between the Stacey crossed product and the original algebra.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.1

returned_results.slogan: An extendible injective endomorphism with a specified range defines an Exel system. The universal representation and an isometry form a Stacey-covariant representation. The resulting map is an isomorphism between the Stacey crossed product and another crossed product algebra.
returned_results.name: Theorem 6.2

returned_results.slogan: Suppose an endomorphism acts on a C-star algebra, and there is a Stacey-covariant representation with a faithful star-homomorphism. If there exists a strongly continuous circle group action fixing the homomorphism's image and scaling the isometry by the circle parameter, then the integrated representation is faithful on the crossed product by the natural numbers.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.1

returned_results.slogan: Suppose an endomorphism acts on a C-star algebra, and there is a Stacey-covariant representation with a faithful star-homomorphism. If there exists a strongly continuous circle group action on the image algebra that fixes the homomorphism and scales the isometry by the circle parameter, then the integrated representation is faithful on the crossed product by the natural numbers.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.1

returned_results.slogan: Given a C-star algebra with a faithful trace and a nonunitary isometry satisfying certain invariance conditions, define an endomorphism using the isometry. The Stacey crossed product formed from this endomorphism is isomorphic to the Paschke crossed product built from the algebra and isometry. This crossed product is a simple C-star algebra.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.4 (\cite{Ortega}, Example 1.19)

returned_results.slogan: Given a unital weak-star continuous isometric endomorphism alpha on L infinity X mu, and a representation of Stacey's crossed product L infinity X mu times alpha n N on L squared X mu, several conditions are equivalent. The crossed products L infinity X mu times alpha n N and L infinity X mu times alpha m N are star-isomorphic while fixing L infinity X mu elementwise. There exists a representation of L infinity X mu times alpha m N on L squared X mu. The values n and m are equal. The tensor algebras L infinity X mu times alpha T n plus and L infinity X mu times alpha T m plus are completely isometrically isomorphic while fixing L infinity X mu elementwise.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.6

returned_results.slogan: An injective endomorphism beta exists on the fixed point algebra of the Exel crossed product. This endomorphism satisfies a specific formula involving the canonical maps and is extendible with a particular projection property. The identity map and the canonical isometry form a Stacey-covariant representation. The induced map is an isomorphism between the Stacey crossed product and the original Exel crossed product.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.1

returned_results.slogan: Given an Exel system with an almost faithful L on a specific set, an endomorphism beta exists on the direct limit C_infinity. This beta satisfies a conjugation relation and is both extendible and injective with a particular range. An isomorphism kappa from C_infinity to a fixed point algebra and an isometry V form a Stacey-covariant representation. The pair induces an isomorphism from the Stacey crossed product to the Cuntz-Pimsner algebra.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.3

returned_results.slogan: A unital C-star algebra with a unital injective star-endomorphism always has a covariant representation consisting of a Hilbert space, a star-homomorphism, and an isometry. This representation satisfies the covariance condition relating the endomorphism to the isometry.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.1

returned_results.slogan: The isometric representation from P to bounded operators on L-squared of A has multiplicity one. If an additive cocycle exists for this representation, then every component of the cocycle is identically zero.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.4

trajectory.query: crossed product by endomorphism universal operator belongs to multiplier algebra proposition

returned_results.slogan: A uniformly bounded family of operators with uniformly bounded propagation yields a unique multiplier in a certain crossed product algebra. This multiplier restricts to a specific sequence under an identification with a function space. The multiplier's image under a canonical projection matches the image of a direct sum under a different map. Both images coincide in the maximal crossed product algebra.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.15

returned_results.slogan: The initial projection of the universal partial isometry lies in the multiplier algebra of the crossed product C-star algebra.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2.12

returned_results.slogan: A faithful representation of a crossed product algebra implies that if the unitary operators are equal, then the corresponding multipliers must also be equal.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.3

returned_results.slogan: An element in the tensor product of two operator algebras is a universal multiplier exactly when its induced weak-star continuous mapping is completely bounded.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.4

returned_results.slogan: Given a dynamical system with extendible endomorphisms and transfer operators, the product system's Toeplitz algebra has a universal representation. An approximate unit for A leads to strict convergence in the multiplier algebra. The maps defined from A and S into the multiplier algebra form a Toeplitz crossed product. The map from A is injective.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.1

returned_results.slogan: A covariant homomorphism from a system into a multiplier algebra induces a unique nondegenerate homomorphism from the crossed product algebra. This homomorphism restricts to the given representations on the algebra and group. Any C*-algebra with a covariant homomorphism satisfying the same universal property is isomorphic to the crossed product. The isomorphism preserves the embeddings of the group and algebra.
returned_results.name: Theorem B.3

returned_results.slogan: The universal C-star envelope of the crossed product algebra exists.
returned_results.name: Lemma 5.26

returned_results.slogan: The crossed product of an algebra by a groupoid is universal for covariant representations. For any algebra and covariant representation of the pair, there exists a unique essential algebra homomorphism from the crossed product into the multiplier algebra. This homomorphism extends the representation of the algebra and the groupoid.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.16

returned_results.slogan: The crossed product of Theta acting on its multiplier algebra by Gamma is contained in the crossed product of L-infinity of B with respect to nu_B by Gamma. If Theta acting on its multiplier algebra equals L-infinity of B with respect to nu_B, then the image of the multiplier algebra under the dual map Theta-hat equals the crossed product algebra. In that case, the crossed product algebra is a von Neumann subalgebra of a larger algebra. The dual map Theta-hat is a faithful normal conditional expectation onto that subalgebra.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2

returned_results.slogan: An element u in the multiplier algebra preserves a dense subalgebra under left multiplication. If there exists an operator S mapping the image of elements in the subalgebra to the image of their product with u, then u also preserves the full algebra. The operator S extends to act on the image of the full algebra, satisfying the same relation. Specifically, applying S to the image of any element equals the image of that element multiplied by u.
returned_results.name: Lemma

trajectory.query: canonical quotient system A/R alpha_R J contained in annihilator of kernel crossed product isomorphic quotient system

returned_results.slogan: The kernel I of the quotient map from the induced algebra crossed product with K equals the kernel J of the quotient map from the induced algebra crossed product with H under the action of X-Ind. Consequently, the reduced crossed product with K is Morita equivalent to the reduced crossed product with H. Moreover, the system with H acting is amenable exactly when the system with K acting is amenable.
returned_results.name: Corollary 3 (Quigg-Spielberg~ \cite{qs})

returned_results.slogan: The maximal crossed product is isomorphic to a quotient algebra. This isomorphism is realized by the canonical quotient map from the crossed product to the quotient algebra.
returned_results.name: Proposition

returned_results.slogan: The C-star algebras constructed from A with alpha and from the quotient of A by the relation R alpha with the induced action are star isomorphic. Similarly, the crossed product of A by the natural numbers with alpha is isomorphic to the crossed product of the quotient by the induced action. The quotient algebra A by R alpha embeds into its own crossed product with the induced action. It also embeds into the C-star algebra built from that quotient and the induced action.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.2

returned_results.slogan: The semicrossed product for a given system is completely isometrically isomorphic to the semicrossed product of the quotient system. This holds under the specified conditions involving the relation and induced map. The result establishes an equivalence between these operator algebraic structures.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.4

returned_results.slogan: The union of kernels over S forms an ideal I contained in the kernel of phi. This ideal I is invariant under the inverse action of elements in S and is mapped into itself by elements in T. The action alpha induces a homomorphism from T to the endomorphism ring of the quotient A over I, and this induced map is injective on S. The crossed product construction with the original action is equal to the crossed product using the quotient module and the induced action.
returned_results.name: Lemma 1.6

returned_results.slogan: The subset J defined by delta one a minus delta negative one u a for a in I is a closed ideal in A. There are canonical isomorphisms between the full crossed product, the reduced crossed product, and the algebraic crossed product of A with S. These are also isomorphic to the quotient of the crossed product of A with the integers modulo two by the ideal J.
returned_results.name: Proposition 52

returned_results.slogan: The kernel of a certain ideal and a specific module are isomorphic over a quotient algebra.
returned_results.name: Proposition 6.11

returned_results.slogan: The canonical map applied to the kernel of theta equals the ideal J. Consequently, the canonical map for C is an isomorphism of R-corings.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.2.8

returned_results.slogan: The annihilator of the kernel ideal J maps into the module of A-linear homomorphisms from the dual of B to B. This mapping induces an isomorphism between the annihilator and the homomorphism module. The kernel J is defined from the multiplication map on the tensor product of B over A. The result establishes an equivalence between these two algebraic structures.
returned_results.name: Lemma 6.3.7

returned_results.slogan: Given an ideal in a semigroup crossed product, the intersection with the coefficient algebra defines an ideal in that algebra. The induced action on the quotient algebra is well-defined and injective. There is a homomorphism from the original crossed product to the crossed product of the quotient algebra. This homomorphism induces an isomorphism between the quotient of the original crossed product and the crossed product of the quotient algebra.
returned_results.name: Lemma 8.2.6

trajectory.query: partial isometry Ua = delta(a)U iff U*U in commutant proposition endomorphism crossed product

returned_results.slogan: A partial isometry U satisfies Ua equals delta(a)U for all a in a unital C-star algebra A if and only if U is a partial isometry and its initial projection U*U lies in the commutant of A. This is also equivalent to U*U being in the commutant of A and the map delta from A to its image being a morphism.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.1

returned_results.slogan: The partial isometry U from the polar decomposition of operator a has several properties. The k-th power of the delta endomorphism applied to the absolute value of a is contained in the closure of a set generated by 1, the absolute value of a, and products of U and its adjoint. Delta is an endomorphism of the C-star algebra generated by these elements. The products U to the k times its adjoint to the k equal the k-th power of delta applied to 1 and lie in a specific algebra. For indices k and l, certain commutation and multiplication relations hold among these products.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.1

returned_results.slogan: The partial isometry U from the polar decomposition of operator a has several algebraic properties. U*U lies in the bicommutant of the algebra generated by 1 and |a|. Powers of U and their adjoints are also partial isometries and commute in certain ways. A morphism delta is defined on the algebra of |a|, satisfying relations with U and its adjoint. The iterates of delta are contained in algebras involving projections from powers of U.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.1

returned_results.slogan: Let V be a partial isometry and A be a C-star subalgebra of L(H). If V star V is in the commutant of A and V A V star is a subset of A, then the map delta_V from A to A is an endomorphism. Additionally, V star to the k times V to the k is in the commutant of A for every positive integer k.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.5

returned_results.slogan: If delta is an endomorphism defined by a unitary operator U, and U star U is in the commutant of A, then the C-star algebra B generated by the union of U star to the n times A times U to the n is commutative. Both the mapping delta and its star mapping delta star are endomorphisms on B.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.1

returned_results.slogan: A Cartan subalgebra B in a crossed product algebra M equals A semidirect product Gamma. If there is a non-zero partial isometry w and a positive real number t such that a certain commutation relation holds between w and elements of B under a modular automorphism, then B is unitarily conjugate to A. Specifically, there exists a unitary u in M such that B equals u A u star.
returned_results.name: Theorem 6.1

returned_results.slogan: U sub rho is an isometry. It satisfies U sub rho times x equals rho of x times U sub rho for all x in the crossed product algebra. The map phi sub rho of x equals the adjoint of U sub rho times x times U sub rho. These properties hold for rho in the endomorphism set of M sub zero.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.6

returned_results.slogan: An injective endomorphism of a unital C-star algebra with strict comparison or pure infiniteness, where the image is hereditary and the unit is not fixed, leads to a crossed product algebra. Under the condition that no proper ideal is invariant under the endomorphism, every full projection in the algebra relates to a partial isometry and a natural number. Specifically, applying the endomorphism's adjoint power to the partial isometry and projection yields the identity element. This equality holds in the crossed product algebra generated by the original algebra and the isometry implementing the endomorphism.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.2 ({cf. \cite[Lemma 3.2]{Ror}})

returned_results.slogan: Given an endomorphism and a representation, the operator is a partial isometry and commutes with the representation in a specific way. The projection from the operator belongs to the commutant of the represented algebra. The ideal of covariance is defined as the set of elements for which the projection acts as the identity on their images.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.21

returned_results.slogan: Given a C-star subalgebra A of bounded operators on a Hilbert space, if V is a partial isometry with V star V in the commutant of A, then the map delta V from A to its image is a morphism, and V commutes with elements of A in a specific way. If A contains the identity and both V V star and V star V are in the commutant of A, then several conditions are equivalent. These include V star V being a projection, V V star being a projection, and the maps defined by conjugation with V or V star being morphisms.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.4

trajectory.query: GV-sheaf on abelian variety implies nef sheaf theorem Pareschi Popa

returned_results.slogan: Every GV-sheaf on an abelian variety is nef. This means such sheaves have non-negative intersection with all curves. The result holds without additional assumptions on the variety or sheaf. It applies to all abelian varieties and their GV-sheaves.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.1

returned_results.slogan: A torsion-free GV-sheaf on an abelian variety has a nef determinant.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.4

returned_results.slogan: Given a morphism from a klt pair to an abelian variety, with a nef and abundant divisor and a Cartier divisor numerically equivalent to a multiple of the log canonical divisor plus the nef divisor, the pushforward of the divisor's sheaf is a GV-sheaf.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.4

returned_results.slogan: A smooth projective variety with given Albanese dimension and a Poincare line bundle is considered. For a line bundle and an effective divisor where their difference is nef, the tensor product of the canonical bundle, the line bundle, and a multiplier ideal sheaf satisfies a GV-sheaf condition. The index of the GV condition depends on the dimension and the Kodaira dimension of the nef difference. Specifically, if the line bundle itself is nef, then the tensor product of the canonical bundle and the line bundle is a GV-sheaf with an index determined by the dimension and the Kodaira dimension of the line bundle.
returned_results.name: Theorem B

returned_results.slogan: An abelian variety has a coherent sheaf that is a GV-sheaf if and only if, for any sufficiently positive ample line bundle on the dual variety, the cohomology groups vanish in all positive degrees after tensoring with the inverse of the dual line bundle. This condition is also equivalent to the derived dual of the sheaf satisfying the weak index theorem in degree equal to the dimension.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.3

returned_results.slogan: A coherent sheaf is a GV-sheaf if and only if, for any sufficiently large power of an ample line bundle on the dual abelian variety, certain cohomology groups vanish. This vanishing condition involves the tensor product of the sheaf with a particular derived pullback. Equivalently, after pulling back the sheaf via the isogeny induced by the line bundle and tensoring with that bundle, the higher cohomology groups also vanish.
returned_results.name: Theorem

returned_results.slogan: A semihomogeneous vector bundle is a GV-sheaf if and only if it is nef. It is also equivalent for the bundle to have a nef determinant. These three conditions are all equivalent for such bundles.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.7

returned_results.slogan: A coherent sheaf is a GV-sheaf exactly when, for every isogeny to the abelian variety and every ample line bundle on the covering variety, the higher cohomology groups of the pullback tensor the line bundle vanish.
returned_results.name: Theorem 14

returned_results.slogan: A sheaf F on an abelian variety is a GV-sheaf if, for every finite etale morphism from an abelian variety B to A, and every ample line bundle L on B, the higher cohomology groups of the pullback of F twisted by L vanish. This condition requires that all such higher cohomology groups are zero for positive degrees. The result characterizes GV-sheaves by this vanishing property across all finite etale covers and ample twists.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.12

returned_results.slogan: A coherent sheaf on an abelian variety is a GV-sheaf exactly when certain cohomology groups vanish. This vanishing condition must hold for all isogenies from any abelian variety to the given one. It also requires that the pullback of the sheaf tensored with any ample line bundle has no higher cohomology. The result characterizes GV-sheaves through these cohomological properties.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.3 (Hacon)

trajectory.query: IT0 sheaf on abelian variety ample twist globally generated and higher cohomology vanishing

returned_results.slogan: A coherent sheaf satisfying the IT zero condition on an abelian variety becomes globally generated after tensoring with any ample line bundle. This holds without further assumptions on the sheaf or the variety. The result applies universally for every choice of ample line bundle. Global generation is guaranteed under these conditions.
returned_results.name: Theorem 7.11

returned_results.slogan: A finite etale morphism between Abelian varieties and an ample line bundle on the source satisfy a vanishing condition for certain sheaf cohomology groups. For all positive integers i and every integer j, the cohomology in degree i of the tensor product of the ample bundle with the pullback of a particular sheaf is zero. This result holds without any restrictions on j. The vanishing applies to all higher cohomology groups beyond degree zero.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.1

returned_results.slogan: Vanishing holds for higher cohomology groups of a specific twisted sheaf involving the canonical divisor, an effective divisor, a multiple of a divisor with non-negative Iitaka dimension, and an ample divisor, tensored with a non-lc ideal sheaf. A related sheaf becomes globally generated when twisted further by a sufficiently large multiple of a globally generated ample divisor. The required lower bound for this multiple is the dimension of the underlying smooth projective variety.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.6

returned_results.slogan: The ideal sheaf is IT1, meaning it satisfies a certain vanishing condition for its higher cohomology groups. This property holds for the specific sheaf in question. It implies that the first cohomology group vanishes after twisting by an ample line bundle. This is a technical condition used in algebraic geometry.
returned_results.name: Lemma

returned_results.slogan: Given a finite morphism from a smooth projective variety to an abelian variety, and an ample line bundle satisfying certain technical conditions, any torsion-free coherent sheaf with a specific vanishing property also satisfies higher-degree vanishing when twisted by the pullback of any ample line bundle from the abelian variety. The conditions on the ample line bundle include either a property (P_a) or a decomposition involving a globally generated or adjoint-type line bundle. The vanishing holds for cohomology degrees at least as large as a given integer between one and the dimension of the variety.
returned_results.name: Corollary 3.14

returned_results.slogan: A nonzero IT-zero sheaf on an abelian variety has a nonzero global section. This holds if all higher cohomology groups vanish after tensoring with any degree zero line bundle. The result confirms the existence of sections under these cohomological vanishing conditions.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.2

returned_results.slogan: A nonzero coherent sheaf on an abelian variety that satisfies the IT-zero condition has nonzero global sections when twisted by any degree zero line bundle.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.2 ({\cite[Lemma 2.1]{CH1}})

returned_results.slogan: A normal Cohen-Macaulay subvariety of an abelian variety has vanishing higher cohomology groups when twisted by an ample line bundle. Specifically, for any positive integer i, the cohomology group H to the i of X with coefficients in the canonical sheaf tensored with L is zero. This holds under the given conditions on X and L. The result applies to all degrees i greater than zero.
returned_results.name: Corollary 1.6

returned_results.slogan: A coherent sheaf on a projective variety satisfies vanishing conditions for certain cohomology groups. If the cohomology vanishes for specific twists, then it also vanishes for larger twists. The vanishing holds for all positive degrees and sufficiently large twists. Additionally, the sheaf is generated by its global sections.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.4 (Mumford-Castelnuovo Criterion)

returned_results.slogan: For a coherent sheaf on a scheme with an ample line bundle, there exists an integer such that for all sufficiently large twists, the higher cohomology groups vanish.
returned_results.name: Theorem 9 (Serre's theorem)

trajectory.query: M-regular sheaf on abelian variety ample line bundle twist globally generated

returned_results.slogan: A polarized abelian variety with a coherent sheaf is considered. If the sheaf twisted by the negative of the polarization is M-regular, then the original sheaf is globally generated.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2.8

returned_results.slogan: An M-regular coherent sheaf and an M-regular line bundle on an Abelian variety have a tensor product that is globally generated.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.2 ({\cite[p.~ 285]{Pareschi:Popa:2003}})

returned_results.slogan: Given an ample line bundle and coherent sheaf on an abelian variety, if a certain twisted sheaf is M-regular, then the original sheaf is globally generated. If a different twisted sheaf is M-regular with a rational parameter less than one, then the multiplication map from tensor product to global sections is surjective. For two locally free sheaves, if their respective twists are M-regular and a condition on parameters holds, the multiplication map between their global sections is also surjective. These results connect M-regularity conditions to generation and surjectivity properties.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.2 ({Propositions \ref{lemma_globally_generated}, \ref{prop_surjectiveity_E,F}})

returned_results.slogan: An M-regular sheaf on an abelian variety is continuously globally generated. This means that such sheaves have strong positivity properties. The result ensures that these sheaves are well-behaved in terms of generation by global sections.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.4 (\cite{PP2} Cor. 5.3)

returned_results.slogan: A coherent sheaf on projective space over a field is m-regular. Then, the sheaf twisted by m is globally generated.
returned_results.name: Lemma 33.35.10.

returned_results.slogan: A M-regular sheaf on an abelian variety is continuously globally generated at every point.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.5

returned_results.slogan: A coherent sheaf and an invertible sheaf supported on a subvariety of an abelian variety are considered. If both sheaves are M-regular on the abelian variety, then their tensor product is globally generated.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.4

returned_results.slogan: An M-regular sheaf on an abelian variety is continuously globally generated. For any M-regular sheaf, the dimension of global sections twisted by any line bundle in the dual variety is positive. If the sheaf satisfies the IT(0) condition, this dimension remains constant across all such line bundles.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.3 (\cite {blnp})

returned_results.slogan: If a coherent sheaf and an invertible sheaf are both M-regular on an abelian variety, then their tensor product is globally generated. This holds when the sheaves are supported on a subvariety, including the whole variety. M-regularity ensures the global sections generate the tensor product sheaf.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.7

returned_results.slogan: An ample line bundle A on an abelian variety X and coherent sheaves E and F satisfy several properties. If F twisted by the inverse of A is M-regular, then F is globally generated. If F twisted by the inverse of A squared is M-regular, then the multiplication map from global sections of A to the n power and F to those of their tensor product is surjective for n at least two. If both E and F are locally free and each twisted by the inverse of A squared is M-regular, then the multiplication map from global sections of E and F to those of their tensor product is surjective.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1 ({\cite[Theorem 6.3]{MR1949161}, \cite[Theorem 7.34]{MR2807853}})

trajectory.query: GV-sheaf characterization by vanishing after pullback by isogeny and ample twist on abelian variety

returned_results.slogan: A coherent sheaf is a GV-sheaf if and only if, for any sufficiently large power of an ample line bundle on the dual abelian variety, certain cohomology groups vanish. This vanishing condition involves the tensor product of the sheaf with a particular derived pullback. Equivalently, after pulling back the sheaf via the isogeny induced by the line bundle and tensoring with that bundle, the higher cohomology groups also vanish.
returned_results.name: Theorem

returned_results.slogan: A coherent sheaf on an abelian variety is a GV-sheaf exactly when certain cohomology groups vanish. This vanishing condition must hold for all isogenies from any abelian variety to the given one. It also requires that the pullback of the sheaf tensored with any ample line bundle has no higher cohomology. The result characterizes GV-sheaves through these cohomological properties.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.3 (Hacon)

returned_results.slogan: A coherent sheaf is a GV-sheaf exactly when, for every isogeny to the abelian variety and every ample line bundle on the covering variety, the higher cohomology groups of the pullback tensor the line bundle vanish.
returned_results.name: Theorem 14

returned_results.slogan: A sheaf F on an abelian variety is a GV-sheaf if, for every finite etale morphism from an abelian variety B to A, and every ample line bundle L on B, the higher cohomology groups of the pullback of F twisted by L vanish. This condition requires that all such higher cohomology groups are zero for positive degrees. The result characterizes GV-sheaves by this vanishing property across all finite etale covers and ample twists.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.12

returned_results.slogan: An abelian variety has a coherent sheaf that is a GV-sheaf if and only if, for any sufficiently positive ample line bundle on the dual variety, the cohomology groups vanish in all positive degrees after tensoring with the inverse of the dual line bundle. This condition is also equivalent to the derived dual of the sheaf satisfying the weak index theorem in degree equal to the dimension.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.3

returned_results.slogan: A coherent sheaf on a smooth projective variety is a GV-sheaf if, for every sufficiently ample line bundle, the cohomology groups vanish in all positive degrees after pulling back along a certain morphism and tensoring.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.3

returned_results.slogan: A GV-sheaf on an abelian variety has a vanishing property for cohomology groups. If the i-th cohomology group of the sheaf twisted by a degree zero line bundle vanishes, then the next higher cohomology group also vanishes. This holds for all nonnegative integers i and all such line bundles.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.6

returned_results.slogan: For a coherent sheaf on an abelian variety, there is a natural isomorphism relating derived global sections with the Fourier-Mukai transform of the dualizing complex. The Fourier-Mukai transform of the dualizing complex lies in a bounded derived category, and its support equals the cohomological support variety. A coherent sheaf is a GV-sheaf if and only if its Fourier-Mukai transform is concentrated in degree zero. This is also equivalent to the vanishing of higher cohomology groups after twisting with the dual of a sufficiently ample line bundle.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.4
