The conditions depend on whether the ring is Z_p or a subring of the rationals, and involve inclusions of skeleta for primes not invertible in R.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.1

returned_results.slogan: The T-action on M is equivariantly formal exactly when a specific long exact sequence in equivariant cohomology is exact. This sequence begins with the cohomology of M and maps through the cohomology of the fixed point set and its successive pairs. The sequence ends with the cohomology of M relative to its singular set. Exactness of this sequence characterizes equivariant formality.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.4 (\cite{Bredon}, \cite{FranzPuppe})

returned_results.slogan: The Atiyah-Bredon sequence is exact at positions up to j minus two if and only if the equivariant cohomology of X is a j-th syzygy.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1 (\cite[Thm.~ \ref{thm:conditions-partial-exactness}]{AlldayFranzPuppe})

returned_results.slogan: The Atiyah-Bredon sequence is exact at positions up to j-2 if and only if the equivariant cohomology of X is a j-th syzygy.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1

returned_results.slogan: The sequence is exact at the equivariant cohomology of the fixed point set under certain conditions. These conditions require the space to be compact or paracompact with a finite set of identity components of isotropy subgroups. The action must be equivariantly formal and performed by a torus.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.5 (Chang-Skjelbred Lemma {\cite[Lemma 2.3]{CS}})

returned_results.slogan: For any integer j between zero and r, four conditions are equivalent. The Atiyah-Bredon sequence is exact at positions from negative one to j minus two. The restriction map from the equivariant cohomology of X with respect to T to that with respect to any subtorus of rank r minus j is surjective. The equivariant cohomology ring is free over all subrings corresponding to quotients of T of rank j, and it is a j-th syzygy.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.7

returned_results.slogan: For a given integer j between 0 and r, the equivariant cohomology of X is a j-th syzygy over the ring R_G precisely when certain cohomology groups vanish for indices up to j-2. This vanishing condition is equivalent to the exactness of the initial segment of the Atiyah-Bredon sequence for the sheaf F, up to degree j-1. The sequence involves terms from H_G^*(X) through H_G^*(X_{j-1}, X_{j-2}). The result characterizes syzygies in equivariant cohomology via the Atiyah-Bredon complex.
returned_results.name: Theorem 6.10

trajectory.query: generic subtorus acts locally freely commuting action principle H_T^*(M) isomorphic H_{T/K}^*(M/K) fixed points equivariantly formal

returned_results.slogan: An equivariantly formal T-action on M implies that for any subtorus K of T, the restricted K-action on M is also equivariantly formal. Additionally, the induced action of the quotient torus T/K on the fixed point set M^K is equivariantly formal. This property holds for both the subgroup and the quotient actions.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.10

returned_results.slogan: A compact manifold M has a smooth action by a compact torus K. A subtorus G of K acts on M with finite stabilizers. The quotient torus T is defined as K divided by G. The natural map induces an isomorphism of rational equivariant cohomology rings over the cohomology of the classifying space of T.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.3

returned_results.slogan: When a subtorus K acts trivially on X, the equivariant cohomology and homology with compact support of X for the torus T are isomorphic to the tensor product of the representation ring of T with the corresponding equivariant cohomology and homology for the quotient torus L equals T over K. These isomorphisms hold as modules over the representation ring of T. The result applies to both cohomology and homology with compact support.
returned_results.name: Proposition 7.1

returned_results.slogan: For a finite T-CW complex Z fixed by a compact subgroup H of T, let K be the quotient group T over H. The theorem states that the equivariant cohomology or K-theory of Z for the torus T is naturally isomorphic to the tensor product of the equivariant cohomology or K-theory of Z for K with the coefficient ring of T over the coefficient ring of K. This holds when considering either ordinary equivariant cohomology or equivariant K-theory. The isomorphism is natural and relates the theories for the groups T and K.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.13

returned_results.slogan: Given a subtorus K of T with quotient L, and a closed T-pair (A,B) in X where K acts freely on A minus B, the cohomology of the quotient pair (A/K, B/K) is finite-dimensional. The equivariant cohomology of (A,B) with respect to T is isomorphic to that of (A/K,B/K) with respect to L. Similarly, the equivariant homology of (A,B) with respect to T is isomorphic to a shifted version of the homology of (A/K,B/K) with respect to L. This also holds for any T-pair if K acts locally freely on all of A.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.7

returned_results.slogan: Given a maximal subtorus acting locally freely on a manifold, the equivariant cohomology of the manifold under the full torus is isomorphic to that of the quotient space under the quotient torus. The action of the full torus is Cohen-Macaulay exactly when the action of the quotient torus on the quotient space is equivariantly formal.
returned_results.name: Proposition 5.4 ({\cite[Remark~ 2]{GT2009}})

returned_results.slogan: A torus acts on a smooth variety. The fixed points of a subtorus are considered. The pullback map in localized equivariant K-theory from the variety to its fixed point set is an isomorphism.
returned_results.name: Theorem 6.2 (relative first localization theorem cf. \cite{Tho} theorem 2.1, or \cite{Se} proposition 4.1 for topological case)

returned_results.slogan: A torus T acts on a normal quasi-projective variety X, with a subtorus S acting trivially. The action factors through the quotient torus T' = T/S. The theorem establishes an isomorphism between the equivariant K-theory of X with respect to T' tensored with the representation ring of S, and the equivariant K-theory with respect to T. This isomorphism holds over the rational numbers.
returned_results.name: Lemma 5.4

returned_results.slogan: If the group action of K beta is locally free on the intersection of Z beta and the fixed point set M to the T beta, then the equivariant cohomology of that intersection with respect to G beta is isomorphic to the tensor product of the cohomology of the classifying space of H beta and the cohomology of the symplectic quotient of M to the T beta by K beta.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.2.18

returned_results.slogan: For a compact manifold with a group action, the equivariant K-theory group is isomorphic to the invariants of the torus-equivariant K-theory under the action of a certain group.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2.17

trajectory.query: Cohen-Macaulay action preserved under quotient by locally free subtorus exact sequence regular element codimension one subtorus

returned_results.slogan: A Cohen-Macaulay module over a local noetherian ring remains Cohen-Macaulay after quotienting by a regular sequence. The resulting module has dimension and depth equal to the original dimension minus the length of the sequence.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.9.

returned_results.slogan: Let R be a local ring and M a finitely generated R-module. If a sequence of exact zero-divisors acts on M, then M is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if the quotient of M by the submodule generated by that sequence is also Cohen-Macaulay.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2.9

returned_results.slogan: For a Cohen-Macaulay module M, a sequence is M-regular if and only if the quotient module is nonzero and its dimension equals the dimension of M minus the length of the sequence. In that case, the quotient module is also Cohen-Macaulay.
returned_results.name: Proposition 0.1.8

returned_results.slogan: An M-regular sequence in an ideal I of a Noetherian local ring R implies that M is I-Cohen Macaulay exactly when the quotient of M by the submodule generated by the sequence is Cohen Macaulay over the corresponding quotient ring with respect to the image of I.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.10

returned_results.slogan: A Cohen-Macaulay local ring and a finitely generated module of dimension at least one are considered. For any element in the maximal ideal, the dimension of the quotient module is at least one less than the original dimension.
returned_results.name: Lemma 8.4

returned_results.slogan: A quotient of a Cohen-Macaulay ring by a regular sequence remains Cohen-Macaulay. This holds when the ring is Noetherian. The result applies to ideals generated by regular sequences.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.15

returned_results.slogan: A sequence of exact zero-divisors on a Cohen-Macaulay local ring with a canonical module is also a sequence of exact zero-divisors on that canonical module. The quotient ring by this sequence remains Cohen-Macaulay and has the same dimension. The canonical module of the quotient is the quotient of the original canonical module by the submodule generated by the sequence.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2.12

returned_results.slogan: A local ring module is relative Cohen-Macaulay with respect to an ideal if and only if the quotient by a regular element on both the module and the dual of the top local cohomology module is also relative Cohen-Macaulay. This equivalence holds when the cohomological dimension is positive. The result extends to regular sequences on both the module and the dual of the top local cohomology module. In that case, the module is relative Cohen-Macaulay if and only if the quotient by the sequence is relative Cohen-Macaulay.
returned_results.name: Corollary 1.2

returned_results.slogan: The quotient ring is Cohen-Macaulay.
returned_results.name: Lemma 19

returned_results.slogan: For a Cohen-Macaulay local ring with dimension at least two and an equimultiple canonical ideal, if an element is regular modulo the canonical ideal, then the Cohen-Macaulay degree of the ring is at most the Cohen-Macaulay degree of the quotient by that element.
returned_results.name: Proposition 6.11

trajectory.query: toric pair characterization via complexity zero rationally connected smooth projective reduced divisor log canonical pair toric criterion

returned_results.slogan: A divisor over X is toric with respect to every boundary in the ample set if and only if it is a log canonical place of the pair. Similarly, a subvariety is a toric stratum of every boundary in the ample set if and only if it is a log canonical center. The theorem establishes these equivalences for log Calabi-Yau pairs of complexity zero.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4

returned_results.slogan: For a projective pair with log canonical singularities and numerically trivial log canonical divisor, the complexity is nonnegative. If the complexity is zero, then the pair is toric.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.30 (cf.~ \cite{BMSZ18}*{Theorem 1.2})

returned_results.slogan: Given a field of characteristic zero and a proper variety with a log canonical pair where the negative of the log canonical divisor is nef, if there is a decomposition of complexity less than one, then there exists a divisor forming a toric pair. This divisor is at least the fractional part of the boundary divisor. All but at most the floor of twice the complexity of the components of this divisor come from the set of components in the given decomposition.
returned_results.name: Corollary 1.5

returned_results.slogan: A log Calabi-Yau pair with complexity zero is toric if and only if it has index one. This is also equivalent to the existence of a complement with log canonical threshold equal to one. These three conditions are mutually equivalent for such pairs.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.5

returned_results.slogan: A log Calabi-Yau pair of complexity zero is toric if and only if the set of its log canonical centers has exactly one element.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.8

returned_results.slogan: A smooth projective variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero with a normal crossing divisor is a toric variety with toric boundary equal to that divisor if and only if the logarithmic cotangent bundle is numerically flat and the variety is rationally connected.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.6

returned_results.slogan: A log Calabi-Yau pair with complexity zero and a divisor satisfying a certain inequality is considered. If a specific boundary arrangement derived from the pair is toric, then the original boundary is also toric. This result holds under the given conditions on the coefficients.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.10

returned_results.slogan: The generalized log Calabi-Yau pair in dimension two has non-negative complexity. Zero complexity implies the pair is toric. For pairs with trivial boundary and zero complexity, the variety is either projective plane, a product of projective lines, or a Hirzebruch surface. Under generalized klt conditions and zero complexity, the variety is projective plane or a product of projective lines.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.1

returned_results.slogan: A smooth projective variety over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic, equipped with a normal crossing divisor, is a toric pair under two conditions. The variety must be separably rationally connected. Additionally, the log differential sheaf must be numerically flat.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.5

returned_results.slogan: A proper variety with a log canonical pair of complexity under one, where the negative of the log canonical divisor is nef, is considered. If a divisorially log terminal model of this pair is toric with a boundary containing the round-down of its own boundary, then the original pair is also toric. The boundary on the original variety is the pushforward of the toric boundary and contains the round-down of its original boundary. This establishes a condition under which the original pair inherits the toric structure.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.3.11

trajectory.query: int-amplified endomorphism etale outside divisor toric pair predecessor ramification divisor logarithmic differential

returned_results.slogan: A rationally connected smooth projective variety with a reduced divisor is toric exactly when it has an int-amplified endomorphism that restricts to an étale map on the complement of the divisor.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.4

returned_results.slogan: A log Calabi-Yau pair with pdlt singularities that has an int-amplified endomorphism is a finite quotient of a toric log Calabi-Yau fibration over an abelian variety.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.1

returned_results.slogan: An int-amplified endomorphism with totally invariant ramification on a rationally connected smooth projective variety leads to several structural properties. After replacing the map by a positive power, the induced action on the Néron-Severi group is diagonalizable with one or two positive integer eigenvalues. The variety and its ramification divisor form a toric pair at each step of a minimal model program. The Kawaguchi-Silverman conjecture holds for any surjective endomorphism of these intermediate varieties.
returned_results.name: Proposition 10.7

returned_results.slogan: Let X be a normal projective variety smooth in codimension 2 with a reduced divisor D. Suppose f is an int-amplified endomorphism fixing D and quasi-étale away from D. Then there exists a smooth open subset U of X such that the complement has codimension at least 3 and D intersect U is a normal crossing divisor. The sheaf of logarithmic differentials is locally free on U.
returned_results.name: Proposition 10.2

returned_results.slogan: Let X be a rationally connected smooth projective variety with a reduced divisor D. Suppose f is an int-amplified endomorphism of X that fixes D setwise and is quasi-etale on the complement of D. If the pullback action of f on the Neron-Severi space is diagonalizable with only one or two positive integer eigenvalues and no others, then the pair (X, D) is toric.
returned_results.name: Theorem 10.6

returned_results.slogan: An int-amplified endomorphism of a normal projective Fano-type variety, smooth in codimension two, preserves a reduced divisor and is quasi-etale away from it. Under these conditions, the logarithmic cotangent sheaf of the variety with respect to the divisor is slope semistable with respect to any ample Cartier divisor.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.2

returned_results.slogan: Suppose X is a normal projective variety with Q-factorial Kawamata log terminal singularities, and f is an int-amplified endomorphism of X. If the number of totally invariant prime divisors equals the Picard number plus the dimension of X, then the pair consisting of X and the sum of these divisors is toric.
returned_results.name: Corollary 1.2

returned_results.slogan: Given a klt type variety X with a log Calabi-Yau pair where the canonical divisor plus a boundary divisor is linearly trivial, suppose the pair admits an int-amplified endomorphism. For any finite cover induced by an etale cover of the regular locus minus the boundary, there exists a sufficiently large iterate of the endomorphism such that its pullback via the fiber product is also int-amplified.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.13

returned_results.slogan: An int-amplified endomorphism preserves a reduced divisor on a normal projective variety that is smooth in codimension two. The variety has dimension at least two, and the endomorphism is quasi-etale away from the divisor. For any ample divisor, the first and second Chern classes of the logarithmic cotangent sheaf vanish when intersected with powers of the ample divisor. These intersection numbers are all zero.
returned_results.name: Proposition 10.3

returned_results.slogan: An int-amplified endomorphism of a normal projective variety preserves a reduced divisor and is quasi-etale outside it. The variety is smooth in codimension two and has dimension at least two. The first and second Chern classes of the logarithmic cotangent sheaf vanish when intersected with powers of an ample divisor. These intersection numbers are all zero.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.1

trajectory.query: Meng Zhang theorem rationally connected smooth projective variety int-amplified endomorphism toric pair

returned_results.slogan: A rationally connected smooth projective variety with a reduced divisor is toric exactly when it has an int-amplified endomorphism that restricts to an étale map on the complement of the divisor.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.4

returned_results.slogan: A smooth rationally connected projective threefold with Picard number two is toric precisely when it has an int-amplified endomorphism.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.3

returned_results.slogan: A smooth projective variety with an int-amplified endomorphism is toric if the pushforward of every line bundle under the endomorphism splits into a direct sum of line bundles.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.7

returned_results.slogan: Suppose X is a normal projective variety with Q-factorial Kawamata log terminal singularities, and f is an int-amplified endomorphism of X. If the number of totally invariant prime divisors equals the Picard number plus the dimension of X, then the pair consisting of X and the sum of these divisors is toric.
returned_results.name: Corollary 1.2

returned_results.slogan: A smooth projective variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero with an int-amplified endomorphism is toric exactly when the pushforward of every line bundle under the endomorphism splits as a direct sum of line bundles.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1

returned_results.slogan: Let X be a rationally connected smooth projective variety with a reduced divisor D. Suppose f is an int-amplified endomorphism of X that fixes D setwise and is quasi-etale on the complement of D. If the pullback action of f on the Neron-Severi space is diagonalizable with only one or two positive integer eigenvalues and no others, then the pair (X, D) is toric.
returned_results.name: Theorem 10.6

returned_results.slogan: A smooth Fano threefold with Picard number at least three that has an int-amplified endomorphism must be toric. This result connects the existence of such endomorphisms to the geometric structure of the variety. It implies that under these conditions, the variety is isomorphic to a toric variety. The theorem establishes a necessary condition for int-amplified endomorphisms on these Fano threefolds.
returned_results.name: Theorem 8.1

returned_results.slogan: A smooth and rationally connected variety with an int-amplified endomorphism is of Fano type.
returned_results.name: Corollary 1.4 (Corollary \ref{main cor'})

returned_results.slogan: A rationally connected smooth projective variety is of Fano type if it has an int-amplified endomorphism.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1

returned_results.slogan: A smooth Fano fourfold with a conic bundle is toric if and only if it has a polarized endomorphism. It is also equivalent to the existence of an int-amplified endomorphism. If any of these conditions is satisfied, the variety is rational.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.4

trajectory.query: smooth projective variety normal crossing divisor toric iff logarithmic cotangent bundle numerically flat rationally connected

returned_results.slogan: A smooth projective variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero with a normal crossing divisor is a toric variety with toric boundary equal to that divisor if and only if the logarithmic cotangent bundle is numerically flat and the variety is rationally connected.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.6

returned_results.slogan: A smooth projective variety over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic, equipped with a normal crossing divisor, is a toric pair under two conditions. The variety must be separably rationally connected. Additionally, the log differential sheaf must be numerically flat.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.5

returned_results.slogan: For a smooth projective variety over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic with a normal crossing divisor, three conditions are equivalent. The variety is a toric variety with toric boundary equal to the divisor. Alternatively, the logarithmic cotangent bundle is numerically flat and the variety is separably rationally connected. A third equivalent condition is that the logarithmic cotangent bundle is numerically flat, the variety is rationally connected, and it is globally F-split.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.5

returned_results.slogan: A log smooth projective pair has a numerically flat logarithmic tangent bundle. This implies the existence of a smooth morphism with connected fibers onto a torus quotient. The fibration is locally trivial in the analytic topology. Each fiber is a smooth toric variety with an induced boundary divisor.
returned_results.name: Corollary 1.7

returned_results.slogan: A smooth projective variety over a perfect field of positive characteristic with a normal crossing divisor has a numerically flat logarithmic cotangent bundle if and only if an ample divisor exists making the bundle semistable. The first and second Chern classes of the logarithmic cotangent bundle must vanish when multiplied by appropriate powers of the ample divisor.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.2

returned_results.slogan: A log smooth projective pair with a nef anti-canonical divisor minus the boundary and a flat logarithmic tangent bundle implies the variety is toric. If the variety is simply connected and has no holomorphic forms in positive degrees, then it must be a smooth toric variety. The boundary divisor in this case is exactly the toric boundary. This result characterizes such pairs as being toric.
returned_results.name: Corollary 1.5

returned_results.slogan: Given a log smooth reduced pair with X projective, if the negative of the log canonical divisor is nef and the logarithmic tangent bundle is R-flat, then there exists a smooth projective variety T with trivial canonical divisor. There is a smooth morphism with connected fibers from X to T, and the fibration is locally trivial analytically. Each fiber is a smooth toric variety with boundary divisor, and T contains no rational curves.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1

returned_results.slogan: A smooth projective variety over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic with a normal crossing divisor has two equivalent conditions. One condition is the existence of a finite etale cover that leads to a toric fibration over an ordinary abelian variety. The other condition is that the variety is globally F-split and its logarithmic cotangent bundle is numerically flat. These two properties are equivalent.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.4

returned_results.slogan: The tangent bundle twisted by the log divisor on a projective log smooth pair admits a holomorphic connection. This condition implies that the bundle is numerically flat.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.8

returned_results.slogan: A smooth projective variety with a simple normal crossing divisor and an ample divisor is considered, where the negative of the canonical divisor plus the divisor is nef. If the logarithmic tangent bundle is semistable and a certain Chern class condition holds, then the pair is either a toric fiber bundle over an Abelian variety quotient or the variety is rationally connected with a nontrivial canonical divisor and the logarithmic tangent bundle splits. In the second case, if the pair is a Mori fiber space, it must be isomorphic to projective space with a hyperplane.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.5

trajectory.query: int-amplified endomorphism quasi-etale outside divisor logarithmic cotangent numerically flat vanishing Chern classes semistable

returned_results.slogan: An int-amplified endomorphism of a normal projective variety preserves a reduced divisor and is quasi-etale outside it. The variety is smooth in codimension two and has dimension at least two. The first and second Chern classes of the logarithmic cotangent sheaf vanish when intersected with powers of an ample divisor. These intersection numbers are all zero.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.1

returned_results.slogan: An int-amplified endomorphism preserves a reduced divisor on a normal projective variety that is smooth in codimension two. The variety has dimension at least two, and the endomorphism is quasi-etale away from the divisor. For any ample divisor, the first and second Chern classes of the logarithmic cotangent sheaf vanish when intersected with powers of the ample divisor. These intersection numbers are all zero.
returned_results.name: Proposition 10.3

returned_results.slogan: An int-amplified endomorphism of a normal projective Fano-type variety, smooth in codimension two, preserves a reduced divisor and is quasi-etale away from it. Under these conditions, the logarithmic cotangent sheaf of the variety with respect to the divisor is slope semistable with respect to any ample Cartier divisor.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.2

returned_results.slogan: Let X be a normal projective variety of dimension at least two, and D a reduced divisor on X. Suppose f is an int-amplified endomorphism of X that fixes D setwise and is quasi-etale away from D. If the pullback action of f on the Neron-Severi space is diagonalizable with only one or two positive integer eigenvalues, then the logarithmic cotangent bundle of X along D is slope semistable with respect to any ample divisor H.
returned_results.name: Proposition 10.5

returned_results.slogan: A smooth projective variety over a perfect field of positive characteristic with a normal crossing divisor has a numerically flat logarithmic cotangent bundle if and only if an ample divisor exists making the bundle semistable. The first and second Chern classes of the logarithmic cotangent bundle must vanish when multiplied by appropriate powers of the ample divisor.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.2

returned_results.slogan: A normal projective variety X of dimension at least two, smooth in codimension two, has a reduced divisor D. If there is a polarized endomorphism f fixing D and quasi-etale outside D, with an ample divisor H satisfying f*H proportional to qH for q greater than one, then certain Chern class products with H vanish. The first Chern class squared and the second Chern class of the logarithmic cotangent sheaf, each multiplied by appropriate powers of H, are zero. Additionally, the logarithmic cotangent sheaf is H-slope semistable.
returned_results.name: Proposition 5.3

returned_results.slogan: The theorem applies to a maximally quasi-etale projective klt variety. It considers a reflexive subsheaf of the cotangent sheaf with positive semistability under certain intersection conditions. If a specific linear combination of Chern classes vanishes when intersected with ample divisors, then the sheaf is locally free. This result establishes a criterion for local freeness based on stability and Chern class constraints.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2.11

returned_results.slogan: Let X be a normal projective variety of klt type that is maximally quasi-étale, and let E be a reflexive sheaf of rank at least one on X. If the determinant of E is Q-Cartier, E is semistable with respect to an ample divisor, and its restriction to the regular locus is locally free and projectively flat, then the vanishing of the first Chern class implies that E is locally free and flat.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.16

returned_results.slogan: A reflexive sheaf on a normal projective variety with certain singularities and an ample divisor is considered. If the sheaf is semistable with respect to the divisor and two specific Chern class products vanish, then there exists a quasi-etale cover of the variety. On this cover, the pullback of the sheaf becomes locally free and flat.
returned_results.name: Theorem (Flatness criterion)

returned_results.slogan: A projective klt variety of dimension at least two with an ample divisor has a semistable sheaf of reflexive differentials. If a certain combination of Chern classes evaluated on the divisor equals zero, then the variety is quasi-Abelian. This means it has a quasi-etale cover from an Abelian variety.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.2

trajectory.query: maximal rationally connected fibration base not uniruled Graber Harris Starr theorem pseudoeffective canonical bundle

returned_results.slogan: The Graber-Harris-Starr theorem states that for an irreducible variety X, the base Z of a maximal rationally connected fibration is not uniruled. This means Z does not contain a rational curve through a general point. The result holds for any dominant rational map g from X to Z that is a maximal rationally connected fibration.
returned_results.name: Corollary

returned_results.slogan: The Maximally Rationally Connected fibration is a unique map from a space to a base. Its fibers are rationally connected. The base is not uniruled, meaning its canonical divisor is pseudo-effective. This fibration is also known as the MRC-fibration.
returned_results.name: Theorem 6.4

returned_results.slogan: A compact Kähler space has a maximal rationally connected fibration mapping to a base. The base of this fibration is not uniruled. This means the base does not contain any rational curves through a general point. The result holds for the MRC fibration of such a space.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.14

returned_results.slogan: The maximal rationally connected fibration of a compact Kähler manifold yields a base that is not uniruled. This means the base does not contain a rational curve through every point. The result holds for any compact Kähler manifold.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.8 ({\cite{Graber-Harris-Starr-2003}, \cite[\S 3]{CampanaWinkelmann2016}})

returned_results.slogan: A fibration f from X to Z factors through a map g from X to Y and a map h from Y to Z. For a general point z in Z, the restriction of g to the fiber over z is the maximal rationally connected fibration of that fiber. This implies the canonical divisor of the fiber of Y over z is pseudo-effective.
returned_results.name: Corollary 6.5

returned_results.slogan: The maximal rationally chain connected fibration exists for any normal and proper variety. This fibration maps the variety to a base space. The base space is not uniruled. The result holds without assuming the variety is projective.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.7 (Campana, and Kollar, Miyaoka and Mori)

returned_results.slogan: The maximal rationally connected fibration of a variety maps to a base that is not uniruled. This base does not contain any rational curves through a general point. The result holds for any variety.

returned_results.slogan: A minimizer exists for the variational problem involving an energy functional with an interaction potential and a diffusion term. The minimization is over nonnegative functions with fixed mass in certain Lebesgue spaces. The existence condition requires strict subadditivity of the infimum energy with respect to mass splitting. This holds for all masses less than a given total mass.
returned_results.name: Theorem 12

returned_results.slogan: A minimizing sequence for a variational problem can be decomposed into a finite number of functions that separate spatially. These functions each have a specific mass and satisfy associated minimization problems with the same Lagrange multiplier. The sum of their masses equals the original total mass, and their energies sum to the original minimal energy. If the potential is not identically zero, one function can be centered at the origin.
returned_results.name: Theorem \thesection .1

returned_results.slogan: A minimizer exists for the minimization problem involving a convex function and an interaction kernel under a mass constraint. The problem is defined over nonnegative functions with fixed total mass in certain Lebesgue spaces. The strict subadditivity condition on the infimum values with respect to mass splitting is sufficient for existence. The result applies for specific exponents and a class of strictly convex functions with prescribed growth behavior.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.6

returned_results.slogan: Under certain conditions on V, if the energy for mass M is less than the sum of energies for any split mass, then all minimizing sequences are compact. If minimizing sequences diverge, then there exists a split mass where the energy for that part attains a minimizer and the total energy equals the sum of the energies for the split masses.
returned_results.name: Lemma \thesection .2

returned_results.slogan: A minimizer of the energy functional under a mass constraint has components with separated supports. The distance between any two distinct connected components of the same component function is bounded below by a positive constant. This constant depends only on the given masses and the positive coefficients. The separation holds uniformly for all such components.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.2

returned_results.slogan: For small positive mass values, the energy functional is strictly subadditive. This strict inequality implies that minimizing sequences are compact up to translations and subsequences. Consequently, a minimizer exists for the given mass constraint.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.1

returned_results.slogan: The infimum is achieved by a sum of measures over a set Z. These measures have disjoint supports and correspond to an ordered partition of Y. For each subset in the partition, a specific equality involving the measures and functions holds. For all other points, an inequality condition is satisfied.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.6

returned_results.slogan: A minimizing sequence for the functional F_lambda in the given Sobolev space cannot split into two separate parts as described. The measures mu_nu defined in the referenced equation prevent such a splitting from happening. This result holds under the conditions of the subadditivity assumption.
returned_results.name: Lemma

returned_results.slogan: A minimizing sequence can be split into two parts using smooth cutoff functions centered at a sequence of points with growing radii. The mass of the sequence splits into two positive values that sum to the original total mass. The mass in the annular region between the cutoff scales tends to zero. The sum of the energies of the two parts is at most the energy of the original sequence.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.7

returned_results.slogan: Given a non-negative function in the weak Lp space and a strictly convex function with specific growth conditions, the energy functional defined over a set of density functions with fixed mass has a minimizer. A minimizing sequence converges to this minimizer after appropriate translations if and only if the energy is strictly subadditive for all masses less than the total mass. This condition ensures compactness and the existence of a minimizer. The result holds for densities in L1 and Lq spaces.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.2 (\text{\cite[Theorem II.1]{Lions_1984}})

returned_results.slogan: The theorem considers two smooth, even, non-increasing functions with compact support. It defines a new function by shifting and summing these functions so their supports are disjoint. The derivative of the symmetric decreasing rearrangement of this new function is square-integrable. An inequality bounds the squared L2 norm of this derivative, showing it is at most the original derivative norm minus a fraction of the smaller derivative norm.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.8

returned_results.slogan: The squared L2 norm of the derivative of the symmetric decreasing rearrangement of the sum of two shifted functions is bounded above. This bound is the sum of the squared L2 norms of the derivatives of the individual functions minus a fraction of the smaller of these two squared norms. The functions are smooth, compactly supported, even, nonnegative, and radially nonincreasing. Their shifted versions have disjoint supports.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.6

returned_results.slogan: The symmetric decreasing rearrangement of the sum of two shifted, non-negative, even, smooth, compactly supported functions has a distributional derivative that is square-integrable. The squared L2 norm of this derivative is bounded above by the squared L2 norm of the derivative of the original sum. This bound is reduced by at least three-quarters of the smaller squared L2 norm of the derivatives of the individual functions. The functions are assumed to be non-increasing on the non-negative reals and have disjoint supports after shifting.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.10

returned_results.slogan: Two smooth, even, non-increasing functions with compact support are shifted so their supports do not overlap. The sum of these shifted functions has a symmetric decreasing rearrangement. The derivative of this rearrangement is square integrable. Its squared L2 norm is bounded above by the squared norm of the original derivative minus three-fourths the smaller squared norm of the individual derivatives.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.7

returned_results.slogan: Given nonnegative, even, smooth, compactly supported functions f and g that are non-increasing on the positive reals, consider a function w formed by translating f and g so their supports are disjoint. The symmetric decreasing rearrangement of w has a derivative in L squared. The squared L two norm of this derivative is bounded above by the squared norm of w's derivative minus three-fourths of the minimum of the squared norms of the derivatives of f and g.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.6

returned_results.slogan: The energy of a non-negative bounded function with support contained in a set S is at most the energy of its symmetric decreasing rearrangement.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.2

This holds for all real constants. The symmetric decreasing rearrangement is used to compare the function's energy. The inequality demonstrates a lower bound on the perturbed derivative norm.

This inequality holds for any measurable function. The result compares the energy of the perturbed function to that of its symmetrized version.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2.1

returned_results.slogan: A function's distribution function satisfies an inequality relating its derivative to an integral over level sets. The distribution function is absolutely continuous if and only if the set where the gradient of its symmetric rearrangement is zero has measure zero. If the function and its symmetric rearrangement have equal Dirichlet energy and the absolute continuity condition holds, then the function equals its symmetric rearrangement almost everywhere after translation.

The function w is defined as the sum of u and a shifted v such that their supports do not overlap. This yields an isomorphism between the equivariant cobordism ring of the product and the completed tensor product of the equivariant cobordism of Y and the ordinary cobordism of projective space.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.5

returned_results.slogan: Given a B-minus action on a non-singular variety X and a B-minus w-invariant effective cycle Y in X, there exist B-minus-invariant effective cycles Z1 through Zm. The T-equivariant cohomology class of Y is contained in a sum involving these cycles. The sum includes coefficients from the natural numbers multiplied by classes of negative roots in the set I of w. This relation holds in the T-equivariant cohomology ring of X.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.3

returned_results.slogan: Given a G-irreducible scheme Y with a smooth G-prime divisor D and an admissible tower P over Y with certain sheaves, there exists another admissible tower P' over Y and quasi-admissible towers Q0 through Q3 over D with associated invertible sheaves. The construction modifies the tower at a specific level by twisting one summand by the divisor. An equality holds in the equivariant algebraic cobordism group of Y, expressing the difference between the classes of P' and P as an alternating sum of classes from the towers over D.
returned_results.name: Lemma 6.5

returned_results.slogan: The image of the injective pull-back map from the equivariant cohomology of the flag variety to the twisted group algebra consists of sums over the Weyl group. Each sum has coefficients and basis elements satisfying a divisibility condition. For every root, the difference of coefficients corresponding to elements related by the root reflection is divisible by the root. This characterizes the elements in the image of the map.
returned_results.name: Theorem 9.2

returned_results.slogan: The equivariant cohomology of w Sigma is described by a set of tuples indexed by elements of W to the P. Each tuple consists of rational functions in the dual of the torus T sub w. The functions satisfy that their differences lie in the ideal generated by a specific linear combination. This condition applies whenever the indices are related by multiplication with a transposition.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.1

returned_results.slogan: The product of y_i and the identity element equals the difference between y_i raised to w and a weighted term involving y_id raised to w, plus a weighted divisor class. Similarly, the product of u_alpha and the identity equals w times u_alpha plus a weighted divisor class. The weights depend on w_i, w_id, and w_alpha. These relations hold in the equivariant cohomology ring of the complement of a hyperplane arrangement.
returned_results.name: Proposition 5.4

returned_results.slogan: A T-invariant subvariety Y in G/B has an equivariant homology class expressed as a sum over the Weyl group. This sum involves Schubert varieties X_w multiplied by coefficients f_w. Each coefficient f_w is a nonnegative linear combination of monomials in the roots alpha_1 through alpha_d. The result holds for every element w in the Weyl group.
returned_results.name: Corollary 5.3

returned_results.slogan: The equivariant cohomology ring of a GKM-variety is isomorphic to the set of tuples of elements from the polynomial ring, indexed by the graph vertices. Each tuple must satisfy that the difference of entries at adjacent vertices is divisible by the weight associated to the connecting edge. This holds for every edge in the moment graph of the variety. The result provides a combinatorial description of the cohomology ring.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.7

returned_results.slogan: The equivariant cohomology ring of a GKM-variety with a moment graph is isomorphic to the set of tuples of elements from the base ring, indexed by the graph vertices. Each tuple must satisfy that the difference of entries at adjacent vertices is divisible by the label of the connecting edge. The base ring is typically the polynomial ring in the characters of the torus. This result characterizes the cohomology ring in terms of combinatorial data from the moment graph.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.11

returned_results.slogan: The GKM graph of a GKM action determines the equivariant cohomology algebra. The inclusion of the fixed point set into the manifold induces an isomorphism of R-algebras. This isomorphism maps the equivariant cohomology to a set of tuples indexed by the graph vertices. Each tuple consists of elements in R such that the difference of values at adjacent vertices is divisible by the label of the connecting edge.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.7

returned_results.slogan: Given a reductive group with Weyl group and weight lattice, the Lazard ring and a specific algebra S are defined. The Weyl group acts on S by permuting variables. A product is defined on the direct sum over the Weyl group, and a coinvariant ring is considered. An injective algebra homomorphism maps the coinvariant ring to a subalgebra of the direct sum, characterized by congruence conditions involving positive roots.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.1

returned_results.slogan: Complex cobordism of a point is isomorphic to the Lazard ring. This result is due to Quillen. It identifies the coefficient ring of complex cobordism with the universal formal group law ring.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.6

returned_results.slogan: For a special reductive algebraic group, the map from the tensor product of the algebraic cobordism of a scheme and the equivariant algebraic cobordism to the equivariant algebraic cobordism of the scheme is an isomorphism. The equivariant algebraic cobordism is a projective module over the Lazard ring. Its dual is isomorphic to the ring of invariants of the completed representation ring of a maximal torus under the Weyl group. This dual ring is also isomorphic to the ring of invariants of a formal power series ring in variables corresponding to the rank of the group.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.2.2

returned_results.slogan: The natural map from equivariant cobordism of a space with group G to that with group T induces an isomorphism of C(G)-modules. This isomorphism identifies the G-equivariant cobordism ring with the Weyl group invariants of the T-equivariant cobordism ring. In particular, the ring C(G) is isomorphic to the Weyl group invariants of C(T).
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.3

returned_results.slogan: The cohomology ring of the homogeneous space G over L with integer coefficients is isomorphic to the ring of invariants of the Weyl group of L acting on the symmetric algebra. This ring is further isomorphic to the quotient of the symmetric algebra invariants by the ideal generated by the positive degree invariants of the full Weyl group.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.4

returned_results.slogan: The cobordism ring of X is isomorphic to a polynomial ring with coefficients in the Lazard ring and generators of degree one. This polynomial ring is quotiented by the ideal generated by homogeneous symmetric polynomials of positive degree. The isomorphism identifies the cobordism ring with this quotient structure.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1

returned_results.slogan: The ring of invariants under the Weyl group action is isomorphic to the algebra of dominant weights with coefficients in a polynomial ring. This isomorphism holds as algebras over the ring of polynomials in a parameter. It identifies symmetric functions on the coroot lattice with polynomials in the dominant chamber. The result is expressed using formal variables and coefficients from a commutative ring.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.1

returned_results.slogan: The cohomology ring of G over P is contained in the cohomology ring of G over B. It consists of those elements that are invariant under the Weyl group of G over P. This Weyl group is the same as the Weyl group of L, where P is written as LAN. The equality holds with rational coefficients.
returned_results.name: Lemma 16 (Borel \cite{Borel:1953})

returned_results.slogan: The cohomology ring of the Weyl group with integer coefficients is isomorphic to the algebra of symmetric functions.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.2

returned_results.slogan: The equivariant cohomology ring of X with respect to S is given by the tensor product of symmetric algebras over the Weyl group invariants. This ring is constructed using symmetric algebras on the duals of the Lie algebras of T and S. Elements in this ring are represented as polynomials in two sets of variables. The variables correspond to bases of the dual Lie algebras of T and S.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.1

trajectory.query: restriction to torus fixed points injective image characterized by edge divisibility in equivariant algebraic cobordism cellular GKM variety

returned_results.slogan: For a torus action of GKM type with fixed points, the equivariant cohomology injects into the direct sum of the cohomology of the classifying space over all fixed points. The image consists of tuples of elements from the cohomology of the classifying space. These tuples satisfy that the difference between entries corresponding to adjacent fixed points is divisible by the label on the connecting edge. The divisibility condition holds with some element from the cohomology of the classifying space.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.8 (\cite [Theorem 7.2]{GKM})

returned_results.slogan: For a torus acting on a compact GKM2 manifold with fixed points, the equivariant cohomology algebra maps injectively into a direct sum of polynomial rings. This image consists of tuples of polynomials corresponding to each fixed point. The polynomials must agree on the kernel of the weight associated to any edge connecting two fixed points in the GKM graph. This condition characterizes the equivariant cohomology ring as a subalgebra of the product over fixed points.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.2

returned_results.slogan: For a compact Hamiltonian torus space meeting conditions A and B, the equivariant cohomology map into the fixed point set is injective. The image consists of tuples of rational functions over the fixed points. These functions satisfy that their differences are divisible by certain weights along edges in the graph. This characterization is known as the GKM description.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.8 (Goresky-Kottwitz-MacPherson \cite {GKM})

returned_results.slogan: For a Hamiltonian GKM space with pairwise coprime weights at fixed points, consider a map from the fixed point set to the cohomology of the classifying space. This map lies in the equivariant cohomology ring if and only if for every edge in the GKM graph, the difference between the images at adjacent vertices is divisible by the label on that edge.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.3

returned_results.slogan: Given a GKM-space M, the restriction map from equivariant K-theory to a product of representation rings over fixed points is injective. The image consists of tuples where each component is a representation of the torus. For any two indices I and J with J less than or equal to I, the difference between corresponding components is divisible by the Euler class of a certain vector bundle. This condition characterizes the elements in the image of the restriction map.
returned_results.name: Theorem 6.3

returned_results.slogan: For a smooth filtrable variety with a split torus action, the inclusion of the fixed point locus induces a map between equivariant algebraic cobordism rings. This map is injective. It becomes an isomorphism after inverting a specific multiplicative set.
returned_results.name: Theorem 7.1

returned_results.slogan: For a smooth T-filtrable scheme with a torus action and finitely many fixed points, the pullback map from equivariant algebraic cobordism of the scheme to that of the fixed points is injective. The image of this map is the intersection of the images of similar pullback maps for all codimension one subtori. These pullback maps are taken with rational coefficients. The result holds when considering the inclusion of the fixed point subscheme.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.19

returned_results.slogan: The map from the T-equivariant algebraic cobordism of a smooth projective variety to that of its fixed point locus under a split torus action is injective. This map becomes an isomorphism after inverting a certain set M in the coefficient ring.
returned_results.name: Corollary 7.2

returned_results.slogan: The pullback map from the equivariant cohomology of a space with a torus action to the equivariant cohomology of its fixed point set is injective. This holds when the space has a torus-invariant cell decomposition with only even-dimensional cells. The ring coefficients must have torsion coprime to the order of the stabilizer group's component group. The result applies to spaces with finitely many cells in each dimension.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.2

returned_results.slogan: The restriction map from equivariant K-theory of a toric variety to its fixed point set is injective. Its image consists of tuples of functions that satisfy congruence conditions along codimension one cone intersections. The forgetful map to ordinary K-theory is surjective, with kernel generated by differences of functions from their evaluation at the identity. Similar statements hold for equivariant Chow cohomology, with analogous conditions and a surjective forgetful map to ordinary Chow cohomology.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.1

trajectory.query: equivariant algebraic cobordism G/B Bott-Samelson basis free S-module flag variety

returned_results.slogan: The T-equivariant algebraic cobordism ring of the flag variety X equals G over B is a free module over the symmetric algebra S. Its basis consists of the Bott-Samelson classes. The same statement applies to the ordinary algebraic cobordism ring of X. Both rings share this structural property.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.10

returned_results.slogan: The algebraic cobordism ring of the flag variety is a free module over the Lazard ring. It is generated by the Bott-Samelson classes. Each class corresponds to a Weyl group element. A reduced decomposition is chosen for each element to define these generators.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.1

returned_results.slogan: The Bott-Samelson resolution class in the algebraic cobordism ring of a complete flag variety equals a product of operators applied to the class of a point. This product is formed by applying operators corresponding to a sequence of simple roots. The operators are applied in the order given by the tuple of simple roots. The result holds for any such tuple and any complete flag variety.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.2

returned_results.slogan: The T-equivariant algebraic cobordism ring of a toric variety X is a free module over the symmetric algebra S, with basis given by the classes of invariant subvarieties. The non-equivariant algebraic cobordism ring is a free module over the Lazard ring, with the same basis. There is an isomorphism between the motivic cobordism ring of X and a direct sum of copies of the motivic cobordism ring of the base field. This isomorphism is linear over the motivic cobordism ring of the base field.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.9

returned_results.slogan: The algebraic cobordism ring of the flag bundle of a vector bundle over a smooth scheme is isomorphic to a polynomial ring over the base cobordism ring, modulo the ideal generated by the differences between elementary symmetric functions and the Chern classes of the vector bundle.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.2.1

returned_results.slogan: The equivariant cohomology of the Bott-Samelson variety for a positive indexing sequence is isomorphic to a tensor product of bimodules over the torus-equivariant cohomology. Each factor in the tensor product is itself isomorphic to a tensor product of two copies of the torus-equivariant cohomology over the equivariant cohomology of a point for a subgroup. Additionally, the equivariant cohomology of the flag variety is isomorphic to the Hochschild homology of the Bott-Samelson bimodule with coefficients in the torus-equivariant cohomology.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.8

returned_results.slogan: The ring homomorphism r^G_X induces an isomorphism c_X from S(T) tensor S(G) L to the algebraic cobordism ring of X. This isomorphism is of L-algebras. When G is the general linear group GL_n(k), the cobordism ring of the flag variety G/B is isomorphic to a polynomial ring modulo an ideal. The ideal is generated by homogeneous symmetric polynomials of positive degree.
returned_results.name: Theorem 8.1

returned_results.slogan: The equivariant cohomology of the Bott-Samelson variety is a rank two free module over the torus-equivariant cohomology ring. It is generated by the classes 1 and delta. The class delta satisfies the relation delta squared plus alpha times delta equals zero. Here, alpha is a degree two element corresponding to the root difference x_i minus x_{i+1}.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.1

returned_results.slogan: Given a Real oriented spectrum and a complete flag in a complete Real universe, the equivariant cohomology of complex projective space is a free module over the base cohomology ring. The basis consists of products of certain classes associated to the irreducible representations in the flag.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.10

returned_results.slogan: The natural map from the tensor product of two copies of the symmetric algebra of the torus over the symmetric algebra of the group to the equivariant motivic cohomology of the flag variety is an isomorphism of algebras. This map sends a tensor product of elements to their product under the restriction map. The result holds for a connected and split reductive group over a field with a split maximal torus and a chosen Borel subgroup. The isomorphism preserves the module structure over the symmetric algebra of the torus.

returned_results.slogan: Mutation at a vertex k in a quiver Q induces an isomorphism between the associated groups of Q and its mutated quiver. The isomorphism sends the generator for vertex i to a conjugate by the generator for k if i points to k or under specific arc rotation conditions. For all other vertices, the generators map directly without conjugation. This defines a group isomorphism preserving the structure after mutation.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.11

returned_results.slogan: Given a quiver Q and a mutated quiver Q prime, the theorem defines a group homomorphism from the group of Q to the group of Q prime. The homomorphism sends two generators to conjugates by a specific generator in the target group. The remaining generators are mapped directly to their counterparts. This mapping preserves the group structure defined by the quiver relations.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.31

returned_results.slogan: For a quiver with potential from a triangulated marked surface, mutation at a vertex gamma induces canonical group isomorphisms between the braid groups of the original and mutated quivers. The isomorphism from the original to the mutated braid group sends a vertex alpha to alpha prime if no arrows exist from gamma to alpha, or to alpha prime conjugated by gamma prime otherwise. The inverse isomorphism sends alpha prime to alpha if no arrows exist from alpha prime to gamma prime, or to alpha conjugated by gamma otherwise. These maps are mutually inverse and preserve the group structure.

returned_results.slogan: Given a quiver Q and its mutated version Q prime, there are groups G_Q and G_Q prime with generators satisfying relations from each quiver. returned_results.slogan: The quiver from group mutation is isomorphic to the mutated quiver, with the isomorphism preserving the layered structure. Within each group, plain and primed nodes are exchanged under this mapping.
