returned_results.name: Theorem 9.1 ($W_1$ continuity of the von Neumann entropy)

returned_results.slogan: The conditional entropy difference between two joint distributions is bounded by a function of their total variation distance and the size of the sample space. The bound involves the binary entropy function and a logarithmic term. The total variation distance measures the discrepancy between the distributions. The inequality holds for any two distributions with the same sample spaces.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4 (Classical Alicki-Fannes inequality {\cite {AF04}})

returned_results.slogan: When the relative entropy between two quantum states is finite, the difference in their relative entropies to a reference state is bounded. This bound depends on the trace distance between the states and the binary entropy function. The binary entropy function is defined using logarithms of its input and one minus the input. The inequality holds for any two densities with a given trace distance.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.7

trajectory.query: continuity bound entanglement of formation via Nielsen Winter technique corollary 4 Winter continuity bounds

returned_results.slogan: A concave continuous nonnegative function f on the state space satisfying a specific property yields an entanglement measure E superscript f. This measure is an entanglement monotone. It is also continuous on the bipartite state space.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2

returned_results.slogan: For a quantum channel Phi, two statements are equivalent. The function mapping state rho to the output entropy H_Phi(rho) is continuous and bounded on the set of extreme points of the state space. This is equivalent to the function being continuous on any subset where the von Neumann entropy is continuous.
returned_results.name: Corollary \thecorollary

returned_results.slogan: The relative entropy of entanglement is bounded below by the robustness of entanglement and above by the robustness divided by the concurrence. This bound is tight, meaning it cannot be generally improved. For any positive delta, there exist cases where the relative entropy is at least one minus delta over the concurrence times the robustness.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.2

returned_results.slogan: The definition of E_F remains unchanged when the ensemble size is limited to at most m squared times n squared. The entanglement cost equals the regularized entanglement of formation. Several inequalities relate entanglement measures, such as the entanglement of formation being at least the relative entropy of entanglement. Lower bounds on the squashed entanglement and regularized relative entropy of entanglement are given in terms of distance to separable states using trace and Frobenius norms.
returned_results.name: Lemma 1

returned_results.slogan: The difference in von Neumann entropy between two n-dimensional quantum states is bounded by a term involving their trace distance and the Shannon entropy. Specifically, the bound is the trace distance times the natural log of n minus one, plus the binary entropy of the trace distance. For any positive epsilon, there exists a sufficiently small gamma such that if the trace distance and deviations from unit trace are less than gamma, then the entropy difference is at most epsilon. This shows the continuity of entropy on the set of positive operators close to being density matrices.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.3

returned_results.slogan: If the function mapping a state to its entropy is continuous and bounded on the set of extreme states, then it is also continuous on the set of states with Schmidt rank at most k for every natural number k.
returned_results.name: Lemma 6

returned_results.slogan: For AF factors A and B, a convex decomposition of a normal state omega on the tensor product A tensor B is considered. The inequality provides bounds on the entanglement of formation E_I of omega in terms of the weighted sum of the E_I of the decomposed states. The lower bound includes a negative entropy term, while the upper bound adds twice the entropy term. This result relates the entanglement of the mixture to that of its components.
returned_results.name: Lemma 10

returned_results.slogan: The squashed entanglement and entanglement of formation for any bipartite state are both at least the maximum of zero or the entropy of one subsystem minus the joint entropy. These lower bounds are tight, as there exist states where both measures equal the entropy difference between a subsystem and the whole. This equality holds even when the subsystem and joint entropies take any non-negative values.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.2 (Lower bounds for ${\rm E}_{\rm sq}$ and ${\rm E}_{\rm f}$)

returned_results.slogan: A completely positive map satisfies an inequality involving conditional entropy and a sandwiched Rényi divergence. This implies that the amortized entanglement of a channel is bounded by the regularized sandwiched Rényi divergence between the channel and the map.
returned_results.name: Lemma \thesection .5

returned_results.slogan: The theorem provides an inequality involving a quantum state and a measurement framework. It states that n minus twice a constant c is less than the logarithm of an integral plus the logarithm of n. The integral involves the exponential of a mutual information term between two copies of the quantum state. This result is relativized to an elementary positive operator-valued measure.
returned_results.name: Theorem 8 (\cite{EpsteinAPhysics24})

trajectory.query: Krein-Rutman theorem positive compact operator largest eigenvalue nonnegative eigenfunction spectral radius

returned_results.slogan: The Krein-Rutman Theorem applies to a compact linear operator mapping a total cone in a real Banach space into itself with a positive spectral radius. It guarantees the existence of a nonzero element in the cone that is an eigenvector of the operator. This eigenvector corresponds to the spectral radius eigenvalue.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.1

returned_results.slogan: The Krein-Rutman theorem applies to a compact linear operator on a Hilbert space with a total cone. The operator must be positive, mapping the cone into itself, and have a positive spectral radius. The spectral radius is an eigenvalue of the operator. There exists a nonzero eigenvector in the cone corresponding to this eigenvalue.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2

returned_results.slogan: The Krein-Rutman theorem applies to a compact linear operator on a real Banach space with a total cone. If the operator maps the cone into itself and has a positive spectral radius, then there exists a nonzero element in the cone. This element is an eigenvector of the operator corresponding to the spectral radius.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.8

returned_results.slogan: The Krein-Rutman theorem applies to a real Banach space with a total order cone. It states that for a positive, compact linear operator with positive spectral radius, the spectral radius is an eigenvalue of the operator. The operator has an eigenvector in the cone, and its adjoint has an eigenvector in the dual cone.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.4

returned_results.slogan: The Generalized Krein-Rutman theorem applies to a completely continuous operator on a solid cone. The operator must be positively homogeneous, monotone increasing, and strongly positive. Under these conditions, the operator has a positive eigenvalue. This eigenvalue corresponds to a positive eigenfunction in the interior of the cone.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.1

returned_results.slogan: A compact nonnegative operator on L2 space with a nonzero eigenvalue has a nonnegative eigenfunction corresponding to the spectral radius.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.17

returned_results.slogan: In a Banach space with a dense convex cone, a positive compact linear operator with positive spectral radius has that spectral radius as an eigenvalue. The corresponding eigenfunction is positive.
returned_results.name: Theorem 9.1 (Krein-Rutman Theorem)

returned_results.slogan: The spectral radius of K is strictly positive. There exists a continuous eigenfunction e such that applying K to e equals the spectral radius times e. This eigenfunction e is strictly positive everywhere.
returned_results.name: Theorem A.2.5

returned_results.slogan: In a Banach space with a total cone, a compact linear operator that is positive and has a positive spectral radius will have that spectral radius as an eigenvalue. The corresponding eigenvector is a nonzero element of the cone.
returned_results.name: Theorem A.2 (The Krein-Rutman theorem)

returned_results.slogan: The Krein-Rutman result states that if the spectral radius is positive, it is an eigenvalue with a nonnegative right eigenfunction. The de Pagter theorem says an irreducible operator has positive spectral radius unless it is zero on a one-dimensional space. The Perron-Jentzsch theorem asserts that for an irreducible operator with positive spectral radius, the eigenvalue is simple, the eigenfunction is positive almost everywhere, and is unique. Schwartz's result expresses the multiplicity of eigenvalues and the spectral radius in terms of a decomposition.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.2

trajectory.query: analytic perturbation theorem isolated simple eigenvalue holomorphic family of compact operators power series expansion eigenvalue

returned_results.slogan: For a holomorphic family of operators with a simple isolated eigenvalue at a point, there exists a neighborhood around that point. In this neighborhood, the eigenvalue persists as a unique, isolated, and algebraically simple eigenvalue. This eigenvalue depends analytically on the parameter. An associated eigenvector also exists and depends analytically on the parameter.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.2

returned_results.slogan: The Kato-Rellich theorem states that for a self-adjoint holomorphic family of operators, a simple isolated eigenvalue persists under small complex perturbations. In a neighborhood of zero, the perturbed operator has exactly one eigenvalue near the original one, which remains isolated and simple. This eigenvalue depends analytically on the perturbation parameters. An associated eigenfunction also exists and varies analytically with the parameters.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.4

returned_results.slogan: A self-adjoint operator depending analytically on a real parameter has an analytic expansion. If the operator at zero has an isolated eigenvalue of finite multiplicity, then for small parameter values, the perturbed eigenvalues near the original eigenvalue are real and analytic. The corresponding eigenvectors are also analytic and orthogonal. Each perturbed eigenvector and eigenvalue pair satisfies the eigenvalue equation for the operator.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.3

returned_results.slogan: Consider a family of regular, formally self-adjoint operators near zero, with the operator at zero being self-adjoint. If a finite-multiplicity eigenvalue is isolated in the spectrum of the operator at zero, then there exist convergent power series for eigenvalues and corresponding eigenvectors near zero. These eigenvectors form an orthonormal system and diagonalize the perturbed operator. The perturbed eigenvalues remain isolated in the spectrum for sufficiently small perturbations.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.2

returned_results.slogan: If the eigenvalues are simple, then the eigenvalues of the problem are analytic in epsilon. Each eigenvalue can be expressed as a power series in epsilon. The series expansion starts with the unperturbed eigenvalue. The coefficients of the series are determined by the analytic structure.
returned_results.name: Theorem 15

returned_results.slogan: A bounded linear operator with an isolated simple eigenvalue has a corresponding closed disc containing only that eigenvalue. For operators near the original one, a unique eigenvalue exists inside the disc. The function mapping these nearby operators to their eigenvalues is analytic.
returned_results.name: Lemma 5.2

returned_results.slogan: For a linear operator depending holomorphically on a parameter near zero, if the unperturbed operator has a simple eigenvalue, then the perturbed eigenvalue and its associated eigenprojection are holomorphic near zero. The eigenvalue expansion includes correction terms given by traces involving the perturbation and projection coefficients. The eigennilpotent associated with the perturbed eigenvalue is identically zero.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.4 (A simple case)

returned_results.slogan: For a holomorphic family of type A operators, a simple isolated eigenvalue persists as a holomorphic function of the parameter near the original value. This eigenvalue remains simple and isolated in the spectrum for small parameter perturbations. Under an additional nondegeneracy condition on an eigenvector and a dual vector, there also exists a holomorphic eigenvector function. This eigenvector is normalized with respect to the dual vector.
returned_results.name: Proposition A.1 (cf. \cite {B85})

returned_results.slogan: For an analytic family of operators near a parameter value, an isolated non-degenerate eigenvalue persists as a single isolated non-degenerate eigenvalue in the spectrum nearby. This eigenvalue depends analytically on the parameter. There also exists an analytic eigenvector corresponding to this eigenvalue. Both the eigenvalue and eigenvector are analytic functions in a neighborhood of the parameter.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.3

returned_results.slogan: The Kato-Rellich theorem concerns a self-adjoint holomorphic family of operators. If zero is an isolated and algebraically simple eigenvalue of the operator at zero, then near zero there exists a unique isolated simple eigenvalue. This eigenvalue depends analytically on the parameter. An associated eigenfunction also depends analytically on the parameter.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.2

trajectory.query: persistence probability stationary Gaussian sequence asymptotic largest eigenvalue integral operator

returned_results.slogan: A sequence of continuous centered Gaussian processes with non-negative correlations converges uniformly in their correlation structure to a stationary limiting process. Under conditions on the decay of correlations and the continuity of the limiting process's persistence exponent, the asymptotic persistence probabilities of the sequence and the limit become identical. The result holds for every real threshold level. The conditions ensure that the tail behavior of the maximum over time intervals is preserved in the limit.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.6

returned_results.slogan: For a centered Gaussian process with stationary increments, if the variance function has regularly varying indices in specified ranges, then the limit of the persistence probability over certain intervals is positive and finite as time tends to infinity.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.7

returned_results.slogan: A centered Gaussian process with stationary increments and continuous paths has a finite persistence limit for any positive threshold. The variance function of the process must satisfy certain regularity conditions. The persistence probability over an interval converges to a finite limit as the interval length goes to infinity. This holds regardless of the specific positive value chosen for the threshold.
returned_results.name: Lemma 5.4

returned_results.slogan: For a stationary centered Gaussian process with given covariance behavior near zero and a correlation decay condition, the probability that its maximum over an interval exceeds a large threshold is asymptotically equivalent to a specific expression. This expression involves Pickands constant, the length of the interval, and the threshold, scaled by the process variance. The asymptotic form holds when the right-hand side tends to zero. The result applies under the stated conditions on the parameters.
returned_results.name: Lemma 10

returned_results.slogan: For a stationary centered Gaussian sequence, if the spectral measure's density meets a condition, then the logarithm of the probability that the maximum absolute partial sum stays below a growing threshold is asymptotically equivalent to a negative constant times a slowly varying function of the threshold raised to a power, multiplied by the sequence length. This holds as the length goes to infinity, the adjusted threshold term grows, and the threshold itself increases. The slowly varying function is defined in relation to another function derived from the spectral measure. The constant involved is taken from a referenced equation.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3

returned_results.slogan: For a centered stationary Gaussian process with a covariance function meeting certain conditions, and an independent nonnegative random variable T satisfying a specific assumption, the probability that the supremum of the process over the interval from 0 to T exceeds a large threshold u is asymptotically equivalent to the product of the expected value of T, a constant, and the tail function of the standard normal distribution. The asymptotic expression holds as u tends to infinity. The result involves parameters from the covariance function and the distribution of T.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.1

returned_results.slogan: A centered Gaussian process with continuous paths and stationary increments has an infinite-time persistence probability asymptotically equivalent to a constant times u divided by m of u times Delta of u, multiplied by the tail function Psi of m of u. The constant involves the square root of 2A pi over B and a term H eta Gamma of zero. The functions Delta of u and eta are defined elsewhere. The variance sigma squared of u divided by u approaches a limit between zero and infinity as u grows large.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.1

returned_results.slogan: A stationary continuous Gaussian process with mean zero has a covariance function whose integral grows slower than time. The process also has a lower bound on its smallest eigenvalue that increases with time. The random survival function associated with this process converges to zero almost surely as time goes to infinity.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1

returned_results.slogan: The limiting distribution of the largest real eigenvalue of a matrix is given by a determinant involving integral operators. The expression depends on an operator defined by a Gaussian kernel and another operator built from a specific integral kernel. The result holds as the matrix size tends to infinity. The operator in the kernel is the square of the Gaussian operator.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.1 (Rider, Sinclair \cite {rider2014extremal}, 2014; Poplavskyi, Tribe, Zaboronski \cite {poplavskyi2017distribution}, 2017)

returned_results.slogan: The probability that the largest eigenvalue is less than a value t is given by the square root of the determinant of I minus T times the indicator function of t, multiplied by a factor Gamma_t. The operator T is defined by an integral kernel involving exponentials. Gamma_t is expressed in terms of the inverse of I minus T times the indicator, along with integrals of Gaussian functions and their cumulative distributions. The terms a_t and b_t are defined using these functions and the inverse operator.
returned_results.name: Theorem (B. Rider and C. D. Sinclair, 2014)

trajectory.query: compact Hilbert-Schmidt integral operator self-adjoint compactness spectral theorem kernel operator on L2

returned_results.slogan: An operator on a separable L2 space is Hilbert-Schmidt if and only if it is an integral operator with a square-integrable kernel. The kernel function must belong to the L2 space of the product measure. The Hilbert-Schmidt norm of the operator equals the L2 norm of its kernel.
returned_results.name: Theorem B.11 ({\cite[Theorem VI.23]{reed2012methods}})

returned_results.slogan: If the kernel H_mu is Hilbert-Schmidt for a probability measure mu in P_2, then the associated integral operator on L^2 is compact and self-adjoint. This operator maps functions by integrating against the kernel. As a result, there exists an orthonormal basis of eigenfunctions for the L^2 space. The eigenfunctions correspond to the operator's spectral decomposition.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.2

returned_results.slogan: An operator from L squared mu to L squared nu is Hilbert-Schmidt if and only if it has an integration kernel in L squared of the product measure. The kernel satisfies an integral representation for all functions in the respective spaces. The Hilbert-Schmidt norm of the operator equals the L squared norm of the kernel. Such operators are compact.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.10

returned_results.slogan: An operator on a separable Hilbert space is a Hilbert-Schmidt operator if and only if it is an integral operator with a square-integrable kernel. The kernel function belongs to the space of square-integrable functions on the product measure space. The Hilbert-Schmidt norm of the operator equals the L2 norm of its kernel function. This equivalence holds for almost every point in the underlying measure space.
returned_results.name: Proposition B1.7 (Hilbert-Schmidt operators as kernel operator)

returned_results.slogan: A self-adjoint compact integral operator defined by a symmetric kernel has an eigenfunction expansion. The kernel equals the sum over all eigenvalues multiplied by the products of corresponding eigenfunctions. This equality holds in the sense of L-squared convergence on the product space.
returned_results.name: Lemma A.2

returned_results.slogan: A Hilbert-Schmidt kernel produces a compact operator. The operator acts on a tensor product of L2 spaces. It is defined by integrating the kernel against the input function. Compactness holds when the kernel has finite Hilbert-Schmidt norm.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.9

returned_results.slogan: A bounded operator between two L-squared spaces is a Hilbert-Schmidt operator exactly when it can be represented by an integral kernel from the product L-squared space. The operator acts by integrating a function against this kernel. The Hilbert-Schmidt norm of the operator equals the L-squared norm of the kernel function.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.6

returned_results.slogan: The spectrum of the Hilbert-Schmidt kernel operator equals the spectrum of a specified operator. Both operators are defined on the same function space. The result holds for the given kernel and operator.
returned_results.name: Lemma 8.1

returned_results.slogan: The Hilbert-Schmidt norm of an operator with a given kernel in L2 space equals the square root of the integral of the squared absolute value of the kernel over its domain.
returned_results.name: Lemma A1.

returned_results.slogan: The integral operator is Hilbert-Schmidt. It is also self-adjoint and positive semi-definite.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.4

trajectory.query: Jentzsch theorem positive integral operator simple largest eigenvalue positive eigenfunction

returned_results.slogan: Under the given assumptions, there exists a nonzero positive eigenfunction in the space of integrable functions. This eigenfunction corresponds to the positive spectral radius of the operator. The operator applied to this function equals the product of the spectral radius and the function itself.
returned_results.name: Theorem 8.6

returned_results.slogan: A compact integral operator with a positive kernel on an open set has a positive spectral radius. This spectral radius is a simple eigenvalue. Every eigenfunction corresponding to this eigenvalue is either positive or negative almost everywhere. The operator is defined by integration against a kernel that is positive almost everywhere.
returned_results.name: Lemma Z.6

returned_results.slogan: The spectral radius of the integral operator with kernel K is an eigenvalue. This eigenvalue has multiplicity one and corresponds to a positive continuous eigenfunction. All other eigenvalues have strictly smaller absolute values.
returned_results.name: Theorem A.2 (Jentzsch \cite{Jen} (1912), cf. Hochstadt \cite{Hch})

returned_results.slogan: The integral operator has simple and positive eigenvalues.
returned_results.name: Theorem

returned_results.slogan: The largest eigenvalue in absolute value for a convolution type compact operator is positive and has multiplicity one. The eigenfunction associated with this eigenvalue can be selected to be positive.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.1

returned_results.slogan: The operator A_lambda has a positive eigenvalue equal to its spectral radius with a positive eigenfunction in L1 space when lambda is greater than negative infimum of a. This holds if the range of J^n is contained in Lp for some p between 1 and infinity and some natural number n. It also holds if J is a convolution type kernel with an absolutely bounded K. Alternatively, it holds if there exists an L1 function c such that J is bounded by c.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2

returned_results.slogan: For an integral operator defined by a nonnegative kernel on an Lp space over a sigma-finite measure space, if some power of the operator is compact and the kernel satisfies a positivity condition between complementary sets, then the spectral radius is positive and is an eigenvalue. This eigenvalue has a unique normalized eigenfunction that is positive almost everywhere on any set of positive measure. If the kernel is strictly positive almost everywhere, then all other eigenvalues are strictly smaller in absolute value than the spectral radius.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.6

returned_results.slogan: The leading eigenfunction corresponding to the largest eigenvalue is strictly positive on the interval from zero to one, up to multiplication by a constant.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.11

returned_results.slogan: An operator M on L^2 of a space Z has a power M^k that improves positivity. The eigenvalue of M with the largest absolute value is a real and positive number. This eigenvalue is also simple, meaning it has no multiplicity. The corresponding eigenfunction is positive everywhere on Z.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.7 (Kre\u{\i }n-Rutman)

returned_results.slogan: The operator P defined by the integral of a positive smooth kernel K has a simple positive leading eigenvalue. The eigenfunction associated with this eigenvalue is positive and smooth.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.7

trajectory.query: injective modules generate derived category noetherian ring theorem Rickard theorem 3.3

returned_results.slogan: The triangulated category of injective complexes over a ring is compactly generated by injective resolutions of Noetherian modules. A canonical functor from the homotopy category to the derived category induces an equivalence. This equivalence maps the compact objects in the homotopy category of injectives to the bounded derived category of finitely generated modules.
returned_results.name: Proposition 8.9

returned_results.slogan: If injective modules generate the derived category of a ring graded over an abelian group, then the graded injective modules also generate the derived category.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.23

returned_results.slogan: Derived equivalent rings have equivalent derived categories. If injective modules generate the derived category for one ring, then injectives also generate for the other ring. This property transfers between derived equivalent rings.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.4

returned_results.slogan: For any Noetherian ring R, three specific pairs of injective cotorsion pairs in the chain complex category Ch(R) are given. In each case, the second pair is right localizable to the first, and the resulting quotient models the derived category of R. These pairs lead to recollements involving homotopy categories of Gorenstein injective and DG-injective complexes. The derived category is equivalent to the homotopy category of DG-injective complexes.
returned_results.name: Theorem 8.2

returned_results.slogan: For a left and right noetherian ring A with a dualizing complex R, the localizing subcategory generated by the restriction of R to A equals the localizing subcategory generated by the injective A-modules. This equality holds in the derived category of A.
returned_results.name: Proposition 5.2

returned_results.slogan: For a noetherian ring with a dualizing complex, if a complex of injective modules is K-injective, then three conditions are equivalent. The first condition is that the complex lies in a certain class of complexes. The second condition states that the image under a specific functor lies in the localizing subcategory generated by the dualizing complex. The third condition asserts the existence of an exact triangle involving a module from that localizing subcategory and a totally acyclic complex.
returned_results.name: Theorem 7.11

returned_results.slogan: The homotopy category of injective modules over a noetherian ring is compactly generated, and its compact objects are equivalent to the bounded derived category of finitely generated modules. The homotopy category of acyclic complexes of injective modules is also compactly generated, with compact objects equivalent to the singularity category. The homotopy category of totally acyclic complexes of injective modules is compactly generated if the ring has a dualizing complex. For an Artin algebra, the compact objects of this category are equivalent to the stable category of Gorenstein projective modules precisely when the algebra is virtually Gorenstein.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.20

returned_results.slogan: The stable derived category of a ring with finite global injective dimension is compactly generated. It is equivalent to the bounded derived category modulo the homotopy category of injectives. It is also equivalent to the bounded derived category modulo the homotopy category of projectives. Both equivalences yield compact generation.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.10

returned_results.slogan: In a recollement of derived categories forming a ladder of height two, if the recollement is at the bottom and injectives generate for the middle ring, then injectives generate for the right ring. If the recollement is at the top and injectives generate for the middle ring, then injectives generate for the left ring. If injectives generate for both the left and right rings, then injectives generate for the middle ring.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.9

returned_results.slogan: Given a ring homomorphism from B to A, if A has finite flat dimension as a left B-module and the restriction of A-modules generates the derived category of B, then injectives generating for A implies injectives generate for B. Similarly, if A has finite projective dimension as a right B-module and the restriction cogenerates the derived category of B, then projectives cogenerating for A implies projectives cogenerate for B.
returned_results.name: Lemma 5.2

trajectory.query: bounded complex of pure-injectives implies localizing subcategory generated by injectives is whole derived category

returned_results.slogan: In an abelian category with enough injectives and generators, the bounded derived category with respect to a localizing subcategory is equivalent to the bounded derived category of the localized category.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.12

returned_results.slogan: Every bounded cosilting complex is pure injective. A bounded complex of injective modules is a cosilting object in the derived category if and only if it is a cosilting complex.
returned_results.name: Proposition 6.8

returned_results.slogan: Under the assumptions and notation of the main theorem, there is an equality of localizing subcategories. The left side is generated by the stable derived category of complexes of injective modules with compact cohomology, modulo the suspension. The right side is generated by the injective resolution of the ring. These two localizing subcategories are equal.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.4

returned_results.slogan: For a locally finitely presented additive category with set-indexed products and the pure exact structure, the derived category is compactly generated. The bounded derived category of the category of finitely presented objects is equivalent to the subcategory of compact objects in the derived category. This equivalence is induced by the inclusion of finitely presented objects into the original category. The result establishes a connection between purity and compact generation in derived categories.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.4

returned_results.slogan: Assuming the category has enough injectives and coproducts of injectives are injective, the homotopy category of complexes of injectives with certain conditions is equivalent to the derived category with matching conditions.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.6 (\cite [Corollary~2.25]{bdfik})

returned_results.slogan: For a ring R, the derived category of bounded pure complexes is triangle-equivalent to the homotopy category of bounded above complexes with pure-projective components. It is also triangle-equivalent to the homotopy category of bounded below complexes with pure-injective components. These equivalences hold for the specified categories of complexes.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.6

returned_results.slogan: A bounded below complex of pure injective modules is K-pure injective.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.4

returned_results.slogan: In a locally finitely presented Grothendieck category, the class of pure-injective objects forms an injective class where the monomorphisms are exactly the pure monomorphisms. The category satisfies a certain homological condition relative to this injective class, leading to a model structure on its chain complex category. The associated homotopy category is locally small. This homotopy category is equivalent to the pure derived category for module categories.
returned_results.name: Proposition 8.12

returned_results.slogan: A left and right noetherian ring with a dualizing complex has finite finitistic projective dimension if the localizing subcategory generated by injective modules equals the entire derived category.
returned_results.name: Corollary 5.3

returned_results.slogan: If a category has enough injective and projective objects, then localizing by quasi-isomorphisms gives an equivalence between the homotopy category of bounded below complexes of injectives and the derived category of bounded below complexes. Similarly, it gives an equivalence between the homotopy category of bounded above complexes of projectives and the derived category of bounded above complexes. Furthermore, for two complexes in the homotopy category, if one is a bounded below complex of injectives or the other is a bounded above complex of projectives, then the natural map between hom sets in the homotopy and derived categories is an isomorphism.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.1.2

trajectory.query: faithfully flat homomorphism projective dimension at most 1 Loc(S)=D(R) proposition 4.2

returned_results.slogan: For a local homomorphism from R to S and a homologically finite complex X of S-modules, the projective dimension relative to the homomorphism equals the sum of the flat dimension over R and the depth over R, minus the depth over S.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.5

returned_results.slogan: A ring homomorphism making the codomain a faithfully flat module implies that a module has finite projective dimension over the original ring if and only if its extension does over the codomain. If the homomorphism makes the codomain a finitely generated projective module, then a module having finite projective dimension over the codomain implies its restriction has finite projective dimension over the original ring. When the homomorphism is an isomorphism and the codomain is faithfully flat, the converse also holds. These results relate the finite projective dimension properties of modules under extension and restriction of scalars.
returned_results.name: Proposition 5.3.6

returned_results.slogan: A faithfully flat map between commutative DG-rings preserves projective dimension. If a DG-module has finite projective dimension over the source ring, then its derived tensor product with the target ring has the same projective dimension. This equality holds under the given conditions.

returned_results.slogan: If A is a unital C-star algebra with property SI and a non-empty trace space, then the central sequence algebra F(A) has no characters exactly when the quotient of F(A) by its intersection with the trace-kernel ideal has no characters.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.19

returned_results.slogan: A simple AH-algebra with variation mean dimension zero has strict comparison of positive elements. This property implies that the algebra is classifiable.
returned_results.name: Theorem 8.5

returned_results.slogan: A unital simple AH algebra with strict comparison is Z-stable.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2.2

returned_results.slogan: A unital separable C-star algebra has the strong Corona Factorization Property if its central sequence algebra contains no characters.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.3

returned_results.slogan: Two Villadsen algebras built from a K-contractible finite-dimensional metrizable compact space are isomorphic if and only if their K-zero groups are isomorphic, their tracial state spaces are homeomorphic, and their radius of comparison values are equal. If the radius of comparison is nonzero, the tracial state space condition becomes redundant. In that case, isomorphism holds precisely when the K-zero groups are isomorphic and the radius of comparison values are equal.
returned_results.name: Corollary 7.9

returned_results.slogan: Two Villadsen algebras built on the same finite-dimensional, K-contractible, metrizable compact space are isomorphic if and only if their K-zero groups are isomorphic, their tracial state spaces are homeomorphic, and their radius of comparison values are equal. If the radius of comparison is nonzero, the tracial state space condition becomes redundant. In that case, isomorphism holds precisely when the K-zero groups are isomorphic and the radius of comparison values are equal.
returned_results.name: Theorem 7.1

returned_results.slogan: A simple separable unital amenable C-star algebra without a tracial state has strict comparison if and only if it is isomorphic to its tensor product with the Jiang-Su algebra.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.2

returned_results.slogan: A simple C-star algebra with property TAD has strict comparison for positive elements or is purely infinite.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.2

trajectory.query: unital separable C-star algebra Z-stable iff central sequence algebra F(A) has no characters embedding Jiang-Su into F(A)

returned_results.slogan: A unital separable C-star algebra A is isomorphic to the tensor product of A with the Jiang-Su algebra if and only if there is a unital embedding of the Jiang-Su algebra into the central sequence algebra of A. This is also equivalent to the central sequence algebra of A containing a unital separable subhomogeneous C-star algebra that has no characters. These three conditions are equivalent for such algebras.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.5

returned_results.slogan: A unital, separable C-star algebra is Z-stable if and only if the Jiang-Su algebra embeds into its central sequence algebra. This is also equivalent to the existence of approximately multiplicative, unital, star-linear maps from Z into the algebra. These maps must approximately commute with any finite subset of the algebra. The approximations are made with respect to any given positive tolerance.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.1

returned_results.slogan: A separable C-star algebra A is isomorphic to the tensor product of itself with the Jiang-Su algebra if the central sequence algebra of A contains a unital copy of a subhomogeneous algebra that has no characters.
returned_results.name: Lemma 1.2

returned_results.slogan: A unital, separable, and strongly self-absorbing C-star algebra is Z-stable. This means it is isomorphic to the tensor product of itself with the Jiang-Su algebra. The Jiang-Su algebra is a specific C-star algebra with unique properties. This result establishes a key structural property for such algebras.
returned_results.name: Proposition 8.1.8 (Winter, \cite [Theorem~3.1]{Win11ssaZstable})

returned_results.slogan: A separable C-star algebra A is Z-stable exactly when there is a unital homomorphism from the prime dimension drop algebra I(k, k+1) into the central sequence algebra F(A) for every natural number k.
returned_results.name: Proposition 5.1

returned_results.slogan: A separable and exact C-star algebra that is homotopy equivalent to the Jiang-Su algebra embeds into the central sequence algebra of the Jiang-Su algebra.
returned_results.name: Corollary D

returned_results.slogan: For a unital separable C-star algebra A, three conditions are equivalent. The infinite minimal tensor product of A is isomorphic to itself tensored with the Jiang-Su algebra Z. There exists a unital embedding of Z into the infinite minimal tensor product of A. The infinite minimal tensor product of A contains a unital subhomogeneous C-star algebra that has no characters.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.4 (Dadarlat–Toms)

returned_results.slogan: For a unital separable C-star algebra A, the central sequence algebra F(A) either has a character or lacks any finite-dimensional representation. If it has no finite-dimensional representation, then there exists a unital star-homomorphism from the infinite maximal tensor product of A(n,2) into F(A) for some n greater than or equal to one.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.6

returned_results.slogan: A separable unital C-star algebra with finite nuclear dimension is Z-stable exactly when there exist two full orthogonal elements in its central sequence algebra.
returned_results.name: Theorem F ({\cite[Theorem~ 1.2]{RT17}})

returned_results.slogan: A unital separable projectionless C-star algebra with a unique tracial state and Jiang-Su absorption, having property SI, admits a unital embedding of the Jiang-Su algebra into its central sequence algebra fixed by an automorphism with the weak Rohlin property.
returned_results.name: Lemma 5.5

trajectory.query: simple unital AH algebra strict comparison implies Z-stable theorem

returned_results.slogan: A unital simple AH algebra with strict comparison is Z-stable.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2.2

returned_results.slogan: A unital simple separable nuclear stably finite C-star algebra is Z-stable exactly when it has both strict comparison and uniform property Gamma.
returned_results.name: Theorem 17 ({\cite[Theorem 5.6]{CETW:IMRN}})

returned_results.slogan: A simple separable unital nuclear nonelementary C-star algebra with nonempty tracial state space and finite-dimensional extreme boundary is Z-stable if it has strict comparison.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.7

returned_results.slogan: A simple separable unital nuclear nonelementary C-star algebra with nonempty tracial state space and compact zero-dimensional extreme boundary is Z-stable if it has strict comparison.
returned_results.name: Corollary 3.7

returned_results.slogan: Every Z-stable C-star algebra is pure. Every pure C-star algebra has strict comparison of positive elements.
returned_results.name: Proposition 5.2

returned_results.slogan: A unital simple separable nuclear stably finite C-star algebra with strict comparison and finitely many extremal traces is Z-stable.
returned_results.name: Theorem 7 (Matui–Sato; \cite{MatuiSato:Acta})

returned_results.slogan: A C-star algebra that is Z-stable has an almost unperforated Cuntz semigroup. If such an algebra is also unital, simple, exact, and has at least one trace, then it has strict comparison of positive elements with respect to bounded traces.
returned_results.name: Proposition M ({R\o {}rdam, \cite{Rordam04}})

returned_results.slogan: A sigma-unital and separably Z-stable C*-algebra A implies that the multiplier algebra of A has strict comparison. This means positive elements in the multiplier algebra can be compared using traces. The result holds under these specific conditions on the algebra.
returned_results.name: Corollary 5.2

returned_results.slogan: A unital, amenable, separable, simple C-star algebra with finite weak tracial nuclear dimension is Z-stable under certain conditions. It must have the strict comparison property for positive elements. Additionally, every unital hereditary C-star subalgebra of it must have an m-almost divisible Cuntz semigroup. These properties together imply Z-stability.
returned_results.name: Theorem 8.3

returned_results.slogan: A simple nuclear separable unital infinite-dimensional C*-algebra with non-empty tracial state space is considered. Its tracial state space is affinely homeomorphic to that of an RSH algebra of finite topological dimension. The algebra is Z-stable if and only if it has strict comparison. These two properties are equivalent under the given conditions.
returned_results.name: Proposition 6.9

trajectory.query: weighted Cheeger-Gromoll splitting theorem for Ric_f^1 nonnegative bounded f warped product over R
stable f-minimal hypersurface three-manifold Ric_f^1 nonnegative totally umbilic Ric_f^1(nu,nu)=0

returned_results.slogan: A closed oriented stable f-minimal hypersurface in a complete Riemannian manifold with nonnegative Bakry-Émery Ricci curvature is totally geodesic and satisfies Ric_f(n, n) equals zero. If the hypersurface is also weighted f-area-minimizing in its homology class, the ambient manifold is isometric to a quotient of the hypersurface cross the real line. In three dimensions, such a hypersurface is topologically either a sphere or a torus. When the hypersurface is a torus, the three-dimensional manifold is flat.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1

returned_results.slogan: A complete weighted Riemannian manifold with nonnegative Bakry-Émery Ricci curvature contains an f-parabolic, complete, f-minimal hypersurface. If the Ricci curvature is strictly positive, the hypersurface cannot be L_f-stable. If the Ricci curvature is zero and the hypersurface is L_f-stable, it must be totally geodesic. In that case, the normal component of the Bakry-Émery Ricci curvature also vanishes.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.7

returned_results.slogan: A compact f-minimal hypersurface in a complete weighted Riemannian manifold with f-Bakry-Émery Ricci curvature at least k cannot be Lf-stable if k is positive. If k is zero and the hypersurface is Lf-stable, then it must be totally geodesic. Additionally, the normal component of the f-Bakry-Émery Ricci curvature must vanish.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.2 (\cite{Fan}, Corollary 1.4, \cite{L}, Theorem 1)

returned_results.slogan: A complete oriented stable minimal surface in a complete 3-manifold with nonnegative Ricci curvature is totally geodesic. The Ricci curvature of the manifold normal to the surface vanishes at all points on the surface.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1

returned_results.slogan: An oriented Riemannian manifold of dimension at least three has scalar curvature at least minus n times n minus one. If a compact orientable hypersurface in this manifold is B-stable and does not admit a metric of positive scalar curvature, then the hypersurface is umbilic. The second fundamental form equals the induced metric. The hypersurface is Ricci flat, and the ambient scalar curvature equals minus n times n minus one along it.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.5

returned_results.slogan: A complete orientable immersed stable f-minimal hypersurface in a weighted manifold satisfies certain curvature conditions. The manifold has nonnegative Bakry-Émery Ricci curvature along the hypersurface. The hypersurface also has quadratic weighted volume growth. These conditions imply the second fundamental form is proportional to the metric and the normal component of the Ricci curvature vanishes.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.1

returned_results.slogan: A smooth, compact, oriented hypersurface immersed in a Riemannian manifold with a density of non-negative Bakry-Emery-Ricci curvature is strongly f-stable if and only if it is totally geodesic. The f-Ricci curvature in the normal direction must vanish on the hypersurface. Additionally, the second fundamental form in the normal direction must vanish along the boundary of the hypersurface. These conditions are both necessary and sufficient for strong f-stability.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.1

returned_results.slogan: A complete noncompact oriented stable f-minimal hypersurface in a complete Riemannian manifold with nonnegative Bakry-Émery Ricci curvature on the hypersurface and quadratic weighted volume growth must be totally geodesic. The Bakry-Émery Ricci curvature in the normal direction also vanishes.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2

returned_results.slogan: A closed immersed f-minimal hypersurface in a specific product manifold has an L_f-index of at least one. The index equals one only when the hypersurface is the canonical sphere cross a point. The manifold is a sphere of a particular radius multiplied by the real line. The function f is defined as t squared over four.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2

returned_results.slogan: A complete Riemannian manifold with nonnegative Ricci curvature contains a totally umbilical closed hypersurface. If the Ricci curvature in the normal direction is zero, then the hypersurface has constant mean curvature.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.6

trajectory.query: Schoen Yau theorem complete noncompact 3-manifold positive scalar curvature contractible or surface through each point

returned_results.slogan: A contractible complete three-manifold with uniformly positive scalar curvature is homeomorphic to three-dimensional Euclidean space.
returned_results.name: Corollary 5.12

returned_results.slogan: A non-compact contractible three-dimensional manifold with a complete Riemannian metric that has uniformly positive scalar curvature outside a compact subset must be homeomorphic to Euclidean three-space.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.6 (\cite [Theorem~4.4]{cwy:taming})

returned_results.slogan: A complete oriented 3-manifold with non-negative scalar curvature contains an oriented complete stable minimal surface. If the surface is compact, it is conformally equivalent to a sphere or a totally geodesic flat torus; positive scalar curvature forces it to be a sphere. If the surface is non-compact, it is conformally equivalent to the complex plane or a cylinder, with the cylinder being flat and totally geodesic. Under positive scalar curvature, a cylinder cannot have finite total curvature, and if the Ricci curvature is non-negative, the finite total curvature assumption is unnecessary.
returned_results.name: Theorem 10.4 (Fischer-Colbrie-Schoen)

returned_results.slogan: A complete contractible three-manifold with positive scalar curvature and trivial fundamental group at infinity is homeomorphic to three-dimensional Euclidean space.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1

returned_results.slogan: A contractible 3-manifold with nonnegative scalar curvature and trivial fundamental group at infinity is homeomorphic to Euclidean 3-space.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.8 (\cite {Wang2})

returned_results.slogan: A three-dimensional manifold with positive scalar curvature contains a complete, stable, immersed minimal surface. If the surface is compact, it is diffeomorphic to a sphere. If the surface is noncompact, it is conformally equivalent to the complex plane. The conformal structure on the complex plane is the standard one.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.14

returned_results.slogan: A complete oriented 3-manifold with non-negative scalar curvature contains an oriented complete stable minimal surface. If this surface is noncompact, conformally a cylinder, and has finite positive part of the total curvature, then the surface is flat and totally geodesic.
returned_results.name: Theorem 6.3

returned_results.slogan: A complete, connected, and contractible Riemannian 3-manifold with nonnegative scalar curvature and bounded geometry is diffeomorphic to Euclidean 3-space.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1

returned_results.slogan: In a complete oriented 3-manifold with nonnegative scalar curvature, any oriented complete stable minimal surface is conformally equivalent to a sphere or a torus if compact. If the surface is noncompact, it is conformally covered by the complex plane.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2 (R. Schoen and D. Fischer-Colbrie)

returned_results.slogan: The space of positive scalar curvature metrics on a closed 3-manifold is either contractible or empty.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.12

trajectory.query: Cheeger Gromoll line splitting weighted manifold nonnegative 1-Bakry-Emery Ricci warped product

returned_results.slogan: A complete weighted manifold with nonnegative one-Bakry-Émery Ricci curvature and bounded above potential function splits isometrically as a warped product over the real line if it contains a line.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.4 (\cite{W2})

returned_results.slogan: A geodesically complete weighted manifold with nonnegative Bakry-Émery Ricci curvature and a bounded weight function must split isometrically as a product with the real line if it contains a line. The manifold is isometric to the product of an n-1 dimensional manifold with the real line. The weight function is constant along the line.
returned_results.name: Lemma 7.1

returned_results.slogan: A connected complete Riemannian manifold with a smooth function bounded above and nonnegative N-Bakry-Émery Ricci curvature splits isometrically as a warped product over the real line if it contains a line. When the parameter N is strictly less than one, the splitting is a standard Riemannian product. The result holds under the given curvature and function conditions.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.7 (\cite{W})

returned_results.slogan: A manifold with a bounded function and nonnegative Bakry-Émery Ricci curvature that contains a line either splits isometrically as a product, or it is diffeomorphic to a product of a manifold with no line and the real line. In the latter case, the metric takes a warped product form with a specific conformal factor. The function on the manifold decomposes as the sum of a radial function and a function on the base. The base manifold in this case does not contain any lines.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.9

returned_results.slogan: A complete Riemannian manifold with dimension greater than one has a closed one-form defined by a function. If the weighted Ricci curvature is nonnegative and the manifold contains a line, then it splits as a warped product. The connection associated with the one-form must be geodesically complete.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.5

returned_results.slogan: An n-dimensional connected complete Riemannian manifold with a smooth function and nonnegative N-Bakry-Emery Ricci curvature splits isometrically as a product of the real line and an (n-1)-dimensional manifold if it contains a line.
returned_results.name: Theorem 6.7 (\cite{FLZ})

returned_results.slogan: A sequence of manifolds with weighted measures converges to a limit space. The manifolds have almost nonnegative Bakry-Emery Ricci curvature and bounded potential functions. If the limit space contains a line, then it splits isometrically. The splitting is a product of the real line and another length space.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.10

returned_results.slogan: A smooth metric measure space with a lower bound on its Bakry-Emery Ricci curvature and a quadratic growth condition on its weight function must split as a product of the real line and another manifold if it contains a line through a compact set. If the complement of that compact set has multiple unbounded components, the space is necessarily isometric to the product of the real line and a compact manifold.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.1

returned_results.slogan: An n-dimensional connected complete Riemannian manifold with a smooth function bounded above and nonnegative infinite Bakry-Émery Ricci curvature splits isometrically as a product of the real line and an (n-1)-dimensional Riemannian manifold if it contains a line.
returned_results.name: Theorem 6.10 (\cite{FLZ})

returned_results.slogan: A complete smooth metric measure space with dimension at least three has a lower bound on its Bakry-Emery Ricci curvature and bounded gradient of the potential function. If the first eigenvalue of the weighted Laplacian attains a specific value, then the manifold is either connected at infinity or splits as a warped product. In the splitting case, the manifold is isometric to the real line times a compact manifold. The warping function is exponential for dimensions four and above, and either exponential or hyperbolic cosine in dimension three.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.3

trajectory.query: three-manifold nonnegative scalar curvature universal cover S^3 or splits over R Schoen Yau Liu

returned_results.slogan: A compact geometric graph manifold with nonnegative scalar curvature has a universal cover that splits isometrically as the product of a three-dimensional manifold and Euclidean space. The three-dimensional part is either a sphere cross the real line or a three-sphere with a geometric graph metric. Alternatively, the entire manifold may be flat. This structure arises from the curvature condition.
returned_results.name: Theorem A

returned_results.slogan: A connected, orientable 3-manifold with a complete metric of uniformly positive scalar curvature and a universal cover of bounded geometry must be a connected sum of spherical manifolds and copies of S2 times S1.
returned_results.name: Corollary 11.3

returned_results.slogan: A complete, connected, orientable 3-manifold with uniformly positive scalar curvature must be homeomorphic to a connected sum of spherical 3-manifolds and copies of S2 cross S1. The connected sum may be finite or infinite. This result characterizes the topological structure of such manifolds.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.2 (\cite {Wang3})

returned_results.slogan: A geometrically formal closed oriented three-manifold with non-negative scalar curvature is diffeomorphic to a connected sum of spherical space forms, S1 times S2, or a flat manifold. Conversely, all such manifolds admit Riemannian metrics that are both geometrically formal and have non-negative scalar curvature.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1

returned_results.slogan: A complete finite volume Riemannian manifold with positive nullity and dimension of the kernel of the curvature tensor equal to n minus 3 everywhere has a universal cover that splits isometrically as the product of a 3-manifold and the real line.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3

returned_results.slogan: A complete orientable Riemannian 3-manifold with uniformly positive scalar curvature decomposes as a connected sum. The sum may be infinite. The components are spherical manifolds and products of the 2-sphere with the circle.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1 ({\cite{Gromov_2023,Wang_2023}})

returned_results.slogan: The Schoen-Yau theorem states that for any asymptotically flat, complete Riemannian three-manifold with nonnegative scalar curvature, the total mass is nonnegative. The total mass equals zero only if the manifold is isometric to Euclidean three-space.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1

returned_results.slogan: An orientable asymptotically Euclidean 3-manifold with nonnegative scalar curvature is diffeomorphic to a connected sum of Euclidean space, spherical space forms, and products of spheres. The decomposition includes finitely many copies of S^3 mod finite groups and finitely many copies of S^2 cross S^1. The overall structure is a connected sum of these pieces with R^3.
returned_results.name: Corollary 7.8

returned_results.slogan: A complete noncompact three-dimensional manifold with nonnegative Ricci curvature is either diffeomorphic to Euclidean three-space. Alternatively, its universal cover is isometric to a Riemannian product of the real line and a complete surface. That surface must have nonnegative sectional curvature.
returned_results.name: Theorem (Liu, \cite{L})

returned_results.slogan: A complete Riemannian manifold in three dimensions with nonnegative scalar curvature that is asymptotically Schwarzschild must have nonnegative total mass. The mass equals zero only if the manifold is isometric to Euclidean three-space. This result is known as the Riemannian positive mass theorem. It was established by Schoen and Yau in 1979 and later by Witten in 1981.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2

trajectory.query: Betti polynomial of a decomposable graph in terms of the Betti polynomial of its indecomposable subgraphs Herzog Rinaldo Proposition 3

returned_results.slogan: The bigraded Betti numbers of the binomial edge ideal of a decomposable graph equal the product of the bigraded Betti numbers of the ideals of its decomposable parts.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.4

returned_results.slogan: The multigraded Betti numbers of the edge ring of a decomposable graph equal the product of the multigraded Betti numbers of the edge rings of its decomposition parts. This holds when the graph is expressed as the union of two subgraphs. The formula applies to the Rees algebra of the graph's edge ideal. The result is multiplicative across the decomposition.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.4 ({\cite[Proposition 3]{herzog_extremal_2018}})

returned_results.slogan: For a decomposable graph G equal to the union of G1 and G2, let S1 and S2 be the polynomial rings over the vertex sets of G1 and G2. The bigraded Betti numbers of the quotient ring S over JG equal the product of the bigraded Betti numbers of S1 over JG1 and S2 over JG2.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.5

returned_results.slogan: For a decomposable graph G with decomposition into subgraphs G1 and G2, the bigraded Betti numbers of the graph's binomial edge ideal are multiplicative. The bigraded Betti numbers of G equal the product of the bigraded Betti numbers of G1 and G2. This holds under the given decomposition.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.3

returned_results.slogan: The k-th Betti number of the independence complex of a disjoint graph union equals a sum of products of Betti numbers from the independence complexes of the component graphs. The indices in the sum satisfy that their sum is k minus one. This holds for all integers k greater than or equal to negative one.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4

returned_results.slogan: Each indecomposable graph in the decomposition of a block graph is also a block graph. An extremal Betti number of the graph's binomial edge ideal occurs in a specific homological degree and graded component. This Betti number equals the product of one less than the number of free vertices of each indecomposable graph.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2.3

returned_results.slogan: The polynomial of the edge ideal for a graph equals the product of the polynomials of the edge ideals for its connected components.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.3

returned_results.slogan: The h-star polynomial of the edge polytope of a graph equals the product of the h-star polynomials of the edge polytopes of its connected components.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.1

returned_results.slogan: A graph splits into two induced subgraphs along an edge. If one subgraph is bipartite, then the bigraded Betti numbers of the edge ring of the full graph are determined by those of the subgraphs. Specifically, each Betti number equals the sum over all pairs of indices that add to the original indices. This holds for all nonnegative integer indices.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.11

returned_results.slogan: The subgraph polynomial of a disjoint union of two graphs equals the product of their individual subgraph polynomials. If a graph has multiple connected components, its subgraph polynomial is the product of the polynomials of each component. This multiplicative property holds for the subgraph polynomial over disjoint parts. The result applies to any graph composed of separate, unconnected subgraphs.
returned_results.name: Theorem 12 (Multiplicativity)

trajectory.query: binomial edge ideal decomposable graph Betti polynomial product formula

returned_results.slogan: The bigraded Betti numbers of the binomial edge ideal of a decomposable graph equal the product of the bigraded Betti numbers of the ideals of its decomposable parts.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.4

returned_results.slogan: For a decomposable graph G with decomposition into subgraphs G1 and G2, the bigraded Betti numbers of the graph's binomial edge ideal are multiplicative. The bigraded Betti numbers of G equal the product of the bigraded Betti numbers of G1 and G2. This holds under the given decomposition.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.3

returned_results.slogan: The multigraded Betti numbers of the edge ring of a decomposable graph equal the product of the multigraded Betti numbers of the edge rings of its decomposition parts. This holds when the graph is expressed as the union of two subgraphs. The formula applies to the Rees algebra of the graph's edge ideal. The result is multiplicative across the decomposition.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.4 ({\cite[Proposition 3]{herzog_extremal_2018}})

returned_results.slogan: For a decomposable graph G equal to the union of G1 and G2, let S1 and S2 be the polynomial rings over the vertex sets of G1 and G2. The bigraded Betti numbers of the quotient ring S over JG equal the product of the bigraded Betti numbers of S1 over JG1 and S2 over JG2.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.5

returned_results.slogan: The polynomial of the edge ideal for a graph equals the product of the polynomials of the edge ideals for its connected components.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.3

returned_results.slogan: The Cohen-Macaulay type of the binomial edge ideal of a disjoint union of two connected graphs is the product of the Cohen-Macaulay types of the ideals of the individual graphs. The Betti numbers of the binomial edge ideal of the disjoint union are also the product of the Betti numbers of the ideals of the individual graphs. This holds when each graph has a Cohen-Macaulay binomial edge ideal.
returned_results.name: Lemma 1.3

returned_results.slogan: Given a graph G with a splitting edge e from u to v, where the neighborhood of u is contained in that of v, the Betti numbers of the intersection of ideals J and K decompose as a sum. This sum involves binomial coefficients and Betti numbers of the edge ideal of a subgraph H. The subgraph H is obtained by removing vertices u, v, and all neighbors of v except itself. The formula relates the Betti numbers across different indices and gradings.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.5

returned_results.slogan: Each indecomposable graph in the decomposition of a block graph is also a block graph. An extremal Betti number of the graph's binomial edge ideal occurs in a specific homological degree and graded component. This Betti number equals the product of one less than the number of free vertices of each indecomposable graph.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2.3

returned_results.slogan: If an edge connects a pendant vertex to another vertex, the ideal of the graph equals the sum of the ideal of the graph without that edge and the ideal generated by a certain polynomial. This decomposition is a complete Betti splitting. The Betti numbers of the graph's ideal can be expressed in terms of those of the graph with the edge removed and a related graph. Specifically, each Betti number equals the sum of a Betti number from the smaller graph and a shifted Betti number from the other graph.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.2

returned_results.slogan: For a graph's binomial edge ideal decomposed via an s-partition, the Betti numbers satisfy a splitting formula when the index i is at least the size of the largest clique containing s, or when j is at least i plus four. This formula expresses the Betti numbers of the whole ideal in terms of those of the parts and their intersection. The decomposition is called a (c(s), 4)-Betti splitting.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.3 (\Cref{maintheo2})

trajectory.query: level Cohen-Macaulay ring characterized by unique extremal Betti number type

returned_results.slogan: The Cohen-Macaulay type of the ring modulo the ideal determines all its Betti numbers. This holds under the same conditions as the referenced theorem. The Betti numbers are completely fixed by this invariant.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.8

returned_results.slogan: In a Cohen-Macaulay ring S/I, the type equals the final Betti number in the minimal free resolution of S/I as an S-module.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.7

returned_results.slogan: A ring is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if two specific sets of Betti numbers are equal. It is also equivalent to the equality of two sets of Bass numbers for all indices in a certain set. These three conditions are all equivalent to each other.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.10

returned_results.slogan: For a polynomial ring over a field with a monomial ideal such that the quotient ring is Cohen-Macaulay, all multigraded extremal Betti numbers occur at the projective dimension. The index of these Betti numbers equals the projective dimension of the quotient ring.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.10

returned_results.slogan: A Cohen-Macaulay semi-standard graded ring with a given h-vector is level if and only if a specific graded Betti number vanishes. The h-vector has three entries, and the first entry minus the dimension is positive. The condition depends on the Betti number in a particular homological degree. This holds when that Betti number is zero.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.2

returned_results.slogan: In a Cohen-Macaulay ring S/I, the type equals the last Betti number in the minimal free resolution of S/I as an S-module. This Betti number is the final nonzero term in the resolution. The result connects the ring's type to its homological invariants.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.1

returned_results.slogan: A nonzero Cohen-Macaulay module over a ring implies the ring is also Cohen-Macaulay, and the module has finite projective dimension under certain vanishing Ext conditions. These conditions depend on the multiplicity and minimal number of generators of the module. The vanishing of Ext modules is required over specific ranges of indices. The ranges are defined in terms of the dimensions of the ring and module, along with Betti numbers.
returned_results.name: Theorem 6.1

returned_results.slogan: A local Cohen-Macaulay ring with minimal multiplicity is strongly homologically of minimal multiplicity. Its type is given by the pair one and the multiplicity of the ring minus one.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.6

returned_results.slogan: A complete equicharacteristic Cohen-Macaulay local ring with an algebraically closed residue field has finite maximal Cohen-Macaulay type if and only if it has bounded maximal Cohen-Macaulay type and is an isolated singularity or regular. Bounded type means the Betti numbers or multiplicities of nonisomorphic indecomposable maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules are bounded. The ring must also be an isolated singularity or regular. These conditions together characterize when there are only finitely many such modules.
returned_results.name: Corollary 5.13

returned_results.slogan: A nonzero finitely generated graded module is Cohen-Macaulay exactly when its local cohomology modules vanish in all degrees except one. The exceptional degree is the Cohen-Macaulay type of the module. This characterizes the Cohen-Macaulay property via local cohomology.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.2.1

returned_results.slogan: R is Gorenstein if and only if there exists a nonzero Cohen-Macaulay module M of finite G-dimension g. The type of M is less than or equal to the minimal number of generators of the g-th Ext module of M and R. In particular, this condition holds if the type of M is one.
returned_results.name: Corollary \ref{cor:Gor-iff-there-is-CM-G-dim-finite-mod}

returned_results.slogan: Assume R is Cohen-Macaulay, and M is an R-module with depth r and dimension s. If the homological dimension of Ext from i equals t minus s to t minus r is finite, then the homological dimension of M is finite. The dimension of Ext to the i-th power of M and R is at most t minus i for all i not equal to t minus s, and equals s when i is t minus s. The type of M equals the minimal number of generators of Ext to the t minus r-th power of M and R times the type of R. If M has type one, then R is Gorenstein.
returned_results.name: Corollary 5.11

returned_results.slogan: In a Cohen-Macaulay ring S/I, the type equals the last Betti number in the minimal free resolution of S/I as an S-module. This Betti number is the final nonzero term in the resolution. The result connects the ring's type to its homological invariants.

returned_results.slogan: In a Cohen-Macaulay ring S/I, the type equals the final Betti number in the minimal free resolution of S/I as an S-module.

returned_results.slogan: A ring is Gorenstein if and only if it has a nonzero Cohen-Macaulay module of finite G-dimension whose type is at most the minimal number of generators of its top Ext module. This is equivalent to the ring being Cohen-Macaulay and possessing a G-perfect module of some G-dimension satisfying the same type inequality. The condition holds, for example, when the module has type one.
returned_results.name: Corollary 3.10

returned_results.slogan: A Cohen-Macaulay ring with a canonical module is Gorenstein if the first Betti number of the canonical module is at most the zeroth Betti number.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.2

returned_results.slogan: A Noetherian local ring R is Gorenstein if there exists a Cohen-Macaulay module M with dimension equal to the depth of R, satisfying an inequality involving multiplicities and type, and vanishing Ext modules in a certain range. If a Cohen-Macaulay module C of dimension n satisfies an inequality with its type and multiplicity and has vanishing Ext modules in a range, then R is Cohen-Macaulay and C is maximal Cohen-Macaulay with finite injective dimension. When R is Cohen-Macaulay and C is maximal Cohen-Macaulay, C has finite injective dimension if either an inequality between type, multiplicity, and rank holds, or if C has a rank and its type is at most that rank.
returned_results.name: Corollary 1.3 (Corollaries \ref {cor_Gor}, \ref {cor:case_M_is_R}, \ref {cor:rank}, and \ref {cor_M=C})

returned_results.slogan: A nonzero finitely generated graded module is Cohen-Macaulay exactly when its local cohomology modules vanish in all degrees except one. The exceptional degree is the Cohen-Macaulay type of the module. This characterizes the Cohen-Macaulay property via local cohomology.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.2.1

returned_results.slogan: A nonzero Cohen-Macaulay module over a ring implies the ring is also Cohen-Macaulay, and the module has finite projective dimension under certain vanishing Ext conditions. These conditions depend on the multiplicity and minimal number of generators of the module. The vanishing of Ext modules is required over specific ranges of indices. The ranges are defined in terms of the dimensions of the ring and module, along with Betti numbers.

returned_results.slogan: A Noetherian local ring R with depth r is Gorenstein if and only if there exists a Cohen-Macaulay R-module M of dimension r. This module must satisfy an inequality relating the type of R and the multiplicity of M to the multiplicity of its dual. Additionally, all Ext groups from M to R vanish in degrees 1 through r+1.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2.6

trajectory.query: pseudo-Gorenstein Cohen-Macaulay graded ring characterization in terms of extremal Betti number or h-vector

returned_results.slogan: A Cohen-Macaulay generically Gorenstein graded ring R is pseudo-Gorenstein exactly when it is Gorenstein. This holds under two grade conditions. The first requires the grade of a certain component of the canonical module to be positive. The second requires the grade of a component related to the trace of the canonical module to be at least two.

returned_results.slogan: A Cohen-Macaulay standard graded algebra is pseudo-Gorenstein if and only if the top degree component of the quotient by a regular sequence of linear forms has dimension one. This is equivalent to the leading coefficient of the numerator of the Hilbert series being one. It also corresponds to the highest shift in the free resolution occurring in a specific term with multiplicity one. These conditions characterize when the algebra is pseudo-Gorenstein.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.3

returned_results.slogan: A Cohen-Macaulay generically Gorenstein graded ring R is pseudo-Gorenstein exactly when it is Gorenstein, provided two grade conditions hold. The second condition requires the grade of a component of the trace of the canonical module to be at least two. These conditions together ensure the equivalence between pseudo-Gorenstein and Gorenstein properties.

returned_results.slogan: A pseudo-Cohen-Macaulay local ring is pseudo-Gorenstein exactly when it is c-Gorenstein. For such a ring with geometric dimension d and residue field k, being pseudo-Gorenstein implies that Ext^i(k,R) is zero for all i not equal to d, and Ext^d(k,R) is isomorphic to k. Conversely, if Ext^i(k,R) vanishes for some i greater than d, or if Ext^d(k,R) is isomorphic to k, then the ring is pseudo-Gorenstein.
returned_results.name: Proposition 7.27

returned_results.slogan: A Cohen-Macaulay semi-standard graded ring with a given h-vector is level if and only if a specific graded Betti number vanishes.
