trajectory.query: Jordan's theorem finite subgroup of GL_n has abelian normal subgroup of bounded index depending only on n

returned_results.slogan: The general linear group of n by n real invertible matrices is Jordan. This means every subgroup has a normal abelian subgroup of bounded index. The bound depends only on the dimension n.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.8

returned_results.slogan: Jordan's theorem states that every finite subgroup of complex invertible n by n matrices has an abelian normal subgroup whose index is bounded by a function j(n). This function j(n) depends only on the dimension n. For n at least 71, j(n) is at most (n+1) factorial.
returned_results.name: Theorem 13 (Jordan function)

returned_results.slogan: Every finite subgroup of complex invertible matrices of size n has an abelian normal subgroup whose index is bounded by a function j that depends only on n. The function j maps natural numbers to natural numbers. This bound is uniform across all finite subgroups of a given dimension.
returned_results.name: Theorem (Jordan 1878)

returned_results.slogan: For every positive integer n, there exists a constant J(n) such that any finite subgroup of the general linear group of dimension n over a field of characteristic zero has an abelian normal subgroup whose index is at most J(n).
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.4.3

returned_results.slogan: For any positive integer n, there is a constant J(n) such that every finite subgroup of the general linear group of degree n over a field of characteristic zero has a normal abelian subgroup. The index of this abelian subgroup is at most J(n). The constant J(n) depends only on n and not on the field or the specific subgroup.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1 ({cf.~ \cite{Jordan1878}})

returned_results.slogan: Jordan's lemma states that every finite subgroup of complex n by n matrices has an abelian normal subgroup whose index is bounded by a function of n. For n greater than 63, this bound is (n+2) factorial, and for n less than or equal to 63, it is n to the fourth times (n+2) factorial. If a finite group of automorphisms of an n-dimensional complex manifold fixes a smooth point, it also has an abelian normal subgroup with index at most that bound. The same index bound applies when the manifold is projective and of general type, and the group fixes a smooth point.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.7

returned_results.slogan: For any positive integer n, there is a constant J(n) such that for every prime p and field of characteristic p, every finite subgroup of GL_n(k) has a normal abelian subgroup. The order of this subgroup is coprime to p, and its index is at most J(n) times the cube of the size of a p-Sylow subgroup. This implies that GL_n(k) is p-Jordan for every field of positive characteristic.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.4 ({\cite{BrauerFeit}, \cite[Theorem~ 0.4]{LarsenPink}})

returned_results.slogan: There exists a constant depending only on n such that every finite subgroup of complex n by n invertible matrices has a normal abelian subgroup whose index is bounded by that constant.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.38

returned_results.slogan: For every positive integer n and every field, any finite subgroup of automorphisms of an n-dimensional abelian variety over that field has a normal abelian subgroup with bounded index. This subgroup can be generated by at most 2n elements. The bound depends only on n. Consequently, the automorphism group of any abelian variety is Jordan.
returned_results.name: Corollary 6.3

returned_results.slogan: For any positive integer n, there exists a constant b_n depending only on n. Every finite subgroup of the complex general linear group of dimension n has an abelian normal subgroup. The index of this subgroup in the original group is at most b_n.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4 ({C. Jordan, \cite{jordan} \cite[Theorem 36.13]{curtis-reiner}})

trajectory.query: connected component finite index bounded by number of connected components algebraic subgroup GL_n completely reducible representation Jordan theorem

returned_results.slogan: For a group with finite abelianization, there exists a finite set of algebraic subgroups in the general linear group. For any completely reducible representation, the Zariski closure of its image is conjugate to one of these subgroups. Each subgroup in this collection has a connected component that is semisimple. This holds over any algebraically closed field.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.1

returned_results.slogan: Every n-dimensional algebraic group over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero is Jordan. The group has a Jordan constant bounded by a function of its dimension and the index of its identity component. The bound depends on the dimension n and the number of connected components. The inequality involves the Jordan constant of the general linear group of a related dimension.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4

returned_results.slogan: For groups with property (FAb), every completely reducible representation into GL_n(K) has a Zariski closure that is conjugate to one of finitely many algebraic subgroups. These subgroups are indexed and depend on the dimension n. The connected component of each such subgroup is semisimple. This holds for all n at least 1.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.5

returned_results.slogan: For a group with property FAb and any positive integer n, there exists a finite set of algebraic subgroups of GL_n(K). The Zariski closure of the image of any completely reducible representation from the group to GL_n(K) is conjugate to one of these subgroups. Each subgroup in the collection has a connected component that is semisimple.
returned_results.name: Proposition 6.2.1

returned_results.slogan: For every positive integer n, there exists a constant J(n) such that any closed reductive subgroup H of GL_n has an open subgroup H' with index at most J(n). This subgroup H' equals the product of its center and the commutator subgroup of its identity component.
returned_results.name: Proposition 5.2

returned_results.slogan: For all positive integers n, there exists a constant J(n). Every closed reductive subgroup H of GL_n has an open subgroup H' with index at most J(n). This subgroup H' equals the product of its center and the commutator subgroup of the identity component of H.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.4

returned_results.slogan: A connected reductive linear algebraic group with derived subgroup dimension at most n has a Jordan constant bounded by a function S of n.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.4

returned_results.slogan: The general linear group of n by n real invertible matrices is Jordan. This means every subgroup has a normal abelian subgroup of bounded index. The bound depends only on the dimension n.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.8

returned_results.slogan: Every finite subgroup of a connected affine algebraic subgroup of the birational automorphism group of an irreducible variety of dimension n has a normal abelian subgroup. The index of this subgroup in the original group is bounded by a constant that depends only on n. The constant is denoted as J sub less than or equal to n.
returned_results.name: Theorem 15

returned_results.slogan: For any connected reductive group of rank n over a field, every finite subgroup of its rational points contains a subgroup of bounded index. This subgroup lies within the rational points of a torus defined over the same field. The bound depends only on the rank n.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.11

trajectory.query: finite subgroup of reductive algebraic group bounded component group index representation dimension n

returned_results.slogan: For any connected reductive group of rank n over a field, every finite subgroup of its rational points contains a subgroup of bounded index. This subgroup lies within the rational points of a torus defined over the same field. The bound depends only on the rank n.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.11

returned_results.slogan: For every group and subgroup of finite index, the sum over irreducible representations of the dimension times the rank of the subgroup's image equals the index.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.1 (\cite{dfps21})

returned_results.slogan: For a reductive group G, there is a constant f_G at least 1 such that every finite subgroup of G has an abelian normal subgroup contained in a torus of the identity component. The index of this subgroup in the finite subgroup is bounded by f_G.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.2

returned_results.slogan: The index of a subgroup in a finite group equals the sum over irreducible representations of the product of the representation's dimension and the dimension of its fixed subspace under the subgroup.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.8

returned_results.slogan: A connected algebraic group G with a bounded derived subgroup dimension has a finite subgroup H. There exists a subgroup H1 of H with bounded index relative to n. The derived subgroup of H1 lies in the center of G. The order of this derived subgroup is at most n to the power n.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.7

returned_results.slogan: Given a finite field and a reductive group over it, a subgroup of small index relative to the field's characteristic that intersects every geometric component is considered. For a representation of the group over the algebraic closure, if the group's dimension and certain norms of the representation are small relative to the characteristic, then the invariant subspace under the group equals that under the subgroup.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.6

returned_results.slogan: A connected algebraic group has dimensions for its reductive and abelian parts bounded by given values. For any finite subgroup whose commutator lies in the center, the finite rank of the quotient by that commutator is at most twice the abelian dimension plus the reductive dimension plus a function of the reductive dimension.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.8

returned_results.slogan: The index of a subgroup in a finite group equals the sum over all irreducible complex representations of the group of the product of the representation's dimension and the dimension of its fixed subspace under the subgroup.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.5

returned_results.slogan: For any reductive group G and finite subgroup Γ of G, there exists a constant f_G at least 1. This constant depends only on G. For every finite subgroup Γ, there is an abelian normal subgroup A of Γ contained in a torus of the identity component of G. The index of A in Γ is bounded by f_G.
returned_results.name: Theorem A.1

returned_results.slogan: For a closed normal subgroup N of G with reductive quotient G/N, the representation dimension of G with respect to any module V is bounded by the product of the representation dimension of N with respect to V and the representation dimension of G/N. This inequality also holds when replacing the module-specific dimension of N with its global representation dimension. Consequently, the global representation dimension of G is at most the product of the global representation dimensions of N and G/N.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.3

trajectory.query: for every closed reductive subgroup H of GL_n there exists open subgroup H' of bounded index equal Z(H^0)[H^0,H^0]

returned_results.slogan: For every positive integer n, there exists a constant J(n) such that any closed reductive subgroup H of GL_n has an open subgroup H' with index at most J(n). This subgroup H' equals the product of its center and the commutator subgroup of its identity component.
returned_results.name: Proposition 5.2

returned_results.slogan: For all positive integers n, there exists a constant J(n). Every closed reductive subgroup H of GL_n has an open subgroup H' with index at most J(n). This subgroup H' equals the product of its center and the commutator subgroup of the identity component of H.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.4

returned_results.slogan: Given an open subgroup H of GL(Zhat) with level n and a subgroup G of GL(Zhat), the H-closure of G is an open subgroup whose level divides n. Consequently, there are only finitely many H-closed subgroups in GL(Zhat).
returned_results.name: Corollary

returned_results.slogan: Let H be a subgroup of GL of Z-hat such that the determinant of H intersected with the kernel of pi_m equals 1 plus m times Z-hat for all m at least 1. Let G be a subgroup of GL of Z-hat with SL-level n. Then the H-closure of G is an open subgroup with GL-level dividing n.
returned_results.name: Lemma

returned_results.slogan: For a finitely generated subgroup H of GLn(Z), let H be its Zariski closure in GLn,Z. If the complex points of H have a finite fundamental group, then the adelic closure of H is open in the adelic closure of the integer points of H.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.2.3 (\cite{weis}, \cite{Nori})

returned_results.slogan: For an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and a connected reductive algebraic group H in GL_n, there exists an element g in GL_n such that conjugating H by g results in a subgroup defined over the rational numbers.
returned_results.name: Corollary A.18

returned_results.slogan: For every positive integer n, there exist constants A_n, B_n, and C_n such that for primes p greater than A_n, if a closed subgroup of GL_n over the p-adic integers has Zariski closure G, then its normal dimension is at most the dimension of G. If equality holds, the subgroup is open in the rational points of G. The component group of G has prime-to-p order and a bounded-index normal abelian subgroup. If the radical of the identity component is unipotent, the index of the subgroup in the integral points of G is bounded by C_n.
returned_results.name: Theorem 7

returned_results.slogan: Let H be a subgroup of the general linear group over the integers. Suppose the identity component of the rational points of the Zariski closure of H is semisimple. Then for any prime p, the closure of H in the p-adic points of that closure is open.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.2.1

returned_results.slogan: A connected algebraic group G with a bounded derived subgroup dimension has a finite subgroup H. There exists a subgroup H1 of H with bounded index relative to n. The derived subgroup of H1 lies in the center of G. The order of this derived subgroup is at most n to the power n.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.7

returned_results.slogan: A subgroup H of GL_r(K) either has a bounded index subgroup contained in M_1Z, where M_1 is isomorphic to one of several types of matrix groups, or H lies between an almost quasi-simple group and its central extension. The possible types for M_1 include a unipotent radical of a parabolic subgroup, a general linear group over an extension field, a central product of two general linear groups, or a general linear group over a subfield. The index of the subgroup H_0 in H is bounded by a constant depending only on r.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.1

trajectory.query: property FAb completely reducible representation Zariski closure one of finitely many algebraic subgroups GL_n semisimple identity component

returned_results.slogan: For groups with property (FAb), every completely reducible representation into GL_n(K) has a Zariski closure that is conjugate to one of finitely many algebraic subgroups. These subgroups are indexed and depend on the dimension n. The connected component of each such subgroup is semisimple. This holds for all n at least 1.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.5

returned_results.slogan: For a group with property FAb and any positive integer n, there exists a finite set of algebraic subgroups of GL_n(K). The Zariski closure of the image of any completely reducible representation from the group to GL_n(K) is conjugate to one of these subgroups. Each subgroup in the collection has a connected component that is semisimple.
returned_results.name: Proposition 6.2.1

returned_results.slogan: If a group has the FAb property, then for any dimension n, there exists a finite index subgroup such that the Zariski closure of its image under any n-dimensional complex representation is connected. If the representation is irreducible, this closure is also semisimple.
returned_results.name: Proposition .3

returned_results.slogan: For a group with finite abelianization, there exists a finite set of algebraic subgroups in the general linear group. For any completely reducible representation, the Zariski closure of its image is conjugate to one of these subgroups. Each subgroup in this collection has a connected component that is semisimple. This holds over any algebraically closed field.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.1

returned_results.slogan: A subgroup H of G is completely reducible if and only if its Zariski closure in G is a reductive group. Similarly, a representation rho from Gamma to G_k is completely reducible if and only if the Zariski closure of the image of rho is a reductive group in G_k.
returned_results.name: Proposition A.3

returned_results.slogan: A closed algebraic subgroup of the general linear group over a finite-dimensional vector space has a reductive identity component if the representation is semisimple and the endomorphism algebra is separable.
returned_results.name: Proposition 7.6

returned_results.slogan: For a simple algebraic group over the complex numbers, there exist two finite-dimensional irreducible representations. The Zariski closure of the subgroup generated by any finite set of group elements equals the full group if and only if both representations remain irreducible when restricted to that subgroup.
returned_results.name: Lemma 5.19

returned_results.slogan: If a group has property FA for dimension n minus one, then there are only finitely many conjugacy classes of irreducible representations into the general linear group of dimension n over any algebraically closed field.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.8 (Finiteness of the character variety)

returned_results.slogan: Let V be a finite-dimensional vector space over a field F, and let G be a closed algebraic subgroup of the general linear group on V. If V is semisimple as a representation of G, and the algebra of G-equivariant endomorphisms of V is separable over F, then the identity component of G is a reductive algebraic group.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.2.1

returned_results.slogan: A reductive linear differential algebraic group with a faithful representation of minimal dimension has a completely reducible representation. The Zariski closure of the image of this representation is a reductive linear algebraic group. This reductive linear algebraic group is unique up to algebraic isomorphism. The result does not depend on the choice of the minimal faithful representation.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.7

trajectory.query: isolated hypersurface singularity k-Du Bois smooth if k > (n-1)/2 spectrum bound ordinary double point

returned_results.slogan: An isolated hypersurface singularity of dimension n has an invariant bounded by (n+1)/2. This bound is achieved exactly when the singularity is an ordinary double point. For odd dimensions, no such singularity can be k-rational. The singularity is k-Du Bois or k-liminal only if it is an ordinary double point.
returned_results.name: Corollary 6.12

returned_results.slogan: An isolated locally complete intersection singularity is k-Du Bois if and only if the Steenbrink spectrum numbers vanish for all indices less than or equal to k. This holds for the Milnor fiber of the singularity. The condition characterizes the singularity's Du Bois property in terms of its spectral invariants.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.1

returned_results.name: Theorem

returned_results.slogan: An anti-self-dual manifold with vanishing compactly supported cohomology in degrees zero and two has a moduli space of nearby anti-self-dual conformal structures. This moduli space is a smooth finite-dimensional manifold. Its dimension equals the dimension of the first compactly supported cohomology group.
returned_results.name: Corollary

returned_results.slogan: Suppose a four-dimensional manifold has an anti-self-dual metric with vanishing anti-self-dual harmonic zero-forms and two-forms. Then the moduli space of nearby anti-self-dual conformal structures forms a smooth, finite-dimensional manifold. Its dimension equals the dimension of the space of anti-self-dual harmonic one-forms.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.2

returned_results.slogan: The moduli space of anti-self-dual connections on a principal bundle with a compact semisimple structure group over a four-dimensional compact Riemannian manifold has a finite-dimensional Kuranishi chart at every point. The virtual dimension of this moduli space is determined by a formula involving the first Pontryagin class of the adjoint bundle. It also depends on the Euler characteristic and signature of the base manifold multiplied by the dimension of the structure group. The expression is two times the first Pontryagin class minus half the difference of the Euler characteristic and signature times the dimension of the group.
returned_results.name: Theorem

returned_results.slogan: On a compact oriented Riemannian four-manifold with a complex vector bundle having zero first Chern class, certain hypotheses are satisfied. This implies the set of one-forms satisfying specific curvature and co-closed conditions forms a Kuranishi space at an anti-self-dual connection. If the connection is irreducible, additional hypotheses hold. Then the local moduli space is described by the given equation.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.7

returned_results.slogan: The formal dimension of the moduli space of anti-self-dual bifold connections with action kappa on the pair S4 and Psi n equals 8 kappa minus the square of 1 minus n over 2. For Psi 0, the dimension is 8 kappa minus 1. For Psi 1 and Psi 3, the dimension is 8 kappa minus one quarter. For Psi 2, the dimension is exactly 8 kappa.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.1

returned_results.slogan: The formal dimension of the moduli space of anti-self-dual bifold SU(3) connections with action kappa on the pair (S^4, Psi_n) is 12 kappa minus 4 plus 2n minus n squared over 2. For Psi_0, the dimension is 12 kappa minus 4. For Psi_1, it is 12 kappa minus 5/2. For Psi_2, it is 12 kappa minus 2, and for Psi_3, it is 12 kappa minus 5/2.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.6

returned_results.slogan: The local Kuranishi model for the moduli space near a connection with vanishing (0,2)-curvature is given by a projection of a Kuranishi map. This map sends a small ball in the (0,1)-cohomology space to the self-dual part of the (0,2)-cohomology space. The Kuranishi map is defined by the DT4 equations. The projection targets the self-dual subspace of the obstruction space.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.12

returned_results.slogan: Under certain nondegeneracy assumptions, when the homology class is nonzero, the Kuranishi structure on the moduli space of solutions is S1 equivariant. For the zero homology class, the same equivariance property holds on the corresponding moduli space.
returned_results.name: Theorem 29.8

returned_results.slogan: For a closed symplectic manifold with a compatible almost complex structure, genus, number of marked points, and homology class, natural oriented Kuranishi structures of a specified dimension exist on the moduli space of stable maps. Any two such Kuranishi structures are deformation equivalent. If the symplectic structures are isotopic and the almost complex structures are chosen accordingly, the Kuranishi structures on the corresponding moduli spaces are cobordant.
returned_results.name: Theorem 6.5.1

trajectory.query: self-dual deformation complex index moduli space dimension H1 H2 orbifold anti-self-dual metric

returned_results.slogan: The index of the anti-self-dual deformation complex on a compact anti-self-dual orbifold with one orbifold point of type (q,p) is given by a formula. If q is not equal to p minus one, the index equals one-half of fifteen times the topological Euler characteristic plus twenty-nine times the topological signature, plus four times the sum of e_i from i equals one to k, minus twelve k minus two. If q equals p minus one, the index equals one-half of fifteen times the topological Euler characteristic plus twenty-nine times the topological signature, minus four p plus four.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.3

returned_results.slogan: For an anti-self-dual orbifold-cone metric on a four-manifold with singular set and cone angle, the index equals half of fifteen times the Euler characteristic plus twenty-nine times the signature, minus four times the Euler characteristic of the singular set and minus four times its self-intersection number. For a self-dual metric, the index equals half of fifteen times the Euler characteristic minus twenty-nine times the signature, minus four times the Euler characteristic of the singular set and plus four times its self-intersection number.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.3

returned_results.slogan: The index of the anti-self-dual deformation complex for the orbifold conformal compactification of a Calderbank-Singer space depends on the parameters of the action at infinity. If q is not equal to one, the index is five k plus five minus the sum of four times each e_i for i from one to k. If q equals one, the index is negative four p plus twelve. The integers k and e_i are defined by a modified Euclidean algorithm.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.7

returned_results.slogan: The anti-self-dual ALE metric with group Gamma at infinity has an orbifold conformal compactification. For delta between negative two and zero, a relation holds involving weighted cohomology dimensions on the original space and the orbifold's index. The sum of negative dimension of first cohomology, dimension of second cohomology at negative two minus delta, and dimension of zero cohomology on the quotient space equals the index of the compactified orbifold.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.1

returned_results.slogan: The moduli space of anti-self-dual orbifold-cone metrics near a given metric is a smooth manifold under certain conditions. The metric must be anti-self-dual, Ricci-flat, and have a specified cone angle and singular set. There must be no parallel vector fields or parallel sections of a particular tensor bundle. The dimension of this moduli space is given by a formula involving the Euler characteristic and signature of the manifold, as well as the Euler characteristic and self-intersection of the singular set.
returned_results.name: Corollary 1.11

returned_results.slogan: For a compact self-dual orbifold with one orbifold point and orbifold group a non-cyclic finite subgroup of SO(4), the index of the self-dual deformation complex equals half of fifteen times the Euler characteristic minus twenty-nine times the signature, plus a correction term N(Gamma). If Gamma is a subgroup of U(2), then N(Gamma) is negative four times b_Gamma plus a constant from a table. If Gamma is not in U(2), then N(Gamma) is negative N of the conjugate group minus six or seven, depending on whether the conjugate group is in SU(2).
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.6

returned_results.slogan: A compact anti-self-dual orbifold with one orbifold point and a specified orbifold group type has an index given by a formula. The formula depends on the Euler characteristic and signature of the orbifold. It also subtracts four times the parameter n associated with the orbifold group type. The group types include A_n for n at least one, D_n for n at least three, or E_n for n equal to six, seven, or eight.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.6

returned_results.slogan: For a compact anti-self-dual orbifold with one orbifold point, the index depends on the orientation-reversing conjugacy type of the orbifold group. If the group is type A1, the index equals one-half of 15 times the Euler characteristic plus 29 times the signature, minus 4. For type An with n at least 2, the index is that same half-sum plus 4n minus 10. For type D3, it is the half-sum plus 2, and for type Dn with n at least 4 or type En with n 6, 7, or 8, it is the half-sum plus 4n minus 11.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.5

returned_results.slogan: A compact self-dual Kähler orbifold with positive scalar curvature somewhere has trivial second cohomology group when the orientation is reversed. Reversing the orientation makes the metric anti-self-dual. The result holds under the assumption that the set of points with positive scalar curvature is non-empty.
returned_results.name: Proposition 7.9

returned_results.slogan: Suppose a four-dimensional manifold has an anti-self-dual metric with vanishing anti-self-dual harmonic zero-forms and two-forms. Then the moduli space of nearby anti-self-dual conformal structures forms a smooth, finite-dimensional manifold. Its dimension equals the dimension of the space of anti-self-dual harmonic one-forms.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.2

trajectory.query: Calderbank-Singer orbifold conformal compactification anti-self-dual deformations toric deformations theorem

returned_results.slogan: A Calderbank-Singer space with a (q,p)-action at infinity and its orbifold conformal compactification have a moduli space of anti-self-dual conformal structures. For q=1 and p=2, the metric is rigid. For q=1 and p=3, the moduli space has local dimension 1, and for p>3, it has dimension 4p-12. If q=p-1, the dimension is 3p-7, and for 1<q<p-1, it is at least a given expression involving k and e_i. When p>2, these spaces allow non-toric anti-self-dual deformations.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.8

returned_results.slogan: The index of the anti-self-dual deformation complex for the orbifold conformal compactification of a Calderbank-Singer space depends on the parameters of the action at infinity. If q is not equal to one, the index is five k plus five minus the sum of four times each e_i for i from one to k. If q equals one, the index is negative four p plus twelve. The integers k and e_i are defined by a modified Euclidean algorithm.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.7

returned_results.slogan: The deformation theory of anti-self-dual conformal structures on the one-point conformal compactification of an ALE scalar-flat Kähler four-manifold is unobstructed. The linearized self-dual Weyl curvature operator is surjective at the given conformal class. This surjectivity holds for the compact anti-self-dual orbifold structure.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.2

returned_results.slogan: Suppose a compact toric anti-self-dual orbifold contains a surface constructed from specific combinatorial data. Let the orbit space and its ordered set of fixed boundary orbits be given. If a conformal isometry exists between this orbit space and another, mapping corresponding fixed orbits, then the original orbifolds are conformally isometric.
returned_results.name: Lemma 11.2

returned_results.slogan: A compact toric four-dimensional orbifold with positive Euler characteristic that has an invariant anti-self-dual conformal structure is conformally isometric to a specific model orbifold. This model is determined by subsets of a lattice and the boundary of a polyhedron. The result establishes a classification under these geometric conditions.
returned_results.name: Proposition 11.3

returned_results.slogan: Given a compact conformally anti-self-dual orbifold with a point modeled on a quotient of R4 by a finite group action, and given a conformally anti-self-dual WALE space with the same asymptotic model, there exists a smooth map from a neighborhood in certain cohomology groups to another. The zeros of this map correspond to conformally anti-self-dual metrics on the connected sum of the orbifold and the WALE space. This connected sum is formed by joining the asymptotic region of the WALE space to a neighborhood of the point in the orbifold. The deformation cohomology groups used are as defined in referenced theorems.
returned_results.name: Theorem B

returned_results.slogan: For any flat conformal structure on the orbifold formed by connecting two specific four-dimensional sphere quotients, a certain differential operator mapping symmetric trace-free one-forms to self-dual two-forms is surjective. This implies the deformation theory of anti-self-dual conformal structures on that orbifold is unobstructed at that conformal class.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.5

returned_results.slogan: An ALE anti-self-dual 4-manifold with specified asymptotic decay conditions can be compactified into an orbifold by adding a point at each end. This compactified space carries a canonical real-analytic structure. The original conformal class extends to the compactification as a real-analytic anti-self-dual conformal metric.
returned_results.name: Proposition 12

returned_results.slogan: Two compact four-dimensional orbifolds with self-dual conformal structures and vanishing self-dual deformation cohomology can be joined. The connection is made at orbifold points whose local groups are conjugate via an orientation-reversing map. The resulting orbifold connect sum admits a self-dual conformal structure. This construction requires specific algebraic conditions on the orbifold singularities.
returned_results.name: Theorem 8.5 (\cite{DonaldsonFriedman,Floer,LeBrunSinger,KovalevSinger,AcheViaclovsky2})

returned_results.slogan: A compact Einstein orbifold with specific singularities and integrable deformations lies in the Gromov-Hausdorff closure of a manifold formed by gluing. Under conditions involving either a sequence of stable Ricci-flat metrics converging to it or rigidity with one singularity, the selfdual or anti-selfdual curvature at each singular point has a particular form. The curvature matrix has zeros in all entries except the last diagonal element, which equals the Einstein constant. This structure depends on the orientation of the gluing used in the construction.
returned_results.name: Theorem 0.2

trajectory.query: compact self-dual Kähler orbifold positive scalar curvature somewhere trivial second cohomology reversed orientation anti-self-dual

returned_results.slogan: A compact self-dual Kähler orbifold with positive scalar curvature somewhere has trivial second cohomology group when the orientation is reversed. Reversing the orientation makes the metric anti-self-dual. The result holds under the assumption that the set of points with positive scalar curvature is non-empty.
returned_results.name: Proposition 7.9

returned_results.slogan: A compact four-dimensional orbifold with an anti-self-dual Einstein metric of positive scalar curvature has no compactly supported second cohomology. If the metric is anti-self-dual and Ricci-flat, the compactly supported second cohomology consists of parallel sections of the bundle of two-forms.
returned_results.name: Proposition 8.1

returned_results.slogan: Let M be a smooth compact oriented 4-manifold with positive second Betti number, and let Sigma be a non-empty smooth compact oriented surface in M. For some integer p at least 2, define an orbifold with cone angle 2π/p around Sigma. If this orbifold admits a scalar-flat anti-self-dual metric, then the metric is Kähler and the second Betti number of M is one. The metric is Ricci-flat if and only if the orbifold does not admit any orbifold metrics with positive scalar curvature.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.7

returned_results.slogan: On a compact oriented Riemannian manifold with vanishing divergence of the self-dual Weyl curvature and non-zero self-dual Weyl curvature everywhere, assume a specific pointwise determinant inequality holds. If the real line bundle from the top eigenvalue eigenspace is trivial, then a conformal rescaling of the metric by a power of that eigenvalue yields a Kähler metric. This rescaled metric is compatible with the orientation and has positive scalar curvature.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.1

returned_results.slogan: On a compact oriented Riemannian four-manifold with divergence-free self-dual Weyl curvature, if the determinant of the self-dual Weyl curvature is nonnegative and not identically zero, then it is strictly positive. If the positive part of the second Betti number is one, the manifold is conformal to a Kähler metric with positive scalar curvature. If the positive part of the second Betti number is zero, the pullback to the double cover is conformal to such a Kähler metric.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4

returned_results.slogan: On a compact oriented Riemannian 4-manifold with divergence-free self-dual Weyl curvature, if there exists a near-symplectic self-dual harmonic 2-form with non-negative Weyl pairing, then either the metric is anti-self-dual or the Weyl pairing is strictly positive. In the latter case, the manifold admits a global Kähler metric with positive scalar curvature. The original metric is then a conformal rescaling of this Kähler metric.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2

returned_results.slogan: A compact toric anti-self-dual Einstein orbifold with trivial orbifold fundamental group corresponds uniquely to a special symmetric toric Fano orbifold surface with trivial orbifold fundamental group. The Fano surface admits a Kähler-Einstein metric of positive scalar curvature. If the second Betti number of the orbifold is k, then the second Betti number of the Fano surface is 2k plus 2.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.17

returned_results.slogan: A compact oriented Riemannian 4-manifold with divergence-free self-dual Weyl curvature and a pointwise lower bound on its determinant must have positive determinant everywhere. If the positive part of the second Betti number is one, the manifold admits a positive-scalar-curvature Kähler metric conformal to the original. If the positive part is zero, a double cover exists where the pullback metric is conformally related to a positive-scalar-curvature Kähler metric. In both cases, the original metric is a specific conformal rescaling of this Kähler metric.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.2

returned_results.slogan: A compact oriented Riemannian 4-manifold with divergence-free self-dual Weyl tensor and positive determinant of the self-dual Weyl tensor has two possibilities. If the positive part of the second Betti number is one, the metric is conformal to an orientation-compatible Kähler metric of positive scalar curvature. If the positive part of the second Betti number is zero, a double cover exists where the pullback metric is conformal to a positive-scalar curvature Kähler metric. In both cases, the original metric relates to the Kähler metric via a scalar curvature-dependent conformal factor.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.2

returned_results.slogan: A compact oriented Riemannian 4-manifold with harmonic self-dual Weyl curvature and positive second Betti number admits a compatible Kähler metric of positive scalar curvature. This holds if the determinant of the self-dual Weyl curvature is positive everywhere. The original metric is then a rescaling of this Kähler metric by the inverse square of the scalar curvature.
returned_results.name: Theorem B

trajectory.query: deformation theory one-point conformal compactification ALE scalar-flat Kähler four-manifold unobstructed surjective linearized self-dual Weyl curvature operator

returned_results.slogan: The deformation theory of anti-self-dual conformal structures on the one-point conformal compactification of an ALE scalar-flat Kähler four-manifold is unobstructed. The linearized self-dual Weyl curvature operator is surjective at the given conformal class. This surjectivity holds for the compact anti-self-dual orbifold structure.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.2

returned_results.slogan: A compact smooth four-dimensional manifold with a scalar-flat Kähler metric and no holomorphic vector fields has a special property. For any small deformation of this metric, there exists a unique almost-Kähler anti-self-dual metric. This unique metric lies in the conformal class of the deformed metric.
returned_results.name: Lemma 5

returned_results.slogan: For any flat conformal structure on the orbifold formed by connecting two specific four-dimensional sphere quotients, a certain differential operator mapping symmetric trace-free one-forms to self-dual two-forms is surjective. This implies the deformation theory of anti-self-dual conformal structures on that orbifold is unobstructed at that conformal class.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.5

returned_results.slogan: A compact almost-Kähler manifold in four dimensions with nonnegative scalar curvature and a divergence-free self-dual Weyl tensor is a constant-scalar-curvature Kähler manifold.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2.3

returned_results.slogan: An almost Kähler four-manifold with nonnegative scalar curvature is Kähler exactly when the norm squared of the self-dual Weyl curvature equals the square of the scalar curvature divided by six.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.1

returned_results.slogan: On a compact oriented Riemannian four-manifold with divergence-free self-dual Weyl curvature, if the determinant of the self-dual Weyl curvature is nonnegative and not identically zero, then it is strictly positive. If the positive part of the second Betti number is one, the manifold is conformal to a Kähler metric with positive scalar curvature. If the positive part of the second Betti number is zero, the pullback to the double cover is conformal to such a Kähler metric.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4

returned_results.slogan: A compact simply connected almost-Kähler Einstein four-manifold with a degenerate spectrum of the self-dual Weyl tensor is Kähler-Einstein.
returned_results.name: Corollary 7

returned_results.slogan: A compact oriented Riemannian 4-manifold with divergence-free self-dual Weyl curvature and a pointwise lower bound on its determinant must have positive determinant everywhere. If the positive part of the second Betti number is one, the manifold admits a positive-scalar-curvature Kähler metric conformal to the original. If the positive part is zero, a double cover exists where the pullback metric is conformally related to a positive-scalar-curvature Kähler metric. In both cases, the original metric is a specific conformal rescaling of this Kähler metric.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.2

returned_results.slogan: An almost Kähler four-manifold satisfying the condition that the scalar curvature equals the norm of the self-dual Weyl tensor multiplied by the square root of six must be a Kähler manifold.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.1

returned_results.slogan: A compact almost Kähler Einstein 4-manifold is Kähler exactly when the determinant of its self-dual Weyl curvature equals S over 18 times the squared norm of the self-dual Weyl curvature.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.3

trajectory.query: Gamma convergence liminf inequality lower semicontinuity perimeter partitions fractional perimeter alpha to 1 finite perimeter sets

returned_results.slogan: For alpha between zero and one, if the characteristic functions of measurable sets converge in L1, then the fractional perimeter of the limit set is at most the limit inferior of the perimeters of the approximating sets. This implies a lower semicontinuity property for the fractional perimeter functional. In particular, if functions in a certain class converge in L1, then the associated energy functional is also lower semicontinuous. The result holds for both sets and functions under L1 convergence.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.3

returned_results.slogan: For every measurable set E in n-dimensional space, the Gamma-limit inferior of a scaled fractional functional as s approaches 1 is at least the product of a constant and a generalized perimeter of E in a domain. This holds with respect to local L1 convergence of the characteristic functions of sets. Specifically, the inequality remains valid for any sequence of sets whose characteristic functions converge locally in L1 to that of E, and for any sequence of parameters s increasing to 1.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2

returned_results.slogan: A sequence of sets with finite fractional alpha-perimeter converges locally in L1 to a set E. The fractional derivative of their characteristic functions converges weakly as measures in Omega. The lower semicontinuity of the total variation holds for the fractional derivative. The limit measure's total variation in Omega is at most the limit inferior of the variations of the approximating sets.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.3 (Lower semicontinuity of fractional variation measure)

returned_results.slogan: A sequence of finite-perimeter sets converges locally in L1 to a set E. For any fractional parameter s between 0 and 1, the s-perimeter of E is at most the limit inferior of the s-perimeters of the sets in the sequence. This establishes a lower semicontinuity property for the fractional perimeter under local L1 convergence.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.1 (Lower semi-continuity)

returned_results.slogan: Given a sequence of sets with locally finite fractional Caccioppoli alpha-perimeter in R^n, and assuming their fractional perimeters are uniformly bounded on every ball, there exists a subsequence whose characteristic functions converge locally in L1 to the characteristic function of some set. This limit set also has locally finite fractional Caccioppoli alpha-perimeter. The convergence holds as the subsequence index goes to infinity.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.6 (Compactness for locally finite fractional Caccioppoli $\alpha $-perimeter sets)

returned_results.slogan: A sequence of sets, each minimizing a fractional perimeter with a given parameter, converges locally to a set with finite fractional perimeter. The parameters converge to a finite nonnegative limit. The limit set minimizes the fractional perimeter for the limit parameter. The fractional perimeter of the limit set in any domain equals the limit of the perimeters of the approximating sets.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.1

returned_results.slogan: A sequence of measurable sets with bounded fractional perimeters converges locally in L1. The limit set has locally finite perimeter. The fractional perimeter is defined using an exponent approaching one. The bound holds uniformly on compact subsets of the domain.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1 (Equi-coercivity)

returned_results.slogan: A set's perimeter in a bounded domain with Lipschitz boundary is finite if and only if a certain limit involving a fractional perimeter is finite. The limit of one minus the fractional parameter times the fractional perimeter equals a constant times the classical perimeter. This constant depends on the dimension of the space. The result connects classical and fractional notions of perimeter.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.18

returned_results.slogan: A sequence of sets converges locally in L1 to a set E. The lower limit of a scaled fractional perimeter functional applied to these sets is bounded below by a constant times the classical perimeter of E in the domain. The scaling factor involves a sequence approaching 1. The result relates fractional and classical perimeters under set convergence.
returned_results.name: Lemma 7

returned_results.slogan: For a set with a smooth boundary, the limit of the fractional perimeter as the fractional parameter approaches one-half equals the classical perimeter almost everywhere. If a sequence of sets has uniformly bounded fractional perimeters, then their characteristic functions converge to that of a set with finite perimeter. If the sets are fractional perimeter minimizers and their characteristic functions converge, then the limit set has minimal perimeter. The sets also converge uniformly to the limit set in any smaller ball.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.3 (\cite{CV1, AdPM})

trajectory.query: recovery sequence limsup inequality fractional perimeter converges to perimeter as s approaches 1 partitions polyhedral domain

returned_results.slogan: For every measurable set E in n-dimensional space, the Gamma-limit inferior of a scaled fractional functional as s approaches 1 is at least the product of a constant and a generalized perimeter of E in a domain. This holds with respect to local L1 convergence of the characteristic functions of sets. Specifically, the inequality remains valid for any sequence of sets whose characteristic functions converge locally in L1 to that of E, and for any sequence of parameters s increasing to 1.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2

returned_results.slogan: A sequence of finite-perimeter sets converges locally in L1 to a set E. For any fractional parameter s between 0 and 1, the s-perimeter of E is at most the limit inferior of the s-perimeters of the sets in the sequence. This establishes a lower semicontinuity property for the fractional perimeter under local L1 convergence.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.1 (Lower semi-continuity)

returned_results.slogan: For a smooth bounded open set and a polyhedral cluster outside it that meets the boundary transversally, the scaled nonlocal perimeter functional converges to a multiple of the classical perimeter as the fractional parameter approaches one. This convergence occurs in the sense of Gamma convergence with respect to L1 convergence over the domain. The functionals are defined only for clusters that match the given polyhedral structure outside the domain and are set to infinity otherwise. The limit involves a constant factor depending on the dimension.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.10

returned_results.slogan: A sequence of measurable sets with bounded fractional perimeters converges locally in L1. The limit set has locally finite perimeter. The fractional perimeter is defined using an exponent approaching one. The bound holds uniformly on compact subsets of the domain.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1 (Equi-coercivity)

returned_results.slogan: For an open set with Lipschitz boundary and a set of finite perimeter in a certain region, there exists a countable set of exceptions. The limit of a scaled fractional perimeter as the fractional parameter approaches one equals a constant times the classical perimeter. This equality holds for almost every parameter value in a given interval, excluding only a countable set of exceptions.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2.24

returned_results.slogan: The s-perimeter of a set E in a bounded domain with Lipschitz boundary equals the infimum of the limit inferior of s-perimeters of approximating sets. These approximating sets are open with smooth boundaries and converge locally to E. This result holds for fractional perimeter functionals in Euclidean space.
returned_results.name: Corollary 1.4

returned_results.slogan: Given an open bounded interval Omega and an admissible partition E with finite perimeters, there exists a sequence of admissible partitions that agree with E outside Omega and converge locally in L1 to E. The upper limit of a scaled fractional energy functional for this sequence is bounded above by a limiting energy functional evaluated on the closure of Omega. This holds as a parameter sequence s_k increases to 1.
returned_results.name: Proposition A.6

returned_results.slogan: For almost every radius r between zero and R, the limit as s approaches 1 of (1-s) times the fractional perimeter of E in the ball of radius r equals the classical perimeter of E in that ball. This holds for any set E with finite perimeter contained in a larger ball of radius R. The result connects fractional and classical perimeter measures.
returned_results.name: Theorem 7.0.2

returned_results.slogan: For a measurable set with polyhedral boundary and zero perimeter relative to the domain, the upper limit of the scaled nonlocal perimeter as the fractional parameter approaches one from below is bounded above by the Zachary-Bangert perimeter.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.12

returned_results.slogan: A set's perimeter in a bounded domain with Lipschitz boundary is finite if and only if a certain limit involving a fractional perimeter is finite. The limit of one minus the fractional parameter times the fractional perimeter equals a constant times the classical perimeter. This constant depends on the dimension of the space. The result connects classical and fractional notions of perimeter.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.18

trajectory.query: compactness for sets of finite fractional perimeter as alpha approaches 1 characteristic functions relatively compact in L1 local

returned_results.slogan: A sequence of sets with bounded fractional alpha-perimeter and contained in a fixed ball has a subsequence whose characteristic functions converge in L1 to the characteristic function of a set with finite fractional alpha-perimeter.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.5 (Compactness for sets with finite fractional Caccioppoli $\alpha $-perimeter)

returned_results.slogan: Given a sequence of sets with locally finite fractional Caccioppoli alpha-perimeter in R^n, and assuming their fractional perimeters are uniformly bounded on every ball, there exists a subsequence whose characteristic functions converge locally in L1 to the characteristic function of some set. This limit set also has locally finite fractional Caccioppoli alpha-perimeter. The convergence holds as the subsequence index goes to infinity.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.6 (Compactness for locally finite fractional Caccioppoli $\alpha $-perimeter sets)

returned_results.slogan: A sequence of measurable sets with bounded fractional perimeters converges locally in L1. The limit set has locally finite perimeter. The fractional perimeter is defined using an exponent approaching one. The bound holds uniformly on compact subsets of the domain.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1 (Equi-coercivity)

returned_results.slogan: For alpha between zero and one, if the characteristic functions of measurable sets converge in L1, then the fractional perimeter of the limit set is at most the limit inferior of the perimeters of the approximating sets. This implies a lower semicontinuity property for the fractional perimeter functional. In particular, if functions in a certain class converge in L1, then the associated energy functional is also lower semicontinuous. The result holds for both sets and functions under L1 convergence.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.3

returned_results.slogan: A sequence of sets with finite fractional alpha-perimeter converges locally in L1 to a set E. The fractional derivative of their characteristic functions converges weakly as measures in Omega. The lower semicontinuity of the total variation holds for the fractional derivative. The limit measure's total variation in Omega is at most the limit inferior of the variations of the approximating sets.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.3 (Lower semicontinuity of fractional variation measure)

returned_results.slogan: A sequence of Lebesgue measurable sets in R^n satisfies a uniform bound on a rescaled nonlocal perimeter functional. This implies the sequence is relatively compact in the local L^1 space. Every limit point of the sequence is a set of locally finite perimeter in the domain. The result holds under the assumption that the fractional parameter approaches one from below.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.1

returned_results.slogan: A sequence of sets in a bounded open set has uniformly bounded fractional perimeters scaled by a function. The characteristic functions of these sets converge in L1 to the characteristic function of some set. For fractional parameters below one half, the limit set has finite fractional perimeter. For parameters from one half to one, the limit set has finite standard perimeter.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.1

returned_results.slogan: A sequence of finite perimeter sets with bounded characteristic functions and locally bounded perimeters has a subsequence converging locally in L1. The limit is the characteristic function of a finite perimeter set. This result holds on a manifold with relatively compact open subsets.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.2 (Compactness \cite{Mi})

returned_results.slogan: For every measurable set E in n-dimensional space, the Gamma-limit inferior of a scaled fractional functional as s approaches 1 is at least the product of a constant and a generalized perimeter of E in a domain. This holds with respect to local L1 convergence of the characteristic functions of sets. Specifically, the inequality remains valid for any sequence of sets whose characteristic functions converge locally in L1 to that of E, and for any sequence of parameters s increasing to 1.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2

returned_results.slogan: A sequence of functions with bounded local norms and fractional seminorms converges locally in L1. The limit function is locally of bounded variation. The fractional order approaches one. The result holds for any compactly contained subset of the domain.
returned_results.name: Proposition A.4 (Equi-coercivity)

trajectory.query: fractional perimeter of partition or cluster equals sum of interface terms lower semicontinuity cluster energy under L1 convergence

This implies a lower semicontinuity property for the fractional perimeter functional. In particular, if functions in a certain class converge in L1, then the associated energy functional is also lower semicontinuous. The result holds for both sets and functions under L1 convergence.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.3

returned_results.slogan: The energy functional has two key properties. If a set has positive fractional perimeter, the energy equals the perimeter divided by the fractional perimeter raised to a power. The energy is also lower semicontinuous with respect to L1 convergence of sets.
returned_results.name: Lemma B.1 (Properties of $\mathcal{Q}(-,\gamma )$)

returned_results.slogan: A sequence of finite-perimeter sets converges locally in L1 to a set E. For any fractional parameter s between 0 and 1, the s-perimeter of E is at most the limit inferior of the s-perimeters of the sets in the sequence. This establishes a lower semicontinuity property for the fractional perimeter under local L1 convergence.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.1 (Lower semi-continuity)

returned_results.slogan: A sequence of sets converges locally in L1, with each set being a local minimizer for a fractional energy functional. The upper limit of the scaled energy remains finite for any compact subset of the domain. The limit set is a local minimizer of the classical perimeter functional. The scaled energy converges to a multiple of the perimeter under certain boundary conditions.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1 (Convergence of local minimizers)

returned_results.slogan: The lower semicontinuity property holds for the fractional perimeter functional. If the indicator functions of sets converge locally in L1 with respect to a weighted measure, then the perimeter of the limit set is at most the limit inferior of the perimeters of the approximating sets. This means the perimeter functional does not suddenly increase in the limit. The result applies to subsets of a domain under a fractional Laplacian framework.
returned_results.name: Corollary 0.7

returned_results.slogan: If the characteristic functions of sets E_k converge locally in L^1 to the characteristic function of set E, then the s-fractional perimeter of E is at most the limit inferior of the s-fractional perimeters of the sets E_k. This holds for subsets of a space X. The result shows lower semicontinuity of the fractional perimeter functional under this type of convergence.
returned_results.name: Proposition 5.1

returned_results.slogan: An N-cluster in a manifold satisfies that its perimeter in any subset equals half the sum of the perimeters of its individual clusters in that subset. If a sequence of clusters converges locally to another cluster, then the perimeter of the limit cluster in any open set is at most the limit inferior of the perimeters of the approximating clusters in that set. This shows lower semicontinuity of the perimeter functional under local convergence.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1

returned_results.slogan: A bounded open set and a fixed cluster outside it are considered. A sequence of clusters matches the fixed one outside and has uniformly bounded fractional perimeter energies. These clusters are relatively compact in the L1 norm on the open set.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.12

returned_results.slogan: Under certain hypotheses and boundary conditions, a sequence of weak solutions to a fractional equation converges to a limit function that is a sum of characteristic functions over a partition. The partition is a nonlocal minimal partition for a given functional, and each set in the partition has finite nonlocal perimeter. The convergence is strong in local Sobolev and Lebesgue spaces, and the energy converges to a nonlocal perimeter functional. The transition sets of the solutions converge locally uniformly to the boundaries of the partition sets.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1

returned_results.slogan: The perimeter of a set F with respect to an (N,M)-cluster X equals half the sum of the perimeters of F with respect to each of the N plus M subdomains of the cluster. If a sequence of clusters converges locally to X and U is an open set, then the perimeter of X in U is at most the limit inferior of the perimeters of the clusters in U.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.4

trajectory.query: Gamma convergence of nonlocal perimeter for clusters partitions as s approaches 1 polyhedral clusters recovery sequence

returned_results.slogan: For a smooth bounded open set and a polyhedral cluster outside it that meets the boundary transversally, the scaled nonlocal perimeter functional converges to a multiple of the classical perimeter as the fractional parameter approaches one. This convergence occurs in the sense of Gamma convergence with respect to L1 convergence over the domain. The functionals are defined only for clusters that match the given polyhedral structure outside the domain and are set to infinity otherwise. The limit involves a constant factor depending on the dimension.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.10

returned_results.slogan: The rescaled nonlocal perimeters Gamma-converge to a local perimeter functional. For any sequence of sets converging locally in L1, the lower limit of the rescaled nonlocal perimeter is bounded below by the local perimeter. There also exists a recovery sequence for which the upper limit of the rescaled nonlocal perimeter is bounded above by the local perimeter. This establishes Gamma-convergence of the rescaled functionals.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.8 ($\Gamma $-convergence of rescaled nonlocal perimeters)

returned_results.slogan: The theorem establishes a Gamma-convergence result for a family of nonlocal perimeters. It states that the limit functional is bounded below by the lower limit of the approximating functionals along any converging sequence of sets. Conversely, for every set, there exists a sequence of sets converging to it such that the limit functional is bounded above by the upper limit of the approximating functionals. This holds under the convergence of the parameters R_n and sigma_n to their limit values.
returned_results.name: Theorem 6.3

returned_results.slogan: A compactness result states that, under a uniform perimeter bound, characteristic functions and a related theta function converge weakly to a limit set and a piecewise constant function. The Gamma-liminf inequality shows that the lower limit of the perimeter is at least the sum of anisotropic perimeters of the limit partition. The Gamma-limsup inequality constructs a recovery sequence whose perimeter upper limit is bounded by the same anisotropic sum. Together, these establish Gamma-convergence of the perimeter functional.
returned_results.name: Theorem A.2

returned_results.slogan: Under certain conditions, if a sequence of sets with finite perimeter converges in L1 to a set E and their perimeters are bounded, then the nonlocal perimeter of the sets converges to the nonlocal perimeter of E for every positive epsilon.

returned_results.slogan: For a given parameter s between 0 and 1, and with the domain as all of n-dimensional space, a certain functional converges as epsilon approaches zero. The limit functional is expressed as the perimeter of a set minus a scaled nonlocal perimeter term. The scaling factor t is any positive number. This convergence holds in the sense of Gamma-convergence.

The nonlocal perimeter of the sequence converges to that of E.

This holds under the condition that the scaling parameter approaches zero. The result applies in any dimension and for any s at least one. The theorem links nonlocal perimeter bounds to the local perimeter property of the limit set.
