This holds for all homological degrees and multidegrees. In particular, the regularity of the k-th symbolic power of the edge ideal of H is at most that of G.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2.6

returned_results.slogan: For an induced subgraph H of a graph G, the graded Betti numbers of the quotient ring S_H over I_H are bounded above by the corresponding Betti numbers of S over I_G. This holds for all indices i and j. The ring S_H is defined using variables corresponding to the vertices of H. The result relates algebraic invariants of the subgraph to those of the full graph.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.7

returned_results.slogan: If H is an induced subgraph of G, then the Betti numbers of the k-th symbolic power of the edge ideal of H are bounded above by those of G. This implies the projective dimension of the symbolic power of I(H) is at most that of I(G). Similarly, the regularity of the symbolic power of I(H) is at most that of I(G). These inequalities hold for all homological degrees and multidegrees.
returned_results.name: Corollary 1.3

returned_results.slogan: If H is an induced subgraph of G, then the regularity of S divided by I of H is at most the regularity of S divided by I of G.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.13

returned_results.slogan: For an induced subgraph H of a graph G and a positive integer n, the graded Betti numbers of the n-th symbolic power of the edge ideal of H are at most those of G. Additionally, the regularity of the n-th symbolic power of the edge ideal of H is at most that of G.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.8

returned_results.slogan: For an edge-weighted graph and its induced subgraph, the graded Betti numbers of the quotient ring for the subgraph are bounded above by those of the original graph for all indices and powers. This inequality holds for every positive integer exponent. In particular, the regularity of powers of the subgraph's edge ideal is at most the regularity of powers of the original graph's edge ideal. This applies uniformly to all powers greater than or equal to one.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.2

trajectory.query: edge ideal of complete intersection of pairwise disjoint monomials regularity equals sum of degrees minus number of generators

returned_results.slogan: For a complete intersection ideal I with monomial generators in nonincreasing degree, the regularity of its n-th power equals n times the largest generator degree plus the sum of the remaining generator degrees, minus the number of generators minus one. This holds for all positive integers n. The formula depends only on the degrees of the minimal monomial generators.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.1

returned_results.slogan: If a monomial ideal is generated by a regular sequence of monomials, then the regularity of the ideal equals the sum of the degrees of the generators minus the number of generators plus one.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.2

returned_results.slogan: The regularity of the sum of two monomial ideals generated in disjoint sets of variables equals the sum of their regularities minus one.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.7

returned_results.slogan: For a complete intersection monomial ideal I of dimension at least one, the regularity of S over I equals the sum of the degrees of the minimal generators minus the number of generators. The delta function of I at degree d is one when d is at least the regularity. For degrees less than the regularity, the delta function is bounded above by a product involving the degrees of the generators.
returned_results.name: Proposition 5.3

returned_results.slogan: The regularity of a monomial ideal generated by pure powers of variables equals the sum of the exponents minus the number of variables plus one.
returned_results.name: Lemma 1.3

returned_results.slogan: The regularity of the edge ideal of a graph equals the sum of the regularities of the edge ideals of its disjoint components.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.2 ({\cite[Lemma 8]{woodroof}})

returned_results.slogan: The regularity of the edge ideal of a graph equals the sum of the regularities of the edge ideals of its disjoint components.
returned_results.name: Corollary 3.10

returned_results.slogan: The theorem relates the regularity of a monomial in a combined ideal to the sum of regularities in two separate extended ideals. It applies to graded ideals in polynomial rings over disjoint variable sets. The result holds for monomials of degree greater than one. The formula expresses the regularity in terms of the regularities after adjoining maximal ideals to each component.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.2

returned_results.slogan: For a complete intersection ideal generated by homogeneous polynomials, the degree of the quotient ring equals the product of the degrees of the generators. The regularity of the quotient ring is the sum of each generator's degree minus one. The number of generators equals the height of the ideal. These formulas hold for such ideals in a polynomial ring.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.11

returned_results.slogan: The regularity of the sum of two graded ideals in disjoint sets of variables equals the sum of their regularities minus one.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.1

trajectory.query: height of critical Galton-Watson tree tail asymptotic via Lukasiewicz path and stable height process
Duquesne Le Gall theorem height process conditioned Galton-Watson tree maximal height tail
multitype Galton-Watson tree projection to monotype forest theorem

returned_results.slogan: A multitype Galton-Watson forest conditioned on a given multitype degree sequence has the same distribution as a multitype forest with that degree sequence. The law of a configuration model multitype Galton-Watson forest is a finite mixture of these conditioned laws over all valid degree sequences. This holds for specified type counts and root counts with at least one root. The progeny distributions are assumed to have independent components.
returned_results.name: Lemma 6

returned_results.slogan: A multitype Bienaymé-Galton-Watson forest with given offspring distribution and root counts has a corresponding reduced forest. The count of vertices of a given type at or below a certain height in the reduced forest equals a random variable R. The count of vertices of a given type at or below a certain reduced height in the original forest equals a random variable U. These equalities hold jointly across types and heights.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.1

returned_results.slogan: Under a given probability measure, a forest constructed from a sequence is a non-degenerate, irreducible, critical multi-type Galton-Watson forest. The offspring distribution for types one through K-1 is defined recursively using generating functions that depend on the generating function for type K. The sequences counting offspring of each type are independent and identically distributed, with generating functions also defined recursively. Any moment conditions on the original offspring distribution are preserved for the new distributions and counting variables.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3

returned_results.slogan: The marked forest is a multitype Galton-Watson forest under the annealed law. Its roots have initial type one.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.2

returned_results.slogan: A multi-type Galton-Watson forest with Poisson offspring distribution, when conditioned on the number of individuals of each type and relabeled by uniform random permutations, becomes uniformly distributed over the set of all labeled forests with the given root type and size counts. The conditional probability of observing any specific labeled forest is inversely proportional to a combinatorial factor involving the total number of individuals. This result holds for forests with d types and Poisson offspring parameter mu. The uniformity is over the class of labeled forests with specified root type and type counts.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2

returned_results.slogan: The offspring distribution of a non-degenerate irreducible multitype Galton-Watson forest converges in distribution as the index increases. The components of the distribution are independent and aperiodic, with zero mean for certain processes. Stable process limits are assumed for scaled increments with specific stability parameters. The convergence holds under the law of the conditioned multitype Galton-Watson forest.
returned_results.name: Lemma 13

returned_results.slogan: The theorem assigns a specific type to each vertex in a tree based on given target sets. Using these assigned types, the original tree and a modified pivotal tree are both characterized as multitype Galton-Watson trees. This classification relies solely on the defined vertex types.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.4

returned_results.slogan: A Galton-Watson tree with mean offspring at most one, conditioned on having exactly n leaves in a certain set, converges in distribution to a modified Galton-Watson tree as n goes to infinity. The same convergence holds when conditioning on having at least n leaves in that set. The limit is defined along the infinite subsequence where the conditioning event has positive probability. The limit tree has an offspring distribution derived from the original and the specified set of leaf types.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.2

returned_results.slogan: For a Galton-Watson tree conditioned on having n nodes, three conditions are equivalent: a specific offspring distribution form, the two-tree forest matching two independent conditioned trees, and the k-tree forest matching k independent conditioned trees. When these hold, the sequence of forests corresponds to a refining partition sequence defined by labeling nodes. This sequence develops by recursive Gibbs fragmentation with linear selection and also forms a Marcus-Lushnikov coalescent with an affine kernel.
returned_results.name: Corollary 3

returned_results.slogan: For a monotype Galton-Watson forest with r tree components and offspring distribution μ, the scaled height process converges in distribution to a multiple of a Brownian excursion as the number of vertices grows large. This holds under certain hypotheses and when the scaling parameter K equals one. The limit is given by two divided by the standard deviation of the offspring distribution times a Brownian excursion. The convergence occurs for processes indexed by time s between zero and one.
returned_results.name: Lemma 8

trajectory.query: infimum of stable spectrally positive Levy process integral tail gives height asymptotic

returned_results.slogan: The density of the infimum of a spectrally positive Lévy process behaves asymptotically near zero. The asymptotic expression involves the gamma function evaluated at parameters related to the process. It also includes the tail of the Lévy measure at the logarithm of the reciprocal of x. The constant factor depends on the expected value of the infimum of the ladder height process raised to a negative power.
returned_results.name: Proposition

returned_results.slogan: For a Lévy process with a Lévy measure satisfying a certain condition, consider a family of predictable positive processes with bounded moments. The limit of the infimum of the tail probability ratio equals the infimum of the expected integral of the process raised to a power. Additionally, the supremum of the absolute difference between the tail probability ratio and this expected integral converges to zero. These results hold as the threshold tends to infinity.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2

returned_results.slogan: The tail of the supremum process is asymptotically equivalent to a function involving an integral transformation. This equivalence holds under conditions on the tail of the intensity measure and moment conditions on the Lévy measure. The result applies as the argument tends to infinity. The asymptotic form depends on the parameters gamma and t, and the Lévy measure pi.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3

returned_results.slogan: The supremum of a transformed Lévy process over a unit time interval has an exponential tail bound. The process is defined by subtracting its infimum from a specific stable Lévy process with downward jumps. The bound holds for all non-negative values of x. The constants in the bound are positive and finite.
returned_results.name: Proposition B.7

returned_results.slogan: For a Lamperti stable process with positive jumps that drifts to negative infinity, the tail of the Lévy measure of its increasing ladder height process belongs to a certain class. The tail asymptotically behaves like a constant multiple of the tail of the original Lévy measure as the argument tends to infinity. The constant depends on the process characteristics and parameters.
returned_results.name: Proposition 8

returned_results.slogan: For any Levy process X and a fixed positive alpha, the tail of the Levy measure of X is in the class L-superscript-alpha if and only if the tail of the Levy measure of its ascending ladder height process H is also in L-superscript-alpha. In that case, the ratio of these tails tends to the Laplace exponent of the ascending ladder height process evaluated at alpha as x goes to infinity.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.2

returned_results.slogan: For a Lévy process with zero mean and finite variance, the infimum up to time t is considered. The limit superior as t approaches infinity of a scaled supremum over u of a certain probability is finite. The scaling factor is the square root of t, and the probability involves the event that the infimum is at least minus u. The result establishes a bound on the asymptotic behavior of this probability expression.
returned_results.name: Proposition 6.4

returned_results.slogan: A Levy process drifting to infinity has an equality in distribution between an integral involving its future infimum process and an integral of its conditioned positive version. The constant m is the mean of the first ladder height. A consequence relates the full integral of the exponentiated process to an integral up to the last time it hits its overall minimum. This involves an independent copy of the future infimum integral scaled by m and the exponential of the process at that last hitting time.
returned_results.name: Lemma 5 (An interesting identity for exponential functionals)

returned_results.slogan: A spectrally positive alpha-stable Levy process with a specific Levy measure has a continuous modification for its height process when shifted by a constant drift. The height process of a scaled random walk converges in distribution to this modified height process under appropriate scaling. The convergence occurs in the space of cadlag functions from the nonnegative reals to the reals, squared. The scaling factors depend on the stability parameter alpha.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.2

returned_results.slogan: The theorem establishes an almost sure convergence result for a spectrally positive stable Lévy process with specific parameters. It requires the process Z to be Hölder continuous with a constant having finite moments. The limit involves the supremum over time and space of a normalized measure converging to the local time. The convergence holds uniformly for all positive times T.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1

trajectory.query: for critical Galton-Watson tree probability height at least n asymptotic constant stable index alpha

returned_results.slogan: The probability that a critical Galton-Watson tree with offspring distribution mu has exactly n vertices is asymptotically equivalent to C divided by n times B sub n. This holds as n tends to infinity, for n where the probability is positive. The constant C is positive, and mu is in the domain of attraction of a stable law. The sequence B sub n satisfies a specific growth condition.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.5 (Local limit theorem)

returned_results.slogan: A critical Galton-Watson tree with offspring distribution in the domain of attraction of an alpha-stable law, where alpha is between one and two, has parameter D equal to alpha divided by alpha minus one. When conditioned on having n vertices, the tree satisfies two assumptions with the same D. The tree also satisfies two other assumptions with the same D, beta equals one over alpha, and any real gamma. The asymptotic behavior of one minus the generating function near zero is provided by two referenced equations.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4

returned_results.slogan: A critical and aperiodic probability measure in the domain of attraction of a stable law with index between one and two leads to a scaling limit for conditioned Galton-Watson trees. The tree is scaled by the inverse of its size and a regularly varying sequence. The limit is a specific random tree measure known as the stable tree of index alpha. This convergence holds when conditioning the tree to have exactly n vertices.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.2 (\cite{Duq})

returned_results.slogan: For a critical Galton-Watson tree, the expectation of one minus the generating function evaluated at one minus alpha is asymptotically equivalent to the square root of alpha as alpha approaches zero. The asymptotic equivalence holds up to multiplicative constants. These constants depend solely on the variance of the offspring distribution.
returned_results.name: Lemma A.3

returned_results.slogan: A random vertex chosen uniformly from a conditioned Galton-Watson tree has a mass that concentrates around a power of n. The offspring distribution has mean one and is in the domain of attraction of a stable law with index alpha between one and two. There exists a constant lambda alpha greater than one over alpha minus one that depends only on alpha. With high probability, the mass lies between n to the negative lambda alpha minus delta and n to the negative lambda alpha plus delta for any positive delta.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1

returned_results.slogan: The probability that the height of a tree is at least n is asymptotically equivalent to a constant times n to the power of negative one over alpha minus one.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.4

returned_results.slogan: For a d-type Galton-Watson tree with a specified offspring distribution, the probability that its height exceeds n decays like a constant over n as n grows large. The constant depends on the type i, the minimal mean offspring alpha, and another parameter c. This limit holds under the main assumptions on the offspring distribution. The expression gives the exact asymptotic rate of decay for the tail probability of the tree height.
returned_results.name: Corollary 1

returned_results.slogan: For a critical Galton-Watson tree with integer offspring distribution and finite variance, the probability that the total size equals n is asymptotically proportional to n to the power of negative three halves. The constant of proportionality involves the square root of two pi and the standard deviation of the offspring distribution. The error term tends to zero as n grows large.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.1

returned_results.slogan: For a critical Galton-Watson tree with finite variance, the probability that the height is at least x given size n is bounded above by a constant times the square root of n multiplied by the probability that a certain random variable eta1 is at least x minus 2.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5

returned_results.slogan: A conditioned critical Bienaymé–Galton–Watson tree with n vertices and offspring distribution attracted to a stable law converges in distribution when scaled appropriately. The scaling involves an increasing slowly varying function and depends on the index alpha between 1 and 2. The rescaled height and contour processes both converge to the same limit. When alpha equals 2, the scaling function tends to a constant related to the variance, and the spatial process limit equals the height limit.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.1 (\textsc{Duquesne \cite{Duquesne2003Contour}})

trajectory.query: Moore polynomial set scattered polynomial index 0 lemma Moore set implies scattered under degree conditions

returned_results.slogan: A Moore polynomial set for given parameters has three functions with specific degree conditions. If the degree n exceeds four times the largest degree plus two, then the second function in the set is scattered. This scattering property holds with index zero. The result applies under the stated inequality.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.9

returned_results.slogan: A set of Moore polynomials with more than three components and a separable second function is considered. Under conditions on the field size, indices, and degree bounds, the second polynomial is scattered. This holds when the field order exceeds five and the main parameter n is sufficiently large relative to the maximum degrees. The result confirms the scattered nature of the specified polynomial component.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.15

returned_results.slogan: A Moore polynomial set for given parameters includes three functions, with the first being a power function. The second function is separable, and the maximum of two values is less than a third value. If the parameter n is sufficiently large, then the second function is scattered with the specified index.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.13

returned_results.slogan: A Moore polynomial set f with three functions and index zero has specific degree conditions. Under given constraints on q and n, if n exceeds a bound based on the largest degree, then f must consist of x, x raised to the q to the M, and x raised to the q to the 2M. The exponent M must be coprime with n.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.10

returned_results.slogan: Given certain conditions on k, n, and q, if a set of Moore polynomials has index t, then the degrees of the polynomials can be reordered to form an arithmetic progression. The conditions depend on whether k equals 3 or is greater than 3. For k greater than 3, q must exceed 5 and n must be sufficiently large relative to M_k and q. For k equal to 3, n must exceed a specific bound based on M_3.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.12

returned_results.slogan: A set of k non-negative integers is a Moore exponent set for given q and n if and only if the corresponding set of q-polynomials forms an MRD-code. This is also equivalent to the linear set generated by these polynomials being scattered with respect to hyperplanes in a projective space.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.15

returned_results.slogan: For a natural number t greater than or equal to two, the only exceptional scattered polynomials of index t are those with at least two non-trivial terms. These terms must have q-degree less than t. The term with q-degree zero is not counted among these.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.3

returned_results.slogan: For a Moore polynomial set with specific conditions on the number of polynomials, field size, and degree, the set must consist of monomials with exponents that are powers of q. The exponents form a geometric progression with a common ratio of q raised to an integer M, where M is coprime to n. The theorem holds when the field size exceeds 5 and the degree n is sufficiently large relative to the largest exponent.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.11

returned_results.slogan: A multidegree m is a Scarf multidegree exactly when the set P_m is empty. This holds for any m not equal to 1 in the set L_M. The set P_m is defined as in a previous theorem.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.21

returned_results.slogan: For k equals 3 and n greater than 4 times M3 plus 2, or for k greater than 3, q greater than 5, and n greater than 13 over 3 times Mk plus log base q of 13 times 2 to the 10 over 3, if f is a Moore polynomial set for q and n of index 0, then the sequence M1 equals 0, M2, up to Mk is an arithmetic progression. Additionally, the sequence m sigma 1 equals 0, m sigma 2, up to m sigma k is also an arithmetic progression for some permutation sigma in the symmetric group on k elements with sigma 1 equal to 1.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.6

trajectory.query: linearized polynomial scattered of index 0 definition basic properties
Moore polynomial set q n index 0 with f1(x)=x basic theorem

returned_results.slogan: For every MOY graph and natural number N, the polynomial F equals the mu function applied to the pair of the polynomial P evaluated at q, q to the N, and x, and q raised to N.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.2

returned_results.slogan: If a polynomial F satisfies a certain modular condition, then whenever a monomial m raised to the q-th power modulo (x^(q^n) - x) appears in F, the monomial m itself modulo (x^(q^n) - x) must also be in F. Additionally, if F contains a monomial of the form α x^(kq+1), then it must also contain the monomial α^(1/q) x^(k + q^(n-1)). These results hold under the given modular constraint on F.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.3

returned_results.slogan: For n at least 2, the polynomial f sub n minus one of q is congruent to the Möbius function of n modulo the n-th cyclotomic polynomial. When n is prime, this simplifies to f sub p minus one of q being congruent to negative one modulo the q-bracket of p.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1

returned_results.slogan: For a positive integer N, if f(X) is a polynomial in the set P(N;q), then the value (-1)^N times f(0) is a primitive element of the finite field F_q.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.1

returned_results.slogan: A quasi-symmetric polynomial f in R[X] satisfies f(t^q) equals f(t) modulo the polynomial t raised to q^n minus t.
returned_results.name: Lemma

returned_results.slogan: The minimal polynomial of alpha is the sum of x raised to powers from zero to n. The set N consists of alpha and its q-powers up to q to the n minus one. This set forms an optimal normal basis for the field extension of q to the n over the base field of q.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.1

returned_results.slogan: A quasi-symmetric polynomial f in R[X] satisfies f of t to the q equals f of t modulo t to the q to the n minus t.
returned_results.name: Lemma

returned_results.slogan: For every positive integer n, f_n to the power of 0 is 1 and f_n to the power of 1 is f_n. For all q and q' in I to the n of K, f_n to the d of q plus q' equals the sum from k equals 0 to d of f_n to the k of q times f_n to the d minus k of q'. For all phi in Pf_n of K and d at least 2, f_n to the d of phi is 0. In particular, f_n to the d of I to the n of K is a subset of A to the n times d of K.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.2.9

returned_results.slogan: The polynomial f_n(x) is the right minimal polynomial for the set Z containing elements a_1 through a_n.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.6

returned_results.slogan: The function S_n of f equals a polynomial P_n evaluated at the quantities q_1 of f, q_2 of f, and so on up to q_n of f. This holds for every integer n greater than or equal to zero.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.2

trajectory.query: arithmetic progression exponents Moore polynomial set index 0 n > 4 M3 + 2 theorem k=3

returned_results.slogan: For k equals 3 and n greater than 4 times M3 plus 2, or for k greater than 3, q greater than 5, and n greater than 13 over 3 times Mk plus log base q of 13 times 2 to the 10 over 3, if f is a Moore polynomial set for q and n of index 0, then the sequence M1 equals 0, M2, up to Mk is an arithmetic progression. Additionally, the sequence m sigma 1 equals 0, m sigma 2, up to m sigma k is also an arithmetic progression for some permutation sigma in the symmetric group on k elements with sigma 1 equal to 1.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.6

returned_results.slogan: Given certain conditions on k, n, and q, if a set of Moore polynomials has index t, then the degrees of the polynomials can be reordered to form an arithmetic progression. The conditions depend on whether k equals 3 or is greater than 3. For k greater than 3, q must exceed 5 and n must be sufficiently large relative to M_k and q. For k equal to 3, n must exceed a specific bound based on M_3.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.12

returned_results.slogan: A Moore polynomial set f with three functions and index zero has specific degree conditions. Under given constraints on q and n, if n exceeds a bound based on the largest degree, then f must consist of x, x raised to the q to the M, and x raised to the q to the 2M. The exponent M must be coprime with n.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.10

returned_results.slogan: For a Moore polynomial set with specific conditions on the number of polynomials, field size, and degree, the set must consist of monomials with exponents that are powers of q. The exponents form a geometric progression with a common ratio of q raised to an integer M, where M is coprime to n. The theorem holds when the field size exceeds 5 and the degree n is sufficiently large relative to the largest exponent.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.11

returned_results.slogan: A Moore polynomial set for given parameters has three functions with specific degree conditions. If the degree n exceeds four times the largest degree plus two, then the second function in the set is scattered. This scattering property holds with index zero. The result applies under the stated inequality.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.9

returned_results.slogan: The function M sub k of 3 is at least three-fourths times two to the k plus two for all k greater than or equal to three.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.7

returned_results.slogan: Let I be a set of non-negative integers not in arithmetic progression. If I has size three and n is greater than four times the largest element plus two, or if I has size greater than three, q is greater than five, and n exceeds a certain bound, then the set of polynomials x, x raised to q to the power of each element in I except the first, is not a Moore polynomial set for q and n.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.5

returned_results.slogan: For k at least 1, if m0 equals 2 to the power of 2k minus 1, minus a sum of terms involving choices of 0 or 1 multiplied by 3 times 2 to the power of 2r plus 1, and minus a beta value of 0 or 2, then 4 times m0 plus 3 can also be written in the same form.
returned_results.name: Proposition 13

returned_results.slogan: For n greater than 1, the expression M_n is defined recursively based on n modulo 3. If n is a multiple of 3, M_n equals M_3 raised to the k power. If n is one more than a multiple of 3, M_n equals M_3 raised to k-1 times M_4. If n is two more than a multiple of 3, M_n equals M_3 raised to k times M_2. These expressions are extremal.
returned_results.name: Proposition 7

returned_results.slogan: For any odd prime p congruent to 3 modulo 4, and integers m at least 2 and n at least 1, the theorem holds for k equal to 2 raised to m times p raised to n.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.6

trajectory.query: Moore exponent set equivalent MRD code scattered linear set theorem

returned_results.slogan: A topological space is scattered if and only if for every subset, the derived set of the subset equals the derived set of the subset minus its own derived set. This is also equivalent to the powerset of the space, equipped with the derived set operator, forming a Magari algebra. These three conditions are all equivalent.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.1 (Simmons, Esakia)

returned_results.slogan: Theorems MR-matrix and MR-matrix are equivalent.
returned_results.name: Lemma 5.11

returned_results.slogan: An X-scattered set is m-equivalent to a countable union of rectangles.
returned_results.name: Theorem

returned_results.slogan: A Lindelof scattered space is exponentially separable.
returned_results.name: Corollary 15

returned_results.slogan: A subset A of a group G is scattered if and only if it is disparse. This is equivalent to A containing no subsets coarsely equivalent to the infinite direct sum of Z2 over omega. It is also equivalent to A containing no piecewise shifted IP-sets. All four conditions are equivalent.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1

returned_results.slogan: The set S sub sc pseudo of M is an e-variable for M if and only if it equals the set S sub sc gro of M.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1

returned_results.slogan: The set M_r satisfies the Minkowski property.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.12

returned_results.slogan: The set M_r satisfies the Minkowski property.
returned_results.name: Lemma

returned_results.slogan: For every subset of the rational numbers, the following conditions are equivalent: the set is scattered, the restriction of the well-ordering relation to the set belongs to a certain class, that same restriction is Borel, and the full well-ordering relation does not embed into its restriction on the set.
returned_results.name: Theorem 6.1

returned_results.slogan: A subset A of a G-space X is scattered if and only if, for each p in the corona of X, the diagonal set of A at p is discrete. This is also equivalent to A containing no piecewise shifted FP-sets. Additionally, A is scattered if and only if it contains no subsets coarsely equivalent to the Cantor macrocube. These four conditions are all equivalent.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.4

trajectory.query: highly acyclic sequence via FI complexes or injective words complex acyclic for symmetric groups

returned_results.slogan: For an integral representation W of the symmetric group on d elements, the homology of the injective words complex with coefficients in W is isomorphic to the tensor product of the homology of the standard complex with W, both stabilized. More generally, for any FI-sharp module V, the homology of its injective words complex at degree k decomposes as an induced representation from a product of symmetric groups. This induced representation involves the homology of the standard complex at a certain degree and the zeroth homology of V at a complementary index. The result expresses the structure in terms of representations of symmetric groups.
returned_results.name: Theorem

returned_results.slogan: An FI-complex sequence has highly acyclic simplicial complexes if each homology module is finitely generated and torsion. This holds for every degree of homology. The result applies uniformly across all terms in the sequence.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2

returned_results.slogan: The space is an acyclic and invariant subcomplex under the symmetric group action.
returned_results.name: Proposition 5.7

returned_results.slogan: The symmetric power of an FI-module is F-acyclic above a certain degree. This holds when the module is generated and related in bounded degrees. The bound depends on the generation and relation degrees. Specifically, it applies for symmetric powers beyond the sum of the relation degree and the minimum of the generation and relation degrees.
returned_results.name: Theorem 12

returned_results.slogan: A sequence of symmetric group representations with connecting maps forms an FI-module if and only if three conditions hold. The inclusions are compatible under composition. The maps are equivariant with respect to the symmetric group actions. The maps are invariant under the action of permutations from the complement.
returned_results.name: Proposition (The $\FI$-module criterion)

returned_results.slogan: The sequence forms an acyclic complex.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2

returned_results.slogan: I(n) is acyclic, meaning its homology is zero. The sequence of I(n) is closed under partial compositions. It is also closed under symmetric group actions.
returned_results.name: Lemma 5.9

returned_results.slogan: For any module W over the group algebra of the symmetric group on m elements, the associated FI-module M(W) has injectivity degree zero. The surjectivity degree of M(W) is at most m.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.38

returned_results.slogan: For any injective FI-group, there is a quasi-isomorphism between derived FI-homology of its chain complex and a tensor product. This implies that the FI-homology groups of the chain complex are isomorphic to the group homology with coefficients in a specific module.
returned_results.name: Proposition 6.1

returned_results.slogan: The category of FI-modules presented in finite degrees is abelian. Kernels and cokernels of maps between such modules are also presented in finite degrees. An FI-module presented in finite degrees is FI-homology acyclic precisely when it is semi-induced. This characterizes the acyclic modules in terms of the semi-induced property.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.3

trajectory.query: Quillen fiber theorem nerve theorem acyclicity from highly connected links poset complex

returned_results.slogan: If a cover of a space satisfies certain acyclic nerve theorem conditions, and its nerve is acyclic, then the homology of the associated complex is acyclic to a specific degree.
returned_results.name: Corollary 3.9

returned_results.slogan: Let f from P to Q be a poset map. If the fiber over each lower set Q less than or equal to q has a t-connected order complex, then the order complex of P is t-connected exactly when the order complex of Q is t-connected. The same holds if t-connected is replaced by t-acyclic.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.1

returned_results.slogan: A simplicial complex covered by subcomplexes has uniformly acyclic properties if and only if its nerve is also uniformly acyclic. This holds under the condition that every non-empty finite intersection of the covering subcomplexes is a full simplex. The result links the topological structure of the complex to the combinatorial structure of its nerve.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.12

returned_results.slogan: A simplicial complex equals the union of a family of subcomplexes. If every finite intersection of these subcomplexes is sufficiently acyclic or connected, then the homology groups of the complex match those of its nerve up to a certain dimension. Alternatively, the complex is l-connected if and only if its nerve is l-connected. This holds under the stated connectivity conditions on the intersections.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.4 (Nerve Theorem)

returned_results.slogan: The Quillen Fiber Lemma applies to an order-preserving map between two posets. If for every element in the target poset, the preimage of all elements greater than or equal to it has a contractible order complex, then the induced map between the order complexes of the posets is a homotopy equivalence. This means the simplicial complexes of the two posets have the same homotopy type.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.1

returned_results.slogan: The forgetful map from a poset minus its maximum element to another poset minus its maximum element meets the condition of Quillen's Equivariant Fiber Lemma. For any partition in the target poset, the preimage of elements above it has an order complex that is the barycentric subdivision of a cone. This implies the order complex is contractible. It also implies the order complex is acyclic.
returned_results.name: Proposition 11.5

returned_results.slogan: The complex is highly acyclic under certain conditions. If the pair R and q satisfies a specific homological property, then the connectivity bound holds. The acyclicity degree depends linearly on the parameter n. The result relates algebraic structures to topological connectivity.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.1

returned_results.slogan: Under certain acyclicity and connectivity conditions on ascending living links, the preimage of any cube in a specified complex under the bundle projection is n-acyclic or n-connected. The same conclusion applies to descending living links.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.9

returned_results.slogan: The Nerve Theorem states that a simplicial complex is k-connected if and only if its nerve is k-connected, provided the complex is covered by subcomplexes and every non-empty finite intersection of these subcomplexes is sufficiently connected. The required connectivity for each intersection depends on the number of subcomplexes in that intersection. Specifically, an intersection of t subcomplexes must be k minus t plus 1 connected. This result relates the topological connectivity of a complex to the connectivity of its nerve complex under these intersection conditions.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.9

returned_results.slogan: A simplicial complex covered by subcomplexes is k-connected if and only if its nerve complex is k-connected. This holds when every non-empty intersection of t subcomplexes is (k-t+1)-connected for all t at least 1. The connectivity of the nerve complex and the original complex are equivalent under these intersection conditions. The result relates the topological connectivity of a space to the combinatorial connectivity of its covering nerve.
returned_results.name: Lemma 6.5

trajectory.query: join complex fin-rips highly acyclic complete join complex weakly Cohen-Macaulay

returned_results.slogan: A complete join complex over a weakly Cohen-Macaulay complex of dimension m is also weakly Cohen-Macaulay. The dimension of the resulting complex remains m. This property holds under the given join construction.
returned_results.name: Proposition 6.7

returned_results.slogan: A complete join complex over a simplicial complex of dimension n preserves the property of being weakly Cohen-Macaulay in the same dimension. If the underlying complex is weakly Cohen-Macaulay, then the join complex is also weakly Cohen-Macaulay. Additionally, if the join complex is k-connected for k at most n, then the original complex is also k-connected.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.7

returned_results.slogan: The map pi from Y to X is a join complex over X, with X being weakly Cohen-Macaulay of dimension n. For every p-simplex tau in Y, the image of the link of tau under pi is weakly Cohen-Macaulay of dimension n minus p minus 2. Under these conditions, Y is connected up to dimension n minus 2 over 2.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.7 (Hatcher--Wahl {\cite [Theorem 3.6]{hatcherwahl}})

returned_results.slogan: A minimal Cohen-Macaulay complex is acyclic. If a Cohen-Macaulay complex is i-fold acyclic and no facet contains more than i-1 boundary ridges, then it is minimal Cohen-Macaulay. For a ball, being minimal Cohen-Macaulay is equivalent to being strongly non-shellable. The join of a minimal Cohen-Macaulay complex with any Cohen-Macaulay complex is also minimal Cohen-Macaulay.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.2

returned_results.slogan: If Y is a complete join complex over a Cohen-Macaulay complex X of dimension n, then Y is also Cohen-Macaulay of dimension n. The same holds for weakly Cohen-Macaulay complexes.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.5

returned_results.slogan: If K is a complete join complex over a weakly Cohen-Macaulay complex L of dimension n, then K is also weakly Cohen-Macaulay of dimension n.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.14

returned_results.slogan: Suppose a complete join map exists from a complex to a base complex. If the base complex is weakly Cohen-Macaulay with dimension one greater than a given target connectivity, then the complex is also weakly Cohen-Macaulay with that same dimension.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.3

returned_results.slogan: If Y is a complete join complex over a wCM complex X of dimension n, then Y is also weakly Cohen-Macaulay of dimension n.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.4

returned_results.slogan: The join of two complexes is Cohen-Macaulay exactly when both individual complexes are Cohen-Macaulay. If one complex is Cohen-Macaulay and the other is CM_t for some t at least 1, then the join is CM with index equal to the dimension of the first complex plus t. This result is sharp, meaning the index cannot be improved. The property holds regardless of the dimension of the second complex.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.1

returned_results.slogan: Let Y be a join complex over a weakly Cohen-Macaulay complex X of dimension n. If the projected link of every p-simplex in Y is weakly Cohen-Macaulay of dimension n minus p minus 2, then Y is at least n over 2 minus 1 connected.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.6

trajectory.query: FI-complex highly acyclic criterion homology finitely generated torsion sequence highly acyclic

returned_results.slogan: An FI-complex sequence has highly acyclic simplicial complexes if each homology module is finitely generated and torsion. This holds for every degree of homology. The result applies uniformly across all terms in the sequence.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2

returned_results.slogan: A finitely generated FI^m-module is acyclic with respect to positive local cohomology functors exactly when it fits into a short exact sequence. In this sequence, the module is an extension of a semi-induced module by a B-torsion module. The semi-induced module appears as the quotient, and the B-torsion module is the kernel. This characterizes the acyclicity condition for such modules.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.10

returned_results.slogan: A bounded complex of FI-modules with finitely generated torsion cohomology groups is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated torsion FI-modules.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.3

returned_results.slogan: An FI_G-module generated in finite degree over a commutative ring has several equivalent properties. These include admitting a filtration with relatively projective cofactors or a series of surjections with relatively projective kernels. The module is homology acyclic, and its first homology group vanishes. It also has a finite resolution by homology acyclic objects generated in finite degree. If the module is presented in finite degree, vanishing of any positive-degree homology group is also equivalent.
returned_results.name: Theorem B

returned_results.slogan: Given a complex H that is acyclic with respect to a certain functor and whose derived module is torsion-free, and setting F as a specific complex derived from H, then for any constructible complex G, the derived Hom complex from G to F has cohomology that is entirely torsion.
returned_results.name: Lemma 5.7

returned_results.slogan: Let V be an FI-module. The homology group H_a of the complex tilde S_* V is a torsion FI-module for all a at least zero. If V is finitely generated over a Noetherian ring, then H_a of tilde S_* V is asymptotically zero for each a at least zero.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.25

returned_results.slogan: An FI_G-module presented in finite degree has a specific acyclicity pattern with respect to a sequence of functors. If it is acyclic for all functors up to a certain index but not for the next, then higher homology groups vanish beyond a certain point. For each positive integer, the homology at a particular index is nonzero. The vanishing and nonvanishing behavior follows a predictable shift based on the initial failure of acyclicity.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.2

returned_results.slogan: A torsion-free FI-module V is F-acyclic if its derivative DV is F-acyclic. This result connects the acyclicity of a module to that of its derivative. It holds under the condition that V has no torsion elements.
returned_results.name: Lemma 11

returned_results.slogan: A finitely generated module over a certain category is acyclic with respect to the torsion functor exactly when its torsion-free part is filtered by a specific property.
returned_results.name: Proposition 5.13

returned_results.slogan: A finitely generated FI-module over a Noetherian ring has vanishing higher torsion. For sufficiently large indices, all torsion components of the module become zero. This means the torsion functor applied to the module eventually yields trivial groups. The result holds uniformly beyond a certain point in the sequence.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.15

returned_results.slogan: If Y is a complete join complex over a Cohen-Macaulay complex X of dimension n, then Y is also Cohen-Macaulay of dimension n. The same holds for weakly Cohen-Macaulay complexes.

The result links the weak Cohen-Macaulay condition to high connectivity.
