trajectory.query: classification of torsion subgroups of elliptic curves over quadratic fields with full 2-torsion over K

returned_results.slogan: For an elliptic curve over a quadratic field with full 2-torsion, the possible torsion subgroups depend on the base group structure and the field discriminant. When the base group is isomorphic to Z/2Z plus Z/12Z or Z/2Z plus Z/10Z, the torsion subgroup remains the same. For base groups isomorphic to Z/2Z plus Z/8Z or Z/2Z plus Z/6Z, the torsion subgroup varies with the discriminant. If the base group is Z/2Z plus Z/4Z, the torsion subgroup depends on whether a certain square condition holds and on the discriminant. For the base group Z/2Z plus Z/2Z, the torsion subgroup is contained in a specific set of groups.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1

returned_results.slogan: For a quadratic cyclotomic field K and an elliptic curve E over K with a 2-torsion subgroup isomorphic to the cyclic group of order 2, the torsion subgroup over any quadratic extension L of K is classified. If K is the field of Gaussian rationals, the torsion subgroup is either cyclic of order 2n for n from 1 to 8 excluding 7, or the direct sum of two cyclic groups of orders 2 and 2n for the same n range, or the direct sum of cyclic groups of orders 3 and 6. If K is the field obtained by adjoining the square root of negative 3, the torsion subgroup can also be the direct sum of two cyclic groups of order 4.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.2

returned_results.slogan: For an elliptic curve over a quadratic field with all two-torsion points defined over that field, the torsion subgroup is either isomorphic to the direct sum of two cyclic groups of order four or to the direct sum of a cyclic group of even order and a cyclic group of order two. The even order in the second case ranges from two to twelve. If the torsion subgroup contains a subgroup isomorphic to the direct sum of two cyclic groups of order four, then the full torsion subgroup is exactly that structure. Similarly, if it contains a subgroup isomorphic to the direct sum of a cyclic group of order ten or twelve and a cyclic group of order two, then the full torsion subgroup has that form.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.3

returned_results.slogan: For an elliptic curve E over a field K in class S with trivial 2-torsion over K, the torsion subgroup over any quadratic extension L of K is isomorphic to a cyclic group of order 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, or 15, or to the direct sum of two cyclic groups of order 3, or to the direct sum of cyclic groups of orders 3 and 9. The group of order 3 direct sum 9 occurs only when K is the field of rational numbers adjoined with the square root of negative 2 or negative 11.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1

returned_results.slogan: For an elliptic curve over a quadratic field with full two-torsion, the possible torsion subgroups depend on the structure of the Galois group. If the group is isomorphic to Z/2Z plus Z/12Z, the torsion set contains Z/2Z plus Z/2Z and Z/2Z plus Z/4Z. For Z/2Z plus Z/10Z, the torsion set is only Z/2Z plus Z/2Z. The torsion sets vary with the discriminant D and the specific group structure, including cases for D equal to negative primes like 7, 11, 19, 43, 67, and 163.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.1

returned_results.slogan: The torsion subgroup of an elliptic curve over a quadratic field is isomorphic to one of 26 possible groups. These groups include cyclic groups of orders 1 through 18, excluding 17. They also include direct sums of cyclic groups of the form Z2 plus Z2m for m from 1 to 6, and Z3 plus Z3m for m equal to 1 or 2. Additionally, the group Z4 plus Z4 is possible.
returned_results.name: Theorem

returned_results.slogan: For a quadratic cyclotomic field K and an elliptic curve E over K, the torsion subgroup of E over the maximal elementary abelian 2-extensions of K is classified. When K is the field of Gaussian rationals, the torsion subgroup is isomorphic to one of several specific finite abelian groups. These groups include various cyclic and product groups with orders up to 15. When K is the field of cube roots of unity, the torsion subgroup may also be isomorphic to the direct sum of cyclic groups of orders 2 and 32.
returned_results.name: Theorem 11.1

returned_results.slogan: For an elliptic curve over a quadratic field, the torsion subgroup is isomorphic to one of 26 possible groups. These groups are cyclic groups of orders 1 through 18 except 17, direct sums of Z2 with Z2m for m from 1 to 6, direct sums of Z3 with Z3m for m equal to 1 or 2, or the group Z4 plus Z4.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.1

returned_results.slogan: The torsion subgroup of an elliptic curve over a quadratic field is isomorphic to one of 26 possible groups. These groups are cyclic groups of order m for m from 1 to 18, excluding 17. They also include direct sums of cyclic groups of orders 2 and 2m for m from 1 to 6, and orders 3 and 3m for m equal to 1 or 2. The final possibility is the direct sum of two cyclic groups of order 4.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1

returned_results.slogan: For an elliptic curve over a quadratic number field, the torsion subgroup of its rational points is isomorphic to one of 26 possible groups. These groups are cyclic groups of orders 1 through 18, excluding 17. They also include products of two cyclic groups with orders 2 and 2N for N from 1 to 6, orders 3 and 3N for N equal to 1 or 2, and the product of two cyclic groups of order 4.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.2 (\cite{KeMo}, \cite{Kamienny})

trajectory.query: possible growth of torsion of elliptic curves over quadratic extensions from Z/2 x Z/2 over quadratic imaginary fields

returned_results.slogan: For an elliptic curve over Q with square root of negative three having full 2-torsion, if the torsion subgroup over the base field is isomorphic to the direct sum of cyclic groups of orders 2 and 8, then it remains unchanged in all quadratic extensions. If the torsion subgroup is isomorphic to the direct sum of cyclic groups of orders 2 and 6, then there is at most one quadratic extension where it grows to the direct sum of cyclic groups of orders 4 and 6, and it remains the same in all other quadratic extensions. If the torsion subgroup is isomorphic to the direct sum of cyclic groups of orders 2 and 4, then there is a quadratic extension where it becomes the direct sum of cyclic groups of orders 4 and 4 under a specific condition, and at most two extensions where it becomes the direct sum of cyclic groups of orders 2 and 8. If the torsion subgroup is isomorphic to the direct sum of two cyclic groups of order 2, then in quadratic extensions it can grow to several possible structures, and growth occurs in at most three extensions.
returned_results.name: Theorem 18

returned_results.slogan: An elliptic curve over the rationals can have its torsion subgroup grow in at most four distinct quadratic extensions. The maximum number of such fields where the torsion subgroup is strictly larger than over the rationals is four. This result is expressed as the maximum size of a certain set related to torsion growth.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4

returned_results.slogan: For quadratic fields Q(i) or Q(sqrt(-3)), if an elliptic curve has torsion subgroup isomorphic to Z/2Z plus Z/2Z over the base field, then over any finite extension the torsion subgroup is isomorphic to one of several specific groups. These groups include those listed in four propositions and the group Z/4Z plus Z/4Z.
returned_results.name: Theorem 8.9

returned_results.slogan: For an elliptic curve over Q(i) with full 2-torsion, if the torsion subgroup is isomorphic to C2 plus C8, there is exactly one quadratic extension where it becomes C4 plus C8, and it remains C2 plus C8 in all others. If it is C2 plus C6, there are at most two quadratic extensions where it becomes C4 plus C6, and it stays C2 plus C6 elsewhere. If it is C2 plus C4, there is a unique quadratic extension where it becomes C4 plus C4, and at most two others where it becomes C2 plus C8. If it is C2 plus C2, the torsion can grow to several structures in quadratic extensions, with growth occurring in at most three extensions. If it is C4 plus C4, there is at most one quadratic extension where it grows to C4 plus C8.
returned_results.name: Theorem 19

returned_results.slogan: For an elliptic curve over the rationals, the number of quadratic extensions where the torsion subgroup grows beyond its rational value is bounded by a constant that depends only on the torsion group structure. The bound is explicitly listed for each possible torsion group. Some groups, like C7 and C9, have a bound of zero, meaning no such quadratic extensions exist. The maximum bound is 182 for the cyclic group of order 2.
returned_results.name: Corollary 7

returned_results.slogan: An elliptic curve defined over the rational numbers has at most four distinct quadratic fields where its torsion subgroup grows. The torsion subgroup over each such field is larger than the torsion over the rationals. These quadratic fields are pairwise non-isomorphic. The maximum number of such fields is exactly four.
returned_results.name: Corollary 1

returned_results.slogan: For a quadratic cyclotomic field K and an elliptic curve E over K with a 2-torsion subgroup isomorphic to the cyclic group of order 2, the torsion subgroup over any quadratic extension L of K is classified. If K is the field of Gaussian rationals, the torsion subgroup is either cyclic of order 2n for n from 1 to 8 excluding 7, or the direct sum of two cyclic groups of orders 2 and 2n for the same n range, or the direct sum of cyclic groups of orders 3 and 6. If K is the field obtained by adjoining the square root of negative 3, the torsion subgroup can also be the direct sum of two cyclic groups of order 4.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.2

returned_results.slogan: For an elliptic curve over certain quadratic fields with a torsion subgroup isomorphic to the direct sum of cyclic groups of orders 2 and 4, the torsion over a quadratic extension contains the direct sum of two cyclic groups of order 4 under specific conditions. When the base field has discriminant -3 and the extension is generated by the square root of -1, this occurs if there exists an algebraic integer such that the difference of two squares equals plus or minus its square. When the base field has discriminant -1, the condition is that the extension equals the field generated by the square root of that same difference.
returned_results.name: Lemma 17

returned_results.slogan: For an elliptic curve over a quadratic field with full 2-torsion, the possible torsion subgroups depend on the base group structure and the field discriminant. When the base group is isomorphic to Z/2Z plus Z/12Z or Z/2Z plus Z/10Z, the torsion subgroup remains the same. For base groups isomorphic to Z/2Z plus Z/8Z or Z/2Z plus Z/6Z, the torsion subgroup varies with the discriminant. If the base group is Z/2Z plus Z/4Z, the torsion subgroup depends on whether a certain square condition holds and on the discriminant. For the base group Z/2Z plus Z/2Z, the torsion subgroup is contained in a specific set of groups.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1

returned_results.slogan: For an elliptic curve over a quadratic field with all two-torsion points defined over that field, the torsion subgroup is either isomorphic to the direct sum of two cyclic groups of order four or to the direct sum of a cyclic group of even order and a cyclic group of order two. The even order in the second case ranges from two to twelve. If the torsion subgroup contains a subgroup isomorphic to the direct sum of two cyclic groups of order four, then the full torsion subgroup is exactly that structure. Similarly, if it contains a subgroup isomorphic to the direct sum of a cyclic group of order ten or twelve and a cyclic group of order two, then the full torsion subgroup has that form.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.3

trajectory.query: elliptic curve over quadratic field torsion Z/2Z x Z/2nZ n=1..6 classification

returned_results.slogan: For an elliptic curve over a quadratic number field, the torsion subgroup of its rational points is isomorphic to one of several cyclic or product groups. The cyclic groups range from order 1 to 18, excluding order 17. The product groups include Z/2Z plus Z/2N2Z for N2 from 1 to 6, Z/3Z plus Z/3N3Z for N3 equal to 1 or 2, or Z/4Z plus Z/4Z.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.6 (Kamienny \cite{kamienny}, Kenku, Momose \cite{kenkumomose})

returned_results.slogan: An elliptic curve over a quadratic field has a torsion subgroup that is one of 26 possible groups. These groups are cyclic groups of orders 1 through 16 or 18, or direct sums of two cyclic groups. The possible direct sums are of the form Z/2Z plus Z/2NZ for N from 1 to 6, Z/3Z plus Z/3NZ for N equals 1 or 2, or Z/4Z plus Z/4Z.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.2 (Kamienny-Kenku-Momose (1992))

returned_results.slogan: For an elliptic curve over a quadratic number field, the torsion subgroup of its rational points is isomorphic to one of 26 possible groups. These groups are cyclic groups of orders 1 through 18, excluding 17. They also include products of two cyclic groups with orders 2 and 2N for N from 1 to 6, orders 3 and 3N for N equal to 1 or 2, and the product of two cyclic groups of order 4.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.2 (\cite{KeMo}, \cite{Kamienny})

returned_results.slogan: The torsion subgroup of an elliptic curve over a quadratic number field is isomorphic to a cyclic group of order n, where n is between 1 and 18 but not 17. It can also be isomorphic to a direct sum of two cyclic groups, specifically Z2 plus Z2n for n from 1 to 6. Another possibility is Z3 plus Z3n for n equal to 1 or 2. The final possibility is the direct sum Z4 plus Z4.
returned_results.name: Theorem (Kamienny \cite{Kam92}, Kenku and Momose \cite{KM88})

returned_results.slogan: An elliptic curve over a quadratic number field has a torsion subgroup that is either cyclic or a product of two cyclic groups. The cyclic group can have order from 1 to 16 or order 18. The product of two cyclic groups can be of the form Z/2Z times Z/2MZ for M from 1 to 6, or Z/3Z times Z/3MZ for M equal to 1 or 2 only over Q(sqrt(-3)). The group Z/4Z times Z/4Z occurs only over Q(sqrt(-1)).
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.2 (Kenku, Momose \cite{kenmom}, Kamienny \cite{kamienny})

returned_results.slogan: For an elliptic curve over a quadratic field, the torsion subgroup is isomorphic to one of 26 possible groups. These groups are cyclic groups of orders 1 through 18 except 17, direct sums of Z2 with Z2m for m from 1 to 6, direct sums of Z3 with Z3m for m equal to 1 or 2, or the group Z4 plus Z4.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.1

returned_results.slogan: The torsion subgroup of an elliptic curve over a quadratic field is isomorphic to one of 26 possible groups. These groups include cyclic groups of orders 1 through 18, excluding 17. They also include direct sums of cyclic groups of the form Z2 plus Z2m for m from 1 to 6, and Z3 plus Z3m for m equal to 1 or 2. Additionally, the group Z4 plus Z4 is possible.
returned_results.name: Theorem

returned_results.slogan: An elliptic curve over a quadratic field has a torsion subgroup that is isomorphic to one of several cyclic groups or direct products of cyclic groups. The possible cyclic groups have orders from 1 to 16, or 18. The possible direct products include a cyclic group of order 2 with cyclic groups of orders 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, or 12. Other possibilities are a cyclic group of order 3 with a cyclic group of order 3 or 6, or a cyclic group of order 4 with another cyclic group of order 4.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.1

returned_results.slogan: For an elliptic curve over a quadratic field, the torsion subgroup is isomorphic to one of 26 possible groups. These include cyclic groups of orders 1 through 18 except 17. They also include groups of the form C2 direct sum C2n for n from 1 to 6, and C3 direct sum C3n for n equal to 1 or 2. The final possibility is the group C4 direct sum C4.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2

returned_results.slogan: An elliptic curve over the rationals has a torsion subgroup over a quadratic field that is either cyclic with order from 1 to 10, 12, 15, or 16, or a product of two cyclic groups with specific orders. The product group cases are either Z/2Z times Z/2MZ for M from 1 to 6, or Z/3Z times Z/3MZ for M equal to 1 or 2 only over Q(sqrt(-3)). The group Z/4Z times Z/4Z occurs only over Q(sqrt(-1)).
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.2 (Najman, \cite{najman}, Theorem 2)

trajectory.query: criterion for halving a 2-torsion point on elliptic curve with full 2-torsion x-coordinate differences are squares

returned_results.slogan: A point P with coordinates (x0, y0) on an elliptic curve E over a field K is divisible by 2 in the group of K-rational points if and only if the differences x0 minus each root of the cubic equation are squares in K.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.1

returned_results.slogan: A point on an elliptic curve is twice another point if and only if the differences between its x-coordinate and each root of the cubic are squares in the field. The curve is defined by a cubic equation in Weierstrass form with distinct roots. The field's characteristic is not 2 or 3. This condition characterizes when a point has a half point.
returned_results.name: Theorem 6.2

returned_results.slogan: A point P on an elliptic curve is divisible by 2 if and only if its x-coordinate is a square in the field. Additionally, there must exist an element l such that l squared plus l equals the sum of the x-coordinate and the curve coefficient a2. If the point has x-coordinate zero, then the curve constant a6 must be a fourth power. These conditions hold under the assumption that the curve already has a point of order 2.
returned_results.name: Theorem 10.3

returned_results.slogan: A point P on an elliptic curve E over a field K is divisible by 2 if and only if there exists a point Q such that 2Q equals P. This condition is equivalent to the existence of square roots of x0 minus the roots of the cubic such that their sum and a symmetric sum are both in K. It is also equivalent to the existence of such square roots where their product equals negative y0, and both the sum and symmetric sum are in K. These three statements are all equivalent conditions for P being twice another point.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2.6

returned_results.slogan: A point P with coordinates (x0, y0) on an elliptic curve E over a field K is divisible by 2 if and only if x0 minus a certain element x is a square in the field extension K_g. When this condition holds, x0 minus alpha is also a square in the base field K.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.1

returned_results.slogan: A point P on an elliptic curve over a field of characteristic not 2 or 3 is twice another point Q if and only if the differences between its x-coordinate and each root of the cubic are all squares in the field.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.1 (\cite{KN1992}, Theorem 4.2)

returned_results.slogan: A rational point P on an elliptic curve is twice another rational point Q if and only if the differences between its x-coordinate and each root of the curve are all rational squares.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2

returned_results.slogan: An algebraic number field contains an elliptic curve defined by a cubic equation in Weierstrass form. A rational point on this curve has a rational halving point if and only if the differences between its x-coordinate and each root of the cubic are all squares in the field.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.3 ({\cite[Theorem 4.2]{knap}})

returned_results.slogan: An elliptic curve is defined by a cubic equation with distinct roots. A point on the curve has a half-point in the field if and only if the differences between its x-coordinate and each root are all squares in that field. This characterizes when a point is divisible by two. The condition is both necessary and sufficient.
returned_results.name: Lemma 10

returned_results.slogan: A point P on an elliptic curve has a half point Q if and only if the differences between its x-coordinate and each root of the curve's polynomial are all squares in the base field.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.4 (\cite{knapp}, Theorem 4.2)

trajectory.query: elliptic curve y^2 = x(x+M)(x+N) point of order 4 exists iff M and N are squares

returned_results.slogan: An elliptic curve defined by specific parameters has points of finite order under certain conditions. Points of order four exist if negative m and n minus m are perfect squares, with coordinates given by expressions involving these square roots. Points of order eight exist if m and n satisfy conditions related to Pythagorean quadruples, and their coordinates are given by formulas involving natural numbers. Points of order three or six exist if m and n can be expressed using coprime integers a and b, with coordinates provided in terms of these integers. In all other cases, the only torsion points are the trivial ones with zero y-coordinate.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.1

returned_results.slogan: An elliptic curve over the rationals has a rational point of order four if and only if one of three specific pairs of numbers are both perfect squares. These pairs are formed from the roots of the cubic equation defining the curve. The pairs are negative e1 with e2, negative e2 with e3, and negative e3 with e1. Each number in the chosen pair must be a square integer.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.1 ({\cite{Ono1996}})

returned_results.slogan: Given a point P of infinite order on a specific elliptic curve, and positive integers m and n with an even product, the square of a certain expression equals the product of two terms under most conditions. If a is not congruent to 4 modulo 16, or the 2-adic order of x(P) is not 1, or m or n has a 2-adic order greater than 1, then the square equals B sub m+n times B sub absolute m-n. If a is congruent to 4 modulo 16, the 2-adic order of x(P) is 1, m has 2-adic order 1, and n is odd, then the square equals 4 times that product. In all cases, the expression is positive.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.5

returned_results.slogan: An elliptic curve defined by y squared equals x times x minus a times x plus b has a rational point of order four if and only if one of the pairs negative a and b, a and a plus b, or negative b and negative a minus b are both perfect squares of integers. The curve has a rational point of order three if and only if there exist integers d, u, and v with u and v coprime, such that d squared times u cubed times u plus two v equals negative a and d squared times v cubed times v plus two u equals b. The ratio u over v must not be in the set containing negative two, negative one half, negative one, one, or zero.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.4 ({\cite{Ono1996}})

returned_results.slogan: An elliptic curve has a rational point of order four if and only if it can be written in a specific form. The point with coordinates (f, ef) is such a point of order four. The quotient curve by the subgroup generated by this point also has a similar equation. If the field contains a square root of negative one, the quotient curve also has a rational point of order four.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.2

returned_results.slogan: An elliptic curve over the rationals with a point of order four defined over the maximal abelian extension, but without full four-torsion over that extension, has a specific model. This model is given by a particular Weierstrass equation. In this representation, either the constant term or a related discriminant-like expression is a nonzero perfect square in the rational numbers.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.4

returned_results.slogan: An elliptic curve over a number field with full 2-torsion can be written in a specific form. The curve has a point of order 4 if certain pairs of parameters are squares in the ring of integers. It has a point of order 8 if the parameters relate to a Pythagorean triple with fourth powers. The curve contains a point of order 3 if the parameters satisfy a given rational expression condition.
returned_results.name: Theorem 9

returned_results.slogan: An elliptic curve over a field K with a point of order four in its K-rational points has a j-invariant that is a nonzero fourth power in K. Conversely, for any nonzero fourth power c in K, there is an elliptic curve over K with j-invariant c that has a point of order four. This curve is unique up to K-isomorphism. The j-invariant being a fourth power characterizes the existence of such a point.
returned_results.name: Corollary 10.5

returned_results.slogan: Let M be the field Q(i). Consider an elliptic curve E over Q with no Q-rational points of order 2. If E over K has a point of order 4, then the discriminant of E is minus a rational square, the j-invariant has a specific rational parametrization, and the 4-torsion over L is isomorphic to the direct sum of two cyclic groups of order 4. Additionally, E over K has no points of order 8.
returned_results.name: Proposition 10

returned_results.slogan: Several conditions are equivalent for an elliptic curve. If any point Q with twice Q equal to W3 is in two times the curve over K, then the conditions hold. Alternatively, if any point R with four times R equal to W3 is in the curve over K, the conditions are also met. There also exist nonzero elements c and d in K, excluding specific values, such that lambda and negative lambda have certain square forms. When these hold, K contains the square root of negative one, and the curve over K includes all twelve points of order four.
returned_results.name: Proposition 6.4

trajectory.query: resolvent kernel derivative integrability against polynomial growth function Lévy process lemma

returned_results.slogan: The integral of a function with respect to a Levy process is differentiable under its parameter. The derivative can be interchanged with the integral under certain conditions. These conditions involve boundedness, measurability, and decay properties of the derivative of the integrand. The result holds almost surely for parameters in a bounded interval.
returned_results.name: Lemma 10.{4}

returned_results.slogan: A Lévy process with a Lévy measure and symbol satisfying a growth condition on the real part of its symbol has a continuously differentiable density. The gradient of this density is integrable. An upper bound on the L1 norm of the gradient is given in terms of an inverse function related to the symbol. This bound holds for all positive times.
returned_results.name: Proposition 7.1

returned_results.slogan: A Levy basis with a specific generating quadruple and finite moment condition is considered. A kernel function is defined with continuity and differentiability properties, along with left and right limits at zero. Under certain boundedness conditions on the derivative of the kernel, a process defined by an integral with respect to the Levy basis is expressed as the sum of its initial value, an integral of another process, and a jump term. This representation implies the sample paths have finite variation on compact intervals.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.1

returned_results.slogan: A Levy process with a density and a finite moment condition on its jump measure is considered. If a function is a weak solution to the generator equation and grows at most polynomially, then it must be a polynomial. The degree of the polynomial is bounded by the growth exponent. This establishes a Liouville property for the generator.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1

returned_results.slogan: The transition density for the Levy process with generator M^z has an L2 norm bounded by a finite function c(t) for each time t. The resolvent r^z_lambda is defined by integrating the density against an exponential decay. The Fourier transform of the resolvent is bounded by a constant divided by the sum of lambda and the absolute value of u raised to the power alpha. This bound holds uniformly in z.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2.8

returned_results.slogan: A finite variation Lévy process under certain assumptions leads to a function defined by a specific equation. This function has locally bounded weak derivatives in a given space. Using a main theorem and following a known procedure, the function is shown to solve a partial integro-differential equation.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.1

returned_results.slogan: Given a Levy measure with finite first moment, and a function with Lipschitz derivative, an integral involving the derivative difference equals an integral over a bounded interval plus a remainder term. The kernel function is defined piecewise using indicator functions and integrals of the Levy measure. The remainder term captures the contribution from large jumps beyond the truncation point. This decomposition holds for any positive truncation level and all real numbers.
returned_results.name: Lemma 5.3

returned_results.slogan: A locally integrable positive decreasing convex function with infinite initial value and a Levy measure second derivative has a resolvent. If the resolvent is continuously differentiable and bounded by a power function, then higher smoothness of the function implies higher smoothness of the resolvent. Under Doney's conjecture, the function and its resolvent have the same order of continuous differentiability for all natural numbers.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.8

returned_results.slogan: An operator is defined by an integral involving a function and its derivative with respect to a Lévy kernel. The kernel and its first two weak derivatives have bounded integrals of a specific form. Certain tail integrals of the kernel must be monotone in a specified way. Under these conditions, the operator generates a unique Feller semigroup and defines a stochastically monotone process.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.1

returned_results.slogan: A Levy process with certain regularity conditions and a density is considered. A measurable function bounded by a polynomial growth condition weakly solves the generator equation. There exists a continuous version of this function almost everywhere. This continuous version is invariant under the process's semigroup for all positive times.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.3

trajectory.query: nondecreasing function of polynomial growth integrable against partial derivative of q-resolvent density

returned_results.slogan: For any positive q and any non-decreasing function g with polynomial growth, the integral of the absolute value of g times the partial derivative of R with respect to its first argument is finite. Additionally, the function mapping y to the integral of H with respect to the measure Pi over positive reals also has polynomial growth.
returned_results.name: Lemma A.1

returned_results.slogan: The result holds under a growth condition on the density function. Specifically, the density must be bounded by a polynomial of degree at most r, where r is between zero and p minus q. This applies to any weak solution with initial condition in a p-th moment space and with density in a specified class. The conclusion is that equation (3) is satisfied.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.3

returned_results.slogan: For positive q and values x and u less than or equal to b, the resolvent measure of U is absolutely continuous with respect to Lebesgue measure. Its density is expressed as an integral formula involving q-scale functions and their derivatives. The expression includes an exponential term with an integral of a ratio of q-scale functions. The formula is valid for u between x and b and involves indicator functions and further integration over y.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.2

returned_results.slogan: For a complex number q outside a certain set and a measurable function f satisfying an integrability condition, an integral involving the q-resolvent density is bounded by a constant times the weighted integral of f. The function R^(q)f is well-defined and belongs to the space of continuous functions vanishing at infinity. The limit of R^(q)f as x tends to infinity equals a specific integral expression. The operator R^(q) is bounded on the space of continuous functions vanishing at infinity.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.1

returned_results.slogan: For x at least b and b at least zero, the derivative of v sub b of x equals a constant K plus a term involving an integral. The constant K is defined using the derivative of the function Phi at q plus r, divided by Phi at q plus r, plus an integral involving the measure mu to the power of q plus r. The function g of t and b is given by an expression involving t, the q-scale function at zero, and integrals of exponential and derivative terms. The note relates an integral expression to the q plus r resolvent measure density of negative X.
returned_results.name: Lemma 5.4

returned_results.slogan: The canonical resolvent of a locally square integrable function is non-negative and non-decreasing. Its integral from zero to t is always non-negative and non-decreasing. If the original function does not vanish on the interval, the integral is strictly positive. These properties hold for all nonzero real parameters.
returned_results.name: Corollary C.2

returned_results.slogan: Condition ref item cond-Reinte holds exactly when X has a bounded q-resolvent density r sub q for q greater than zero. This density satisfies an integral equation involving the expectation of an exponential integral of f applied to X sub t. Additionally, under condition ref item cond-Reinte, condition ref item cond-regular is equivalent to the continuity of the function mapping x to r sub q of x.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.2 (\cite {MR1406564})

returned_results.slogan: For all positive q and non-negative measurable functions f with f at zero equal to zero, the q-resolvent measure under the condition of no positive jumps is expressed as an integral involving the Laplace exponent and a kernel. The q-resolvent at zero is given by the normalized measure. For negative x, the resolvent decomposes into a part from the reflected process and an exponential term. For positive x, it decomposes into a part from the process killed at zero and an integral involving a Green's measure.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.1

returned_results.slogan: For an increasing function V starting at zero, the integral of V from the left against the differential of V raised to q minus one is bounded by a constant times V at time t raised to q. This holds for q greater than one. Similarly, for q between zero and one, the integral with a negative differential is bounded by a related constant times V at time t raised to q.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.1

returned_results.slogan: Under Assumption A, the q-resolvent density r_q exists for all q greater than zero. It is characterized by an integral transform involving a function f. A version of r_q is given by two equivalent integral expressions involving the Fourier transform and the real part of a complex function. The resolvent density is continuous and tends to zero as the absolute value of x goes to infinity.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.1

trajectory.query: convolution with Lévy measure preserves polynomial growth lemma

returned_results.slogan: A Levy process with a density and a finite moment condition on its jump measure is considered. If a function is a weak solution to the generator equation and grows at most polynomially, then it must be a polynomial. The degree of the polynomial is bounded by the growth exponent. This establishes a Liouville property for the generator.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1

returned_results.slogan: For a Lévy process with certain density and moment conditions, the semigroup applied to a polynomially bounded function satisfies a bound on its increments. This bound implies Hölder continuity of the semigroup on compact sets. The Hölder exponent depends on the process parameters and the growth rate of the function. The Hölder norm on large balls is controlled by a constant times the growth factor.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.1

returned_results.slogan: A one-dimensional Lévy process with certain regularity and moment conditions has an infinitesimal generator. If a polynomially bounded function is a weak solution to the generator equation, then that function must be a polynomial. The degree of the polynomial is at most the exponent in the bounding condition.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.2 (Liouville)

returned_results.slogan: A Levy process formed by subordinating Brownian motion has smooth transition semigroups under certain conditions. If a function grows at most polynomially, then applying the semigroup yields a smooth function. The smoothness holds for all positive times, and the derivatives are bounded on large balls. The bounds depend on the polynomial growth rate and the order of differentiation, but not on the function or the ball's radius.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.2

returned_results.slogan: A Lévy process with a Lévy measure and symbol satisfying a growth condition on the real part of its symbol has a continuously differentiable density. The gradient of this density is integrable. An upper bound on the L1 norm of the gradient is given in terms of an inverse function related to the symbol. This bound holds for all positive times.
returned_results.name: Proposition 7.1

returned_results.slogan: For a nonzero pure-jump Lévy process with finite variation and nonzero drift in a specific direction, the absolute value of its Lévy-Khintchine exponent grows at least linearly for large arguments. Under a lower bound condition on the Lévy measure involving a radial measure and spherical probability measure, the exponent's magnitude is bounded below by a function of the integrated radial measure. If a certain cone on the sphere has positive measure, the bound involves a constant depending on the cone's measure and its alignment with the direction. When the integrated radial measure satisfies a power-law condition, the exponent's growth is at least of polynomial order.
returned_results.name: Lemma 5.5

returned_results.slogan: A Levy process with certain regularity conditions and a density is considered. A measurable function bounded by a polynomial growth condition weakly solves the generator equation. There exists a continuous version of this function almost everywhere. This continuous version is invariant under the process's semigroup for all positive times.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.3

returned_results.slogan: A sequence of Levy measures converges to a Levy measure if and only if a lower bound inequality holds for all lower semicontinuous functions with quadratic growth bounds. Equivalently, the convergence holds if and only if an upper bound inequality holds for all upper semicontinuous functions with quadratic growth bounds. These conditions characterize convergence in the space of Levy measures.
returned_results.name: Lemma C.3 (Portmanteau-type lemma for $\Lambda $-weak convergence)

returned_results.slogan: The Levy measure satisfies a finite integral condition. An inequality bounds the integral of the difference between a function evaluated at shifted arguments and its linear approximation. The bound involves two terms: one scaled by the square of the difference in parameters and another by the absolute difference. A special case simplifies when one parameter is zero.
returned_results.name: Lemma \thesection .3 (Lemma 1.4 in \cite{LT})

returned_results.slogan: A one-dimensional Lévy process with a Lévy measure satisfying a moment condition of order Q is considered. For any polynomial f of degree at most Q that vanishes at zero, the expected value of an integral involving f and the process increments is given. This expectation equals a specific expression involving the exponential function and the integral of f with respect to the Lévy measure. The result holds for all positive times t and parameters alpha.
returned_results.name: Lemma 7.2

The integrals involve inner products with polynomials and martingales derived from the process. The result holds for each time t in a given interval.

The limit is taken as lambda tends to infinity over a set defined by B(z) exceeding A(z) times f of A(z). This holds for any finite measure with finite 1-energy.

returned_results.slogan: The depth of the quotient ring S over I equals the minimum depth of S over the radical of the colon ideal I colon f, where f ranges over all monomials not in I.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.3

returned_results.slogan: A homogeneous ideal I in a polynomial ring S has depth zero for the quotient S/I. The minimal graded free resolution of S/I ends with a free module F_n, which is a direct sum of shifted copies of S. The socle of S/I is isomorphic to a direct sum of shifted copies of the base field. The shifts in the socle are determined by subtracting n from the shifts in the last free module.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.6 ({\cite[Lemma 1.3]{soclefits}})

returned_results.slogan: The depth of the quotient ring R over I is zero.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2

returned_results.slogan: The depth of the quotient ring S over J equals d if and only if the depth of S over the quotient by the sum of I and H also equals d, where H is an ideal generated by square-free monomials of degree d plus one.
returned_results.name: Lemma 1.4

trajectory.query: soc star of basic PLP-polymatroidal ideal generated in degrees less than n theorem

returned_results.slogan: The symmetric and ordinary socles of a PLP-polymatroidal ideal of a given type are generated in degrees less than the number of variables.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.7

returned_results.slogan: The socle of a PLP-polymatroidal ideal is given by another ideal with shifted parameters. The parameters are reduced by one in specific components. The result involves the zero vector and standard basis vectors. This formula explicitly computes the socle in terms of the original ideal's parameters.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.13

returned_results.slogan: For a basic PLP-polymatroidal ideal of a given type, four conditions are equivalent. The socle of the ideal is nonzero. The quotient ring modulo powers of the ideal has limit depth zero. The analytic spread equals the number of variables. A set of inequalities involving the parameters must hold simultaneously.
returned_results.name: Corollary 3.5

returned_results.slogan: A PLP-polymatroidal ideal has maximal projective dimension if and only if two inequalities hold. The first inequality requires that for all indices i and j with 1 ≤ i ≤ j < n, the sum of beta_i and the b's from i+1 to j is at least alpha_j plus j+1 minus i. The second inequality requires that for all i from 1 to n, the sum of beta_i and the b's from i+1 to n is at least alpha_n plus n minus i. These conditions ensure the ideal achieves its highest possible projective dimension.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.15

returned_results.slogan: A basic PLP-polymatroidal ideal has depth zero if and only if several inequalities are satisfied. The parameters b sub i must all be at least one. For indices from two to n minus one, alpha sub i must be at most beta sub i minus one. Two further families of inequalities involving sums of beta and b parameters must also hold for all specified index ranges.
returned_results.name: Corollary 3.4

returned_results.slogan: Given a basic PLP-polymatroidal ideal of a specified type, its socle is also a basic PLP-polymatroidal ideal. The socle ideal has a modified type where the second tuple entries are each reduced by one. The third tuple remains unchanged except the last entry which decreases by one. The fourth tuple entries are all decreased by one.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.3

returned_results.slogan: A polymatroidal ideal I can be expressed as an intersection of powers of prime ideals and a power of the maximal ideal. The associated primes of S/I, excluding the maximal ideal, are p1 through pr. There exist positive integers a1 through ar and a nonnegative integer s such that I equals the intersection of p1 raised to a1 through pr raised to ar intersected with m raised to s. If s is positive, then I is generated in degree s.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.1

returned_results.slogan: The depth of the quotient ring S over a PLP-polymatroidal ideal I is determined by the maximum value of a function N applied to exponent vectors of the minimal generators. This maximum is computed over all generators of the ideal. The depth equals the dimension n minus one minus this maximum value.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.3

returned_results.slogan: The ideal's homological shift of degree n minus one is also a PLP-polymatroidal ideal.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.14

returned_results.slogan: The socle of a specific LP-polymatroidal ideal with maximal projective dimension equals the product of certain prime ideals. This product is taken over intervals defined by the given sequences. The result confirms a particular question about such ideals. Additionally, the ideal's highest symbolic power is also a transversal polymatroidal ideal.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.22

trajectory.query: Tor regularity bound from local cohomology regularity over noetherian connected graded algebra with balanced dualizing complex Römer inequality t_i(M) <= CMreg(M)+t_i(k)

returned_results.slogan: For a noetherian graded algebra with semisimple degree zero part and a balanced dualizing complex, the Tor-regularity of a bounded derived graded module with finite projective dimension is bounded above. This bound is the sum of the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity and the Ext-regularity of the algebra as a left module over itself.
returned_results.name: Proposition 5.4

returned_results.slogan: The Tor regularity of an object X is bounded above by the sum of its CM regularity and the Tor regularity of the residue field. The CM regularity of X is bounded above by the sum of its Tor regularity and the CM regularity of the algebra. The AS regularity of the algebra is nonnegative. These inequalities hold for a noetherian connected graded algebra with balanced dualizing complex.
returned_results.name: Theorem 0.3

returned_results.slogan: For a noetherian connected graded algebra with balanced dualizing complex, and a finitely generated graded left module that is s-Cohen-Macaulay, the i-th torsion number of the module is bounded above by the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of the module minus s plus the (i+s)-th torsion number of the residue field. Under an additional hypothesis for the algebra, the i-th torsion number of the module is bounded above by the a-invariant of the module plus the (i+s)-th torsion number of the residue field.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.7

returned_results.slogan: For a noetherian connected graded algebra with balanced dualizing complex, consider a nonzero object in the bounded derived category of finitely generated graded modules with finite projective dimension. The Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of the object equals the sum of its Tor-regularity and the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of the algebra. This equality holds under the stated conditions.
returned_results.name: Theorem 0.7 (Theorem~ \ref{zzthm2.8})

returned_results.slogan: Let A be a noetherian connected graded algebra with a balanced dualizing complex, and let X be a nonzero object in the bounded derived category of finitely generated graded A-modules. The Tor-regularity of X is at most the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of X plus the Tor-regularity of the residue field. The Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of X is at most the Tor-regularity of X plus the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of A.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.5

returned_results.slogan: For a noetherian connected graded algebra with a balanced dualizing complex and nonzero object X, the Tor-regularity and Ext-regularity with respect to a positive parameter xi are equal. This common value is at most the sum of the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of X and the Tor-regularity of the residue field.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.3

returned_results.slogan: The Tor-regularity of a module over a connected graded noetherian algebra is bounded by the sum of the Tor-regularities of the algebra and the module. Under the assumption that the algebra is linear over T, several inequalities and equalities hold for the twists in the Tor functors. These relate the homological invariants of A and T, including their Tor-regularities. As a consequence, A is Koszul if and only if T is Koszul.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.3

returned_results.slogan: Under certain hypotheses, if R equals T to the H, and S is a noetherian AS regular algebra mapping to R with R finitely generated over S on both sides, and n is the global dimension of T, then the t-invariant of R over S at index i is bounded above by the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of T minus n plus the t-invariant of the base field over S at index i plus n. This is further bounded above by the t-invariant of the base field over S at index i plus n minus n. The inequalities hold for all i greater than or equal to zero.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.8

returned_results.slogan: If a module M has finite length, then the regularity of the i-th Tor module of M and N over R is bounded by the regularity of M plus a term t_i(N). Specifically, the regularity of Tor_i^R(M, N) is at most the sum of the regularities of M and N plus the index i.
returned_results.name: Lemma 1.5

returned_results.slogan: The regularity of the Tor module for Borel-fixed ideals I and J is bounded above. The bound depends on the homological degree t, the regularity of I, and the regularity of S over J. The expression is linear in t and involves the sum of regularities of I and S over J.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.5

trajectory.query: if M is s-Cohen-Macaulay then Ext or local duality shift relating CMreg(M) and a-invariant a(M)

returned_results.slogan: Let R be a local ring with dimension d and an ideal a of height c. Let M be a nonzero finitely generated R-module with vanishing Tor modules involving the dual of a. Then, the Ext modules of M tensored with the dual of a are isomorphic to the Ext modules of M with the completion of R. Additionally, the supremum of indices where Ext of M and R is nonzero equals the depth of R minus the depth of M. The module M is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if the local cohomology of M tensored with the dual of a vanishes for all indices not equal to c minus the grade of M.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.13

returned_results.slogan: Let R be a local ring with a proper ideal a, and assume R is a-relative Cohen-Macaulay. For all a-relative maximal Cohen-Macaulay R-modules M, the Ext groups vanish in nonzero degrees when computed with a specific dualizing module. The Hom module from M into this dual is also an a-relative maximal Cohen-Macaulay module. Applying the Hom functor twice with this dual yields a module isomorphic to M.
returned_results.name: Corollary 0.38

returned_results.slogan: For a graded Cohen-Macaulay ideal I in S, the a-invariant of S/I equals the regularity of S/I minus the depth of S/I minus the sum over i of d_i minus one. This also equals the regularity of S/I plus the height of I minus the sum of the d_i.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.4

returned_results.slogan: For a local ring with a dualizing complex and a Cohen-Macaulay complex M, the dimension of the canonical module K_M equals the dimension of M plus the supremum of M. The depth of K_M equals the dimension of M plus the infimum of M. The canonical module K_M is Cohen-Macaulay exactly when M is a module up to a shift.
returned_results.name: Corollary 3.10

returned_results.slogan: For a complete Cohen-Macaulay local ring of dimension d with a canonical module, if a module M is generalized Cohen-Macaulay of dimension t, then the Ext module of M and the canonical module in degree d minus t is also generalized Cohen-Macaulay.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.7

returned_results.slogan: A complete Cohen-Macaulay ring of dimension d has a natural isomorphism between Ext modules and Hom of local cohomology with the injective envelope of the residue field. For any module M and integer i, Ext^i of M with the canonical module is isomorphic to Hom of the local cohomology module H_m^{d-i} of M with E(k). If M is finitely generated, the local cohomology module H_m^{d-i} of M is also isomorphic to Hom of Ext^i of M with the canonical module with E(k). This provides a duality between Ext and local cohomology in this setting.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.10 (Grothendieck local duality)

returned_results.slogan: A maximal Cohen-Macaulay module M with vanishing local cohomology outside grade c yields an isomorphism between H_m^d of H_I^c(M) and H_m^n(M), with other local cohomology vanishing. Similarly, Ext^d_R(k, H_I^c(M)) is isomorphic to Ext^n_R(k, M), and lower Ext groups vanish. If R is also Cohen-Macaulay, then the canonical module of the completion of M is isomorphic to Ext^c_R(H_I^c(M), the canonical module of the completion of R), and higher Ext groups vanish.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.3

returned_results.slogan: Given a Noetherian local ring R and a finitely generated R-module C with depth r, assume there is a Cohen-Macaulay module M of dimension s such that an inequality involving multiplicities and an Ext module holds, and certain higher Ext modules vanish. Then R is Cohen-Macaulay and C is a maximal Cohen-Macaulay module with finite injective dimension. Furthermore, every Cohen-Macaulay R-module of dimension s also satisfies the same conditions as M.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.2 (Theorem \ref {main thm})

returned_results.slogan: For a proper ideal a in a ring R and an integer n between 0 and the cohomological dimension c of a, assume R is a-relative Cohen-Macaulay. For any module M in the class CM^n_a(R), the Ext group from M to the canonical module is nonzero only in degree c-n, where it equals the Hom from the n-th local cohomology of M to a direct sum of injective hulls. The local cohomology of that Ext module is nonzero only in degree n, where it equals the Hom from M to the a-torsion part of that injective sum. The double Ext of that Ext module with the canonical module is isomorphic to the tensor product of M with a product of completions at maximal ideals containing a.
returned_results.name: Theorem 0.23

returned_results.slogan: The a-invariant of S is at least negative one, and the a-invariant of the canonical module of S is at least zero. These bounds become equalities when S is locally Cohen-Macaulay on X.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.2

trajectory.query: balanced dualizing complex local duality Cohen-Macaulay module a-invariant Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity

returned_results.slogan: A Cohen-Macaulay local ring with a dualizing complex is regular if all its maximal Cohen-Macaulay modules have finite injective dimension.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.10

returned_results.slogan: Let R be a local ring with a proper ideal a, and assume R is a-relative Cohen-Macaulay. For all a-relative maximal Cohen-Macaulay R-modules M, the Ext groups vanish in nonzero degrees when computed with a specific dualizing module. The Hom module from M into this dual is also an a-relative maximal Cohen-Macaulay module. Applying the Hom functor twice with this dual yields a module isomorphic to M.
returned_results.name: Corollary 0.38

returned_results.slogan: The a-invariant of R over I is at most the regularity minus the depth of R over I. Equality holds when R over I is Cohen-Macaulay.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.20

returned_results.slogan: A noetherian local-Cohen-Macaulay DG-ring with a dualizing DG-module implies that the dualizing module is itself Cohen-Macaulay. This result holds under the given conditions.
returned_results.name: Proposition 6.3

returned_results.slogan: For a Cohen-Macaulay local ring, two conditions are equivalent. The ring is regular local. This is equivalent to the a-invariant of the associated graded ring being equal to the negative of the dimension of the ring.
returned_results.name: Theorem 6.1

returned_results.slogan: Let R be a local ring with a dualizing complex. Suppose C is a semidualizing module and M is a nonzero finitely generated R-module. If either the C-quasi-projective dimension and injective dimension of M are finite, or the C-quasi-injective dimension and projective dimension of M are finite, then R is Cohen-Macaulay. Moreover, the canonical module of R is isomorphic to C.
returned_results.name: Theorem 7.8

returned_results.slogan: The a-invariant of S is at least negative one, and the a-invariant of the canonical module of S is at least zero. These bounds become equalities when S is locally Cohen-Macaulay on X.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.2

returned_results.slogan: For a Cohen-Macaulay local ring with a dualizing complex, let M be a finitely generated module of dimension d and finite projective dimension p. The module M is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if a certain local cohomology group with coefficients in the canonical module is nonzero. This is also equivalent to the nonvanishing of the same local cohomology group with coefficients in the dualizing complex.
returned_results.name: Corollary 3.5

returned_results.slogan: A noetherian local-Cohen-Macaulay DG-ring with a dualizing DG-module has a bounded complex of finite modules whose amplitude equals that of the ring. This complex is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if the amplitude of its derived hom into the dualizing module also equals the ring's amplitude. When this condition holds, the derived hom complex is also Cohen-Macaulay.
returned_results.name: Proposition 6.2

returned_results.slogan: For a Cohen-Macaulay module M over a ring R, there are integers c and d such that the a-invariant of the local cohomology module H^k_Q(M) in degree j is bounded below by c times j plus d, for all k and all j.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2.11

trajectory.query: s-Cohen-Macaulay module CMreg equals Ext.reg plus s or CMreg equals a-invariant under hypothesis 2.7

returned_results.slogan: A Noetherian local ring R is Cohen-Macaulay under certain conditions on a finitely generated module C and a Cohen-Macaulay module M. If the depth of C is r and M has dimension s, and two specific conditions involving Ext modules and multiplicities hold, then R is Cohen-Macaulay. Additionally, C is a maximal Cohen-Macaulay module with finite injective dimension. These conditions also hold for any other Cohen-Macaulay R-module of dimension s.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.4

returned_results.slogan: Given a Noetherian local ring R and a finitely generated R-module C with depth r, assume there is a Cohen-Macaulay module M of dimension s such that an inequality involving multiplicities and an Ext module holds, and certain higher Ext modules vanish. Then R is Cohen-Macaulay and C is a maximal Cohen-Macaulay module with finite injective dimension. Furthermore, every Cohen-Macaulay R-module of dimension s also satisfies the same conditions as M.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.2 (Theorem \ref {main thm})

returned_results.slogan: For a noetherian connected graded algebra with balanced dualizing complex, and a finitely generated graded left module that is s-Cohen-Macaulay, the i-th torsion number of the module is bounded above by the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of the module minus s plus the (i+s)-th torsion number of the residue field. Under an additional hypothesis for the algebra, the i-th torsion number of the module is bounded above by the a-invariant of the module plus the (i+s)-th torsion number of the residue field.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.7

returned_results.slogan: For a Cohen-Macaulay module M and an ideal I in an equicharacteristic Noetherian local ring with infinite residue field, let H and J be minimal and general minimal reductions of I on M. If the length of M over IM is finite, then the s-invariant for H is less than or equal to that for J, and the s-invariant for J is independent of the choice of J. Under additional conditions on dimension, the G_d and AN^-_{d-2} conditions, and depth, the s-invariant for J remains independent of J, and the s-invariant for H is again bounded above by that for J.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.2

returned_results.slogan: The a-invariant of a quotient ring S by I is at most the regularity minus the depth. Equality holds when the quotient ring is Cohen-Macaulay.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.6

returned_results.slogan: For a Cohen-Macaulay local domain S with a finitely generated module M, if the height of the annihilator of M is h, then the h-th Ext module of M and S satisfies the Serre condition S2 over its support.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.4

returned_results.slogan: For a Cohen-Macaulay local domain S with a finitely generated module M, if the height of the annihilator of M is h, then the h-th Ext module of M and S satisfies the Serre condition S2 over its support.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.4

returned_results.slogan: The a-invariant of R over I is at most the regularity minus the depth of R over I. Equality holds when R over I is Cohen-Macaulay.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.20

returned_results.slogan: In a Cohen-Macaulay local ring with a canonical module, for any Cohen-Macaulay ideal I, there exists a Cohen-Macaulay ideal J contained in I. The delta invariant of certain Ext modules with respect to R over J vanishes for all nonnegative integers i. In particular, the delta invariant of a specific local cohomology module also vanishes. This holds for a specific integer s defined by the minimal number of generators and height of I.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.2

returned_results.slogan: The a-invariant of the quotient ring S by a graded ideal I is at most the regularity minus the depth of S/I. Equality holds when S/I is Cohen-Macaulay.
returned_results.name: Theorem 8.11

trajectory.query: Hypothesis 2.7 implies CMreg(M)=a(M)+s for s-Cohen-Macaulay module

returned_results.slogan: Given a Noetherian local ring R and a finitely generated R-module C with depth r, assume there is a Cohen-Macaulay module M of dimension s such that an inequality involving multiplicities and an Ext module holds, and certain higher Ext modules vanish. Then R is Cohen-Macaulay and C is a maximal Cohen-Macaulay module with finite injective dimension. Furthermore, every Cohen-Macaulay R-module of dimension s also satisfies the same conditions as M.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.2 (Theorem \ref {main thm})

returned_results.slogan: A Noetherian local ring R is Cohen-Macaulay under certain conditions on a finitely generated module C and a Cohen-Macaulay module M. If the depth of C is r and M has dimension s, and two specific conditions involving Ext modules and multiplicities hold, then R is Cohen-Macaulay. Additionally, C is a maximal Cohen-Macaulay module with finite injective dimension. These conditions also hold for any other Cohen-Macaulay R-module of dimension s.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.4

returned_results.slogan: For a Cohen-Macaulay local domain S with a finitely generated module M, if the height of the annihilator of M is h, then the h-th Ext module of M and S satisfies the Serre condition S2 over its support.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.4

returned_results.slogan: For a Cohen-Macaulay local domain S with a finitely generated module M, if the height of the annihilator of M is h, then the h-th Ext module of M and S satisfies the Serre condition S2 over its support.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.4

returned_results.slogan: Assume R is Cohen-Macaulay and M is a finite module satisfying the second Serre condition. If either the special dimension of R is positive and certain localizations of M are maximal Cohen-Macaulay, or R satisfies a special dimension condition, then M is maximal Cohen-Macaulay.
returned_results.name: Corollary 3.11

returned_results.slogan: M of rho is Cohen-Macaulay as a module over M of H.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.3

returned_results.slogan: An M-regular sequence in an ideal I of a Noetherian local ring R implies that M is I-Cohen Macaulay exactly when the quotient of M by the submodule generated by the sequence is Cohen Macaulay over the corresponding quotient ring with respect to the image of I.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.10

returned_results.slogan: The module with the given notation is Cohen-Macaulay. This means it satisfies certain homological conditions related to depth and dimension. The property holds for the specified parameters.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.16

returned_results.slogan: For a Cohen-Macaulay module M and an ideal I in an equicharacteristic Noetherian local ring with infinite residue field, let H and J be minimal and general minimal reductions of I on M. If the length of M over IM is finite, then the s-invariant for H is less than or equal to that for J, and the s-invariant for J is independent of the choice of J. Under additional conditions on dimension, the G_d and AN^-_{d-2} conditions, and depth, the s-invariant for J remains independent of J, and the s-invariant for H is again bounded above by that for J.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.2

returned_results.slogan: A finitely generated module M over a ring S has an annihilator containing a homogeneous ideal J. If S/J is Cohen-Macaulay with codimension equal to its projective dimension and its first twist is at least 2, then the regularity of M is bounded above. The bound is given by a maximum over certain indices and multi-indices involving twists of M and S/J. The expression also includes the c-th twist of S/J minus the projective dimension of M.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.3

trajectory.query: Brown criterion finiteness properties filtration cocompact subcomplexes connectivity of pairs implies type F_n

returned_results.slogan: Brown's finiteness criterion states that if a group acts on an n minus one connected CW-complex with a cellular action and a suitable filtration, then the group is of type F sub n. The filtration must cover the complex, have invariant n-skeletons with cocompact group actions, and satisfy connectivity and stabilizer conditions. Specifically, each p-cell stabilizer must be of type F sub n minus p, and the filtration subsets must eventually be n minus one connected. These conditions together imply the group's finiteness property.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.15

returned_results.slogan: Brown's finiteness criterion states that if a group G acts cellularly on an (n-1)-connected CW-complex X, and there exists a filtration of X satisfying certain connectivity, invariance, and cocompactness conditions, along with stabilizer finiteness properties, then G is of type F_n. The filtration must cover X, with each skeleton invariant under G and the action cocompact. Each p-cell stabilizer must have type F_{n-p}. For large indices, the filtration stages must also be (n-1)-connected.
returned_results.name: Theorem 7.3

returned_results.slogan: Brown's Finiteness Criterion states that if a group G acts cellularly on an (n-1)-connected CW-complex X, and there exists a filtration of X satisfying certain conditions, then G is of type F_n. The filtration must cover X, with each n-skeleton invariant under G and acted on cocompactly. Additionally, each p-cell stabilizer must have type F_{n-p}, and for large enough indices, the filtration subsets must be (n-1)-connected. These conditions together ensure the group has finite type up to dimension n.
returned_results.name: Theorem 9.1

returned_results.slogan: A group acting on a highly connected CW-complex with certain stabilizer conditions is of type F_n if and only if a filtration of the complex by finite modulo G subcomplexes is essentially highly connected. The stabilizer of each k-cell must be of type F_{n-k}. The CW-complex is assumed to be n-1 connected. The filtration must consist of subcomplexes that are finite modulo the group action.
returned_results.name: Theorem 6.1 (Brown’s Criterion)

returned_results.slogan: A countable group acting properly on a contractible CW-complex with a filtration by invariant cocompact subcomplexes is of type F_n if and only if the filtration is essentially (n-1)-connected. Similarly, the group is of type FP_n if and only if the filtration is essentially (n-1)-acyclic.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.11 (Brown’s criterion)

returned_results.slogan: Let G be a group and X an (n-1)-connected G-CW complex. Suppose for each i-cell c, the stabilizer G_c has type F_{n-i}, and there is a G-filtration of X such that each quotient G\X_i has finite n-skeleton. Then G has type F_n if and only if the filtration is essentially (n-1)-connected.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.13 (Brown’s Finiteness Criterion)

returned_results.slogan: A group G is of type F-F_n if and only if, under certain conditions, a filtration of an F-n-good G-CW-complex by finite n-type subcomplexes is pi_k-F-essentially trivial for each k less than n. The forward implication holds without extra assumptions. The reverse implication requires that the complex has a G-finite 0-skeleton. This provides a criterion for the finiteness property F-F_n.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.2

returned_results.slogan: Brown's theorem states that for a group Gamma and an n-good Gamma-complex X with a filtration of finite n-type, Gamma is of type FP_n if and only if the directed system from the filtration is H_k-essentially trivial for all k less than n.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.1

returned_results.slogan: A group acting on a highly connected space with certain stabilizer types is of type F_n exactly when a cocompact filtration of the space is essentially highly connected.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.3 (Brown’s criterion)

returned_results.slogan: Brown's finiteness criterion states that if a group G acts cellularly on a contractible CW-complex X, and there exists an increasing sequence of invariant subcomplexes whose union is X, such that G acts cocompactly on each with finite cell stabilizers, and each subcomplex becomes highly connected as the index increases, then G is of type F infinity.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.1

trajectory.query: Bestvina Brady Morse lemma descending links sublevel sets connectivity

returned_results.slogan: Given a Bestvina-Brady discrete Morse function on a simplicial complex, if the descending link of every vertex in a certain value range is highly connected, then the inclusion between sublevel sets induces isomorphisms in homotopy groups up to a certain dimension and an epimorphism in the next dimension.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.3 (Morse Lemma)

returned_results.slogan: A Morse function on a simplicial complex yields connectivity results for level sets based on the connectivity of descending links. If the descending link of each vertex at a given height is at least (k-1)-connected, then the pair of sublevel sets up to and below that height is k-connected. This connectivity implies that the inclusion map induces isomorphisms on homotopy groups below dimension k and an epimorphism in dimension k. The same conclusion holds if the condition on descending links applies to all vertices at or above the given height.
returned_results.name: Lemma

returned_results.slogan: Given a Morse function on a space, if for vertices within a certain range the descending links are highly connected, then the pair of sublevel sets is also highly connected. Specifically, the relative homotopy groups up to a certain dimension are isomorphisms or epimorphisms. This holds under the connectivity assumptions on the descending links. The result relates the local structure at vertices to the global connectivity of the sublevel sets.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.11

returned_results.slogan: A Morse function on a complex has sublevel sets defined by its values. If the descending link of every vertex with function value between s and t is contractible, then the inclusion from the lower sublevel set to the higher one is a homotopy equivalence. Similarly, if the descending link of every vertex above t is contractible, then the inclusion from the sublevel set at t into the whole complex is also a homotopy equivalence. This relates the topology of sublevel sets to local combinatorial properties.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.3 (Morse Lemma)

returned_results.slogan: An ascending-type Morse function on an affine cell complex yields an essentially (m-1)-connected filtration under certain connectivity conditions on vertex links. returned_results.slogan: Given an affine cell complex with an ascending-type Morse function, if the ascending links of vertices in a certain height range are highly connected, then the inclusion between subcomplexes above certain heights induces isomorphisms and surjections in homotopy groups up to a dimension. Similarly, for a descending-type Morse function, if the descending links in a height range are highly connected, then the inclusion between subcomplexes below certain heights induces analogous maps in homotopy groups. The result holds for both ascending and descending cases with appropriate adjustments to the height conditions.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.3 (Morse Lemma)

returned_results.slogan: Given an n-connected polyhedron complex X and a Morse function f from X to the reals, suppose there is a real number h0 such that the descending link of every vertex at height at least h0 is n-connected. Then the preimage of negative infinity to h0 under f is n-connected.

returned_results.slogan: A discrete height function on a space X has descending links above a level s that are m-connected. This condition implies that the inclusion of the subspace up to level s into the full space induces isomorphisms in homotopy groups up to dimension m. Additionally, it induces an epimorphism in the homotopy group of dimension m+1.

returned_results.slogan: For any vertex v in the set E_m minus VE_m, the mu-descending link of v is connected up to a certain dimension. This connectivity is given by an expression involving nu of mu_1 of v and a logarithm base two of m minus mu_1 of v, minus two. Specifically, the connectivity is at least the smaller of nu of m over two minus two and log base two of m over two minus two.

returned_results.slogan: Given a discrete Morse function on an affine cell complex, if for every zero-cell in a certain sublevel set the descending link is highly connected, then the inclusion between two sublevel sets induces isomorphisms on lower homotopy groups and an epimorphism on a specific higher group. Similarly, if for every zero-cell in another sublevel set the ascending link is highly connected, then a different inclusion induces the same homotopy group behavior. The conditions depend on real parameters bounding the function values. The result relates connectivity of links to homotopy properties of inclusions between subcomplexes.

The filtration must cover the complex, have invariant n-skeletons with cocompact group actions, and satisfy connectivity and stabilizer conditions. Specifically, each p-cell stabilizer must be of type F sub n minus p, and the filtration subsets must eventually be n minus one connected. These conditions together imply the group's finiteness property.

It states that for any positive alpha and beta between zero and two, a certain weighted exponential integral is finite. The supremum of this integral over functions with norm at most one is bounded by a constant depending on the domain. This supremum is finite if and only if alpha divided by four pi plus beta divided by two is less than or equal to one.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.4

returned_results.slogan: For two points with equal and opposite weights, if the minimum weight is positive and the function h meets a given condition, then the Moser-Trudinger functional is bounded below on a radial function space. returned_results.slogan: The sharp subcritical Moser-Trudinger inequality follows from the sharp critical version. If a certain constant is finite, then another related constant is also finite. An upper bound is provided for this constant in terms of the critical constant. A specific case gives a simplified bound when parameters take particular values.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.2

returned_results.slogan: For N at least 2 and F satisfying certain conditions, the Moser-Trudinger type functional MT is attained under several cases. If beta is in (0,1) and F is subcritical, then MT is attained. If beta is in (0,1) and F is critical with a specific lower bound, then MT is attained. For beta equal to 0 and F subcritical with a particular expansion near zero, MT is attained under coefficient conditions. For beta equal to 0 and F critical with both a lower bound and expansion, MT is attained under the same coefficient conditions.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1

returned_results.slogan: For N at least 2 and alpha between 0 and 1, there exists a function u with unit Sobolev norm such that a certain Moser-Trudinger type integral equals its supremum. In the subcritical case, this holds for beta below a threshold, with an additional lower bound when N equals 2. In the critical case, attainment occurs at beta equals beta_N for sufficiently small alpha. For N equals 2 and very small beta, the supremum is not attained regardless of alpha.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1

returned_results.slogan: For a smooth bounded domain in R^n and a point x_0 in the domain, the local Trudinger-Moser functional at x_0 equals an infimum over functions in the Sobolev space on the unit ball. This infimum involves an n-Dirichlet energy term minus the logarithm of the exponential integral. The result is adjusted by subtracting n times the natural logarithm of the n-harmonic radius at x_0. The equality holds under conditions where the exponential integrals diverge and the measures concentrate at x_0.

The concentration occurs in the sense of weak convergence to a Dirac measure at the critical point. The constant in the limit depends only on the dimension.

In the blow-up case, the solutions tend to negative infinity away from the blow-up points, and the associated measures converge to a sum of Dirac masses. The masses are quantized, taking values of 4π or 4π times one plus a parameter, depending on the location. The limiting parameter is a sum of such quantized values. An analogous result applies to bounded domains with Dirichlet boundary conditions.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.9

The limit function is expressed as a sum of logarithmic terms plus a bounded function. At each blow-up point, the gradient of a combination of the bounded function and distances to other points equals the negative gradient of the conformal factor. The blow-up masses are all 8π, and the nonlinear term converges weakly to a sum of Dirac masses at the blow-up points.

returned_results.slogan: The local mass of a sequence of blow-up solutions to the affine Toda system under certain conditions relates to an element of a specific set. Each component of the local mass equals the corresponding component of that element plus an even integer. The integer multiples are arbitrary. This holds for all indices in the index set.
