returned_results.slogan: A two-dimensional quaternion signal can be completely reconstructed using a specific integral formula. This formula involves the quaternion short-time Fourier transform of the signal. It also uses kernel functions and the original window function. The reconstruction is valid for all square-integrable quaternion-valued signals.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.4

trajectory.query: operator maps H^- tensor H^- to itself kernel expansion matrix coefficients t^l_{mn}(Z^{-1})

returned_results.slogan: The operator T_L applied to elements a_kmn yields a scalar multiple of a_kmn. The scalar is the negative square of the integer k minus m plus n. This result holds for all integer k and nonnegative integers m and n.
returned_results.name: Proposition 8.3

returned_results.slogan: The matrix elements of the operator T-lambda are expressed in terms of the basis of L-squared space over K. The formula involves the conjugate of n-hat evaluated at k, and the difference n-hat minus m-hat evaluated at h. It also includes a sum over elements l in K of lambda applied to a composition of functions phi and sigma with y, multiplied by the conjugate of the difference n-hat minus m-hat evaluated at l.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.1

returned_results.slogan: For any n in S and integer N at least zero, the operator T sub 2 comma n of z S from h zero perp to itself expands into a main part and a remainder. The main part involves sums with coefficients a plus k and a minus k applied to Fourier multipliers and their inverses. The coefficients and remainder are real analytic maps with a minus k equal to the conjugate of a plus k. A similar expansion holds for the transpose of the operator.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.8

returned_results.slogan: The operator defined by summing terms involving the conjugate of H polynomials acts on a specific subspace of the tensor product. Its action is scalar multiplication by the value negative k times the quantity n minus k plus one. This result holds when restricted to the singular part of the tensor power shifted by n minus two k.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.6

returned_results.slogan: For each pair of integers m and n, there exist maps T with superscripts plus and minus that send elements from a tensor product of spaces to harmonic function spaces of adjusted degrees. These maps are independent of the parameter a and are nonzero whenever the target space is nonzero. The action of an element z from a Lie algebra part on a specific K-type is given by a formula involving these T maps. The formula expresses the result as a weighted sum of images under the T maps, with coefficients that depend on a, m, n, and the dimensions p and q.
returned_results.name: Lemma

returned_results.slogan: The theorem states two operator equalities on a cohomology space. The first equality relates the operators T prime sub l, T star of l, and a matrix with entries l inverse and one. It also expresses T prime sub l as l to the k minus two times T l times S l inverse. The second equality relates S prime sub l to a matrix with entries l inverse and another l inverse. It expresses S prime sub l as l to the two times k minus two times S l inverse.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.1

returned_results.slogan: The inverse operator H sub z inverse equals the map sending x times negative p in L minus g to x tensor eta sub z of t to the negative p in bar L minus g. This holds for every z in the unit disk.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.12

returned_results.slogan: Applying the operator H(u) tensor H(1-N-u) tensor 1 times C(u,v) to f_{-1} equals applying H(u) tensor H(1-N-u) tensor 1 to a specific linear combination. This combination includes f_{-1} scaled by (z-1)(w+1)/(z w) and four summation terms. Each summation involves tensor products of basis vectors e_1 through e_N and e_{-1} or e_{-k}, with coefficients involving z and w. The result shows an equivalence between these two operator applications.
returned_results.name: Corollary 6

returned_results.slogan: The operator h inverse t times P sub k times h t equals a sum from ell equals zero to absolute k of t to the power negative absolute k plus ell times P sub k comma ell. Each P sub k comma ell is an s-fibred differential operator of order ell. For ell less than the ceiling of absolute k divided by two, P sub k comma ell vanishes on the diagonal. A similar expansion holds for h inverse t times bar P sub k times h t, with Getzler order at most two ell plus N equals zero of k.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.4

returned_results.slogan: The theorem relates a tensor product of operators to an inverse function evaluated at a ratio of parameters. It involves level-k weights and specific mappings between weight spaces. The result is expressed as the inverse of a function applied to a tensor product of vectors. The equation holds for parameters z1 and z2 and a weight lambda.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.10

trajectory.query: operator bar L^(n) equivariant U(2) times U(2) gl(2,H_C) tensor product H+ H+ or H- H-

returned_results.slogan: The operator bar L superscript n maps from the tensor product of two spaces to another tensor product space. It is equivariant under the action of the unitary group U 2 times U 2. It is also equivariant under the action of the Lie algebra gl 2 over the complexified quaternions. This equivariance holds for both group and algebra actions.
returned_results.name: Lemma 9

returned_results.slogan: For any two functions f1 and f2 in Zh, the function bar L superscript n applied to their tensor product is polynomial and lies in Zh plus tensor Zh plus. The operator bar L superscript n maps from a tensor product of certain spaces to another tensor product of spaces. This operator is equivariant under the actions of U2 times U2 and the complexified quaternion algebra gl2, H sub C.
returned_results.name: Proposition 11

returned_results.slogan: For any two elements in the Hilbert space H-, the function defined by the operator L-hat applied to their tensor product remains in the tensor product of H- with itself. The operator L-hat maps between specific tensor products of representation spaces. This mapping is equivariant under the action of the unitary group U(2) times U(2). It is also equivariant under the complexified quaternion algebra gl(2, H_C).
returned_results.name: Proposition 13

returned_results.slogan: The image of the operator L superscript 2 lies in the tensor product of H plus with itself. The map L superscript 2 from the tensor product of pi sub l superscript 0, H plus with pi sub r superscript 0, H plus to itself is gl 2, H sub C equivariant. If an element x in that space belongs to an irreducible component isomorphic to rho n, Zh plus tensor C to the n by n, then L superscript 2 acts on x by multiplication by a scalar mu sub n. The scalar mu sub n equals 1 when n is 1, and equals negative 1 to the n plus 1 power divided by n times n minus 1 when n is at least 2.
returned_results.name: Theorem 26

returned_results.slogan: The spaces F_n plus and F_n minus are invariant under the pi_nl actions of U(2) times U(2) and gl(2, H_C). Similarly, the spaces G_n plus and G_n minus are invariant under the pi_nr actions of U(2) times U(2) and gl(2, H_C).
returned_results.name: Proposition 23

returned_results.slogan: The pairing labeled F-inn-prod is invariant under the Lie algebra u(2,2) for the representations pi_nl with spaces F_n^+ and F_n^-. Similarly, the pairing labeled G-inn-prod is u(2,2)-invariant for pi_nr with spaces G_n^+ and G_n^-. The Lie algebra u(2,2) is a real form of gl(2, H_C) as defined in the reference u(2,2)-algebra.
returned_results.name: Theorem 27

returned_results.slogan: For any two elements in the positive holomorphic discrete series, the function defined by the operator L superscript n applied to their tensor product is polynomial and harmonic in each variable. This function belongs to the tensor product of two copies of the positive holomorphic discrete series. The operator L superscript n maps from the tensor product of two representations to itself. This mapping is equivariant with respect to the complexified quaternionic general linear algebra of degree two.
returned_results.name: Proposition

returned_results.slogan: The map L is equivariant with respect to the group GL(n, H)Sp(1). The space S^4 E* plus U*22 plus Lambda^4 E* contains all R in R where L(R) equals 6R. The space U*31 plus U*211 tensored with S^2 H contains all R in R where L(R) equals 2R. The space U*22 tensored with S^4 H contains all R in R where L(R) equals -6R.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.1

returned_results.slogan: The operator L superscript n maps the tensor product of two Hilbert spaces into itself. This map is equivariant with respect to the complexified quaternion general linear algebra. When applied to an element from an irreducible component, the operator acts by scalar multiplication. The scalar is a sum involving binomial coefficients and a function a superscript k minus one of n and p.
returned_results.name: Theorem

returned_results.slogan: The spaces H-plus, H-minus, V-plus, V-minus, V-prime-plus, and V-prime-minus are irreducible representations of the complexified Lie algebras gl(4,C) and sl(4,C). Each space has a unitary structure where the real form u(2,2) acts unitarily, defined by specific integrals over the three-sphere. A non-degenerate u(2,2)-invariant bilinear pairing exists between H-plus and H-minus, given by an integral expression independent of the radius parameter.
returned_results.name: Theorem 28

trajectory.query: relation between bar L^(n) and L-hat prime integral pairing with phi in H^- quaternionic

returned_results.slogan: A quaternion algebra B containing E exists with certain homomorphism conditions. For any elements phi and phi in specified spaces, an equality holds between two different pairings. The left side involves Weil pairings applied to a theta lift. The right side involves an Iwahori pairing applied to a tensor product of elements.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.2 (Global seesaw identity)

returned_results.slogan: In the constant Z_p-extension L over K, a pairing from U times X prime of K to I(H) modulo I(H) squared, composed with delta_H inverse, maps into H equals Z_p. All values of this pairing lie within the integers contained in H. The pairing also induces a perfect pairing on the rational vector spaces Q U and Q X prime of K.
returned_results.name: Lemma 6.2

returned_results.slogan: Given an element h and a form φ, the pairing L_φ(h) is expressed as an integral over a quotient space of the adelic group. The integration involves the pairing of h and φ evaluated at group elements. The measure includes a term depending on the norm of the multiplier ν raised to a power determined by the weight. The domain of integration is modulo the rational points and the center of the real points.
returned_results.name: Lemma

returned_results.slogan: The integral over H2(F) of the product of two functions, phi-rho and phi-pi, equals the product of the L-function evaluated at n minus m and the function phi-pi-prime at h1.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.6

returned_results.slogan: A canonical perfect bilinear pairing exists from the Cartesian product of H1 of N with itself to a specified module. This pairing is defined by a limit formula involving sums over integers coprime to N times a prime power. The pairing is compatible with the action of a dual Hecke algebra. It satisfies an adjoint property with respect to the action of dual Hecke operators.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.4

returned_results.slogan: The derivation D-bar from L's ring of integers to a quotient of its character group satisfies a pairing formula. The pairing equals the trace of a product involving the logarithm of the derivation applied to beta, scaled by v_n. This holds for all alpha with sufficiently large valuation and for all nonzero beta in L.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.8

returned_results.slogan: Given phi in pi_A and varphi in pi_A dual, the pairing of P_Omega of phi and P_Omega inverse of varphi equals a product involving L-functions and a factor alpha. The result holds as an identity in the tensor product of L prime with the complex numbers. The formula relates the pairing to values of L-functions at specified points. The expression includes terms L of 2 and 1_F, L prime of one half and pi_A and Omega, and denominators with L of 1 and eta squared and L of 1 and pi_A adjoined.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1.1 (The Gross-Zagier-Zhang formula)

returned_results.slogan: The pairing of elements h bar alpha raised to i and j times h bar to the negative n alpha equals 2 if i plus j equals n, 8q if i and j both equal n, and 0 otherwise. The pairing of h bar alpha raised to i times h bar to the negative n alpha with h bar to the n over 2 times beta is always zero for i between 0 and n. The self-pairing of h bar to the n over 2 times beta equals negative one raised to n over 2 divided by 2. These pairings are defined in the quotient space h bar H minus over H minus.
returned_results.name: Proposition 6.5

returned_results.slogan: A non-zero spherical vector phi-circ in sigma yields an equality involving a pairing over H and inner products. The left side equals a constant Delta sub U of V times a ratio of L-functions. The numerator L-function is evaluated at one-half for the tensor product of sigma and the conjugate of mu. The denominator L-function is evaluated at one for the adjoint representation of sigma.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.0.3.1

returned_results.slogan: The integral of the theta function over two specific quaternionic cycles equals twice the pairing between one cycle and the action of a Hecke operator on the other.
returned_results.name: Proposition 5.9

trajectory.query: Calderon commutator multilinear singular integral bounded on L2 for Lipschitz functions

returned_results.slogan: For a given p between 1 and infinity, the Calderon commutator is bounded on Lp space if and only if the function b is Lipschitz continuous. The norm of the commutator applied to f is equivalent to the product of the Lipschitz norm of b and the Lp norm of f. The constants in this equivalence do not depend on b.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1

returned_results.slogan: The commutator of a Calderon-Zygmund operator with a function b in a two-parameter Lipschitz space is bounded from Lp to Lq. The bound depends on the norms of the kernel and b, and a constant independent of these norms. The exponents p and q satisfy a relation involving the parameters alpha1 and n. The result holds for functions in Lp over the product of two Euclidean spaces.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.2

returned_results.slogan: The commutator of a Calderon-Zygmund operator with a function b in a two-parameter Lipschitz space is bounded from a Hardy space to a Lebesgue space. The parameters satisfy specific inequalities and a scaling relation. The bound depends on the norm of the kernel and the Lipschitz norm of b. The constant in the inequality is independent of these norms.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.3

returned_results.slogan: The commutator of a Lipschitz function b with a certain singular integral operator is a Calderon-Zygmund operator. Its kernel K2 is bounded by a constant times the product of the L1 norm of Omega and the L infinity norm of the gradient of b, divided by the distance between x and y raised to the n-th power. The kernel also satisfies a smoothness condition involving a modulus of continuity omega 2,j. This modulus depends on the same norms and the minimum of 1 and a term involving the ratio of h to the distance between x and y.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.5

returned_results.slogan: A bilinear Calderón-Zygmund operator that is 2n-homogeneous in the l-th component is considered. For a locally integrable function b in a Lipschitz space with a given exponent alpha, the norm of b in that Lipschitz space is equivalent to the operator norm of a commutator involving b and T. This equivalence holds under specific conditions on the exponents, where the sum of the reciprocals of three exponents equals the reciprocal of p. The operator norm is taken between products of Lebesgue spaces and a dual Lebesgue space.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.2

returned_results.slogan: The commutator of a Calderón-Zygmund operator with a function from the RBMO space is bounded on Lp spaces for p between 1 and infinity. This holds when the operator is bounded on L2. The result applies to operators defined by kernels satisfying standard size and smoothness conditions.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.1

returned_results.slogan: The commutator of the Toeplitz operator with symbol sigma and the multiplication operator by a bounded Lipschitz function is a compact Calderón-Zygmund operator.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.1

returned_results.slogan: The commutator of a multiplier operator with a Lipschitz function is bounded in L2 norm. The bound depends on parameters s, delta, and j through specific exponential and power terms. The bound also scales linearly with the Lipschitz norm of the function and the L2 norm of the input. The constant in the inequality is independent of the parameters s, delta, and j.
returned_results.name: Lemma 5.4

returned_results.slogan: The commutator of a Lipschitz function b with a certain singular integral operator is a Calderon-Zygmund operator. Its kernel K1 is bounded by a constant times the product of the L infinity norms of Omega and the gradient of b, divided by the distance to the power n. The kernel also satisfies a smoothness condition involving a modulus of continuity omega sub 1,j. This modulus depends on the L infinity norms and a minimum function involving a parameter N of j and the ratio of h to the distance.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.3

returned_results.slogan: Given a pseudodifferential operator T_sigma and a Lipschitz function a with bounded gradient, the commutators of T_sigma and a are bilinear Calderon-Zygmund operators. These commutators are bounded from Lp times Lq to Lr for indices satisfying 1/p plus 1/q equals 1/r, with p and q strictly between 1 and infinity, and r at least 1.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1

trajectory.query: Hilbert transform principal value operator with Lipschitz change of variables bounded on L2

returned_results.slogan: The theorem provides norm estimates for the Hilbert transform and related operators applied to Schwartz functions. It assumes a bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism with a given constant L. The estimates bound the norms of the operators and their commutators in terms of the norms of the functions and the deviation of the homeomorphism's derivative from one. These inequalities hold with constants depending only on L.
returned_results.name: Proposition 7.13

returned_results.slogan: A function u from R squared to R has a Lipschitz condition in its second variable. An operator norm inequality holds for a supremum over a time interval. If p0 equals 2, the Hilbert transform along u is bounded in L2. If p0 is between 1 and 2, the boundedness holds for p greater than 1 plus one over 3 minus p0.
returned_results.name: Corollary 1.4

returned_results.slogan: The Hilbert transform and its variant map square integrable functions to square integrable functions with bounded norms. The norms of these transforms are controlled by the norm of the input function. The homogeneous Sobolev norm of the Hilbert transform is also bounded by that of the input function. These bounds depend on a constant related to the Lipschitz properties of an auxiliary function.
returned_results.name: Proposition 10.3

returned_results.slogan: For a given dimension and a measure on a Lipschitz graph, a certain operator composed with a transformation is bounded in the L2 space with respect to that measure. The operator's norm bound depends only on the dimensions, a constant, a parameter greater than two, a function, and the graph's slope. This result holds when the Hausdorff measure is restricted to the graph.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.2

returned_results.slogan: The result bounds a sum involving a Hilbert transform and Littlewood-Paley projections applied to a function. The bound holds for functions whose second variable has a small Lipschitz constant almost everywhere in the first variable. The inequality is valid for all exponents between one and infinity. The constant depends on the exponent and the chosen test functions.
returned_results.name: Corollary 1.3

returned_results.slogan: The Hilbert transform of a function in the product Hardy space and L2 space is bounded in Lp norm by its product Hardy space norm.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.3

returned_results.slogan: The commutator of the Hilbert transform with a smooth function, composed with a derivative, is bounded on L2. The operator norm is controlled by the L-infinity norm of the derivative of the function. The bound is linear in the norm of the function's derivative. This holds for all functions in L2.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.3 (\cite{cal,coffmey})

returned_results.slogan: The L2 to L2 operator norm of the Hilbert transform is bounded by a constant multiple of the absolute value of k.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.4

returned_results.slogan: The Hilbert transform of a function in L2 space on the interval from negative pi to pi is defined by a specific integral involving a cotangent kernel. The L2 norm of the Hilbert transform is bounded above by the L2 norm of the original function. This inequality holds for all functions in the L2 space over that interval.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4 (Riesz inequality {\cite[(6.167)]{king_2009}})

returned_results.slogan: For any power of two p, the Hilbert transform is a completely bounded map on the Lorentz space L p T with respect to the Lebesgue measure.
returned_results.name: Theorem 6.1

trajectory.query: Sobolev multiplication and composition H^r with r > 3/2 algebra Lipschitz dependence operator mapping H^{r-1}

returned_results.slogan: A locally Lipschitz continuous function composed with a function in the Sobolev space H^r(R) yields a multiplication operator that is bounded on H^r(R). The operator maps any function h in H^r(R) to the product of h and the composition. This result holds under the given Lipschitz condition on the real line.
returned_results.name: Lemma C.1

returned_results.slogan: For an open bounded set with Lipschitz boundary, the composition map from a product of Sobolev spaces into another Sobolev space is continuously differentiable of order r. This holds when the regularity index s exceeds half the dimension plus one. The result applies to functions and diffeomorphisms of specified smoothness.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.19

returned_results.slogan: A reproducing kernel Hilbert space algebra F is continuously embedded in L-infinity. If composing with a C^l function H is Lipschitz on balls in F, then composing with a C^{l+1} function G is also Lipschitz on balls in the Sobolev space F_s(F). Under additional assumptions on the Lipschitz constants of compositions with G' and G'', the Lipschitz constant for composition with G in F_s(F) is bounded by a constant times r times a polynomial in r.
returned_results.name: Proposition 13

returned_results.slogan: The composition operator with a sufficiently smooth function f maps Sobolev functions to Sobolev functions with controlled norms. If u is in H^s with a bounded s_0 norm, then the norm of f(u) in H^s is bounded by a constant times one plus the H^s norm of u. For a Lipschitz family of functions in a parameter, the Lipschitz norm of f(u) in H^s is similarly bounded by a constant times one plus the Lipschitz H^s norm of u. The constants depend on s and the C^s or C^{s+1} norm of f.
returned_results.name: Lemma

returned_results.slogan: A composition operator maps a Sobolev space into another Sobolev space if and only if the function satisfies a local Lipschitz condition. The operator is bounded, and its norm is controlled by a constant depending on the norm of the input function. The inequality relates the norm of the composition to the norm of the original function.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.1.5

returned_results.slogan: A smooth function sigma with Lipschitz bounds in both variables preserves Sobolev regularity. If u is in the homogeneous Sobolev space H^s for s between 0 and 1, then the composition sigma(u, Hu) also lies in H^s. The H^s norm of sigma(u, Hu) is bounded by a constant times the H^s norm of u. The constant depends only on the Lipschitz constant of sigma.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.3

returned_results.slogan: For s between 0 and 1, the product of two bounded functions in the homogeneous Sobolev space H^s is also in H^s, with a specific norm bound. If F is a Lipschitz function, then F composed with an H^s function remains in H^s, and its norm is bounded by the Lipschitz constant times the original norm. For a smooth function F and sigma between 1 and 2, F composed with a function in H^(sigma-1) intersect H^sigma is in H^sigma, with a norm bound depending on the L-infinity norm and the H^(sigma-1) and H^sigma norms of the function.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.4

returned_results.slogan: For any integer s at least 2 and any nonnegative integer r, the composition map from the product of the Sobolev space H^s and the space of diffeomorphisms D to the s plus r to H^s is r times continuously differentiable. The map sends a function u and a diffeomorphism phi to the composition of u with phi. This result holds under the given regularity conditions on the function and diffeomorphism spaces.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.3

returned_results.slogan: A smooth complex function f defines a smooth map between Sobolev spaces of order s greater than half the dimension. This map sends a function u to the composition f(u). It is infinitely differentiable as an operator. Additionally, the map is Lipschitz continuous with a constant depending on s.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.1

returned_results.slogan: The multiplication operator defined by multiplying a function by a given function in a Sobolev space is bounded by the norm of that function. The bound holds uniformly with respect to the Sobolev norm index. If the function depends on a parameter in a Lipschitz manner, the bound also holds for the corresponding Lipschitz norms. This result applies to functions defined on the torus.
returned_results.name: Lemma

trajectory.query: commutator of Hilbert transform with multiplication by Lipschitz function derivative bounded on L2 Calderon first commutator

returned_results.slogan: The commutator of the Hilbert transform with a smooth function, composed with a derivative, is bounded on L2. The operator norm is controlled by the L-infinity norm of the derivative of the function. The bound is linear in the norm of the function's derivative. This holds for all functions in L2.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.3 (\cite{cal,coffmey})

returned_results.slogan: The commutator of the Hilbert transform and a Lipschitz function applied to the derivative of a Schwartz function is bounded. The bound is proportional to the infinity norm of the derivative of the Lipschitz function and the L0 norm of the Schwartz function. The constant C is independent of the functions involved. This inequality holds for all Schwartz functions on the real line.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.4 (Caldern's commutator theorem)

returned_results.slogan: A constant C greater than zero exists such that for all continuously differentiable functions f with square-integrable derivative and all square-integrable functions g, the L-infinity norm of the commutator of f with the Hilbert transform applied to g is bounded by C times the L2 norm of f prime times the L2 norm of g.
returned_results.name: Proposition 25

returned_results.slogan: The commutator of the Hilbert transform with a function in the homogeneous Sobolev space H1 dot applied to the derivative of a function in H one-half dot is bounded in L2 norm. The bound is controlled by the product of the H1 dot norm of the first function and the H one-half dot norm of the second function. This inequality holds for all such functions defined on the real line.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.1 (from~ \cite{AN1})

returned_results.slogan: A constant C greater than zero exists such that for certain functions f and g with zero boundary values and derivatives in L2, and for h in L2, the L2 norm of the derivative of the commutator of f with the commutator of g and the Hilbert transform applied to h is bounded by the product of the L2 norms of the derivatives of f and g and the L2 norm of h.
returned_results.name: Proposition 17

returned_results.slogan: The theorem provides an inequality for the commutator of the Hilbert transform and a function. It bounds the Lp norm of a derivative of the commutator applied to another function. The bound depends on the L infinity norm of a high derivative of one function and the Lp norm of the other. The result holds for real numbers and specific exponents.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.4

returned_results.slogan: A constant C greater than zero exists such that for certain functions f and g with zero boundary conditions, the commutator of f with the Hilbert transform applied to the derivative of g is bounded in L2 norm. This bound is at most C times the L-infinity norm of the derivative of f multiplied by the L2 norm of g. The functions f and g are required to be continuously differentiable on the interval and continuous on the circle, with additional conditions on the derivative of g. The result holds under the assumption that the derivative of g belongs to an Lp space for some p greater than one.
returned_results.name: Proposition 12 ($L^\infty \times L^2$ Estimate \cite{calderon})

returned_results.slogan: A constant C greater than zero exists such that for all continuously differentiable functions f and g with square-integrable derivatives and for any square-integrable function h, the L2 norm of the derivative of the double commutator of f, g, and the Hilbert transform applied to h is bounded by the product of the L2 norms of the derivatives of f and g and the L2 norm of h.
returned_results.name: Proposition 26

returned_results.slogan: The commutator of f with the Hilbert transform H applied to g is bounded in L2 norm by the product of the H1/2 norm of f and the L2 norm of g. The L infinity norm of the same commutator is bounded by the product of the L2 norm of f prime and the L2 norm of g. The commutator applied to the derivative of g has L2 norm bounded by the product of the L2 norm of f prime and the H1/2 norm of g. A three-term commutator involving f, h, and the derivative of g is bounded in L2 norm by a product of norms of the derivatives of f and h and norms of g.
returned_results.name: Proposition 29

returned_results.slogan: There exists a positive constant C such that for all continuously differentiable functions f and g with square-integrable derivatives, the commutator of f with the Hilbert transform applied to g is bounded by the product of the half-derivative norm of f and the L2 norm of g. Additionally, the commutator applied to the derivative of g is bounded by the product of the L2 norm of the derivative of f and the half-derivative norm of g.
returned_results.name: Proposition 23

trajectory.query: multilinear singular integral operator with kernel product of difference quotients bounded on L2 Lipschitz inputs

returned_results.slogan: The theorem establishes L2 norm bounds for a singular integral operator T defined by a principal value integral. The operator involves differences of functions A_i and H, with H satisfying a Lipschitz condition. The first bound depends on the L infinity norms of the derivatives of A_i and the L2 norm of f. The second bound uses the L2 norm of the derivative of A_1 and the L infinity norms of the other A_i derivatives and f.
returned_results.name: Corollary 10.2

returned_results.slogan: A singular integral involving products of derivatives and finite differences of functions is bounded in L2 norm. The bound is expressed in terms of Sobolev norms of the functions raised to various powers. The exponents are nonnegative and their sum is less than one. The constant depends on the Lipschitz norms of the functions.

The bound is proportional to the logarithm of n raised to alpha plus one, multiplied by n raised to the negative of alpha plus one over d plus two. This holds for all nonnegative alpha with a constant depending on the true density, variance function, and other parameters. The number of neighbors k_n is chosen proportional to n raised to two over d plus two.
returned_results.name: Proposition 6

returned_results.slogan: Under a bounded fourth moment condition and positive measure for all balls in the support, the k-nearest neighbors estimators for the conditional mean and variance are L2-consistent. This holds when the number of neighbors k1 and k2 tend to infinity but remain small relative to sample sizes n1 and n2. The mean squared error of both estimators converges to zero.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.1 (Consistency of the Mean and Variance Regression Functions)

returned_results.slogan: The fixed k-nearest neighbor estimator for differential entropy has a bounded mean squared error. This bound holds for independent and identically distributed samples from a density function. The error is at most a constant times the sum of two terms involving the sample size. The constant depends on the smoothness, dimension, and other parameters.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1

trajectory.query: Kozachenko Leonenko estimator asymptotic unbiasedness bounded density finite moment

returned_results.slogan: An estimator for a target functional is asymptotically unbiased under certain conditions. The estimator function must be continuous, and the underlying densities must satisfy specific upper and lower bound assumptions. These bounds involve parameters such as k, a, l, and b, and depend on a function xi from a given set. The estimator parameters k and l must exceed values determined by omega of xi and the parameters a and a tilde.
returned_results.name: Theorem IV.1 (Vanishing bias)

returned_results.slogan: The estimator is asymptotically unbiased for the target functional when the estimator function is continuous. This holds if the underlying density meets two conditions: a lower bound and an upper bound involving parameters and a function. The estimator uses a fixed parameter greater than the negative product of a function and another parameter.
returned_results.name: Theorem III.1 (Vanishing bias)

returned_results.slogan: The estimator is asymptotically unbiased under given conditions. These conditions involve bounds on parameters gamma and k, and constraints on the density function p. The function p must be bounded away from zero and satisfy certain integrability conditions. The expectation of the estimator converges to the true value as sample sizes go to infinity.
returned_results.name: Theorem .4 (Asymptotic unbiasedness)

returned_results.slogan: The density estimator f_m(x) converges uniformly to the true density f(x) over the set S as m increases. The convergence includes a bias term of order m^{-1} with a specific coefficient b(x). The bias term b(x) depends on the first and second partial derivatives of f. The remainder term is of smaller order than m^{-1}.
returned_results.name: Proposition 5.1

returned_results.slogan: The estimator is unbiased with expected value equal to the integral of h with respect to the stationary distribution. It has finite moments for p greater than or equal to one, provided the reciprocal of p exceeds the sum of the reciprocals of m and kappa. These results hold under the condition that the initial distribution has a bounded density relative to the stationary distribution. The function h must be integrable with respect to the stationary distribution with exponent m greater than kappa divided by kappa minus one.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.1

returned_results.slogan: For a continuous probability density function, a sequence of estimators is constructed using independent copies of a random vector. The estimator's mean converges to the true density value as the sample size increases. Its variance is bounded by an expression involving the sample size and the dimension. The bound includes a constant that asymptotically approaches a specific value depending on the dimension.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1 (\textbf {Sequence of estimators of} $p_{\mathbf{H}} ({\boldsymbol{\eta}} )$ \cite {Parzen1962})

returned_results.slogan: The expected squared difference between the estimator and the true entropy converges to zero as the sample size increases. This holds when the random variable has a finite moment of some positive order. The density function is also bounded above. The result applies in the limit of large samples.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1 (\cite{penrose2013})

returned_results.slogan: Under certain assumptions, there exists a positive probability mass function such that for a specific metric and any bounded Lipschitz function, a given estimator is unbiased and has finite variance for the expected value.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.1

returned_results.slogan: The estimator is asymptotically unbiased when gamma is negative and between negative k and zero. The probability density p must be bounded from above and have a support that contains the support of q. For sufficiently small delta, the integral of H with respect to q is finite. This result holds under several boundedness assumptions.
returned_results.name: Theorem 9 (Asymptotic unbiasedness)

returned_results.slogan: The estimates for KL divergence between two distributions are asymptotically unbiased. This holds when the distributions have densities satisfying certain finite functional conditions. The expected value of the estimator converges to the true KL divergence as sample sizes go to infinity.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1

trajectory.query: variance bound for Kozachenko-Leonenko entropy estimator E[(Hhat - E Hhat)^2] tends to 0 fixed k

returned_results.slogan: Under certain conditions, the k-nearest neighbor entropy estimator converges almost surely to its expected value as the sample size grows. The variance of this estimator is bounded by an expression that scales inversely with the sample size and the number of neighbors. This bound depends on constants related to the data distribution and the maximum number of neighbors a point can have. The variance decreases at a rate proportional to one over the product of the sample size and k.
returned_results.name: Theorem 18

returned_results.slogan: For k at least 3, the expected value of the k-local nearest neighbor entropy estimator converges to the true entropy as the sample size goes to infinity. This holds for independent and identically distributed samples from a twice continuously differentiable probability density function. The variance of the estimator is bounded by the square of the log of n divided by n, provided the second moment of the log density is finite. The constant in the bias expression depends only on k and the dimension.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1

returned_results.slogan: The variance of the empirical estimator for entropy is bounded above by a constant multiple of the entropy itself. This holds for any sample size greater than or equal to one. The bound is expressed in terms of the entropy of the underlying probability distribution. The result applies to samples drawn from a discrete distribution.
returned_results.name: Lemma 20

returned_results.slogan: The variance of the truncated KL entropy estimator with N independent samples is bounded by an expression of order. The bound involves terms of log N and log log N raised to certain powers. The exponent on log N depends on constants k and delta. The overall bound scales inversely with the number of samples N.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4

returned_results.slogan: The variance of the k-nearest neighbor estimator for the Hellinger-Pinsker divergence is bounded above by a term on the order of one over N. This bound holds for sample size N.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.2

returned_results.slogan: The expected squared error between the entropy estimator and true entropy is bounded by a sum of two terms. The first term depends on the Holder continuity exponent beta and dimension D. The second term depends inversely on the sample size n and the number of neighbors k. Choosing k proportional to a specific power of n optimizes the convergence rate. The overall bound combines bias and variance contributions.
returned_results.name: Corollary 20

returned_results.slogan: The squared difference between the estimator and the true entropy converges to zero in expectation as the sample size increases. This holds under the condition that the norm of the random variable has a finite moment of some positive order. The function is also assumed to be bounded above. The result applies for any fixed integer parameter greater than or equal to one.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3 (Main theorem)

returned_results.slogan: The variance of the estimator for a fixed k and x less than a approaches an expression as n tends to infinity. The leading term is P of x squared times negative log of P of x, divided by n. A correction term involves k minus one multiplied by the square of the log of P of x minus the log of P of x, all divided by two n squared. The remainder is of smaller order than one over n.
returned_results.name: Proposition 5.2

returned_results.slogan: The expected absolute difference between the estimated entropy and the true entropy is bounded by a constant times the sum of two terms. The first term is k divided by n times log n. The second term is log n divided by the square root of n. This bound holds when log n is at least on the order of log k.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3

returned_results.slogan: The variance of the difference between the estimated entropy and the true entropy is asymptotically negligible compared to one over n. This holds under the conditions specified in the central limit theorem. The variance decays faster than the rate one over n.
returned_results.name: Proposition \thesection .1

trajectory.query: nearest neighbor entropy estimator variance bounded by log N squared over N

returned_results.slogan: Under certain conditions, the k-nearest neighbor entropy estimator converges almost surely to its expected value as the sample size grows. The variance of this estimator is bounded by an expression that scales inversely with the sample size and the number of neighbors. This bound depends on constants related to the data distribution and the maximum number of neighbors a point can have. The variance decreases at a rate proportional to one over the product of the sample size and k.
returned_results.name: Theorem 18

returned_results.slogan: The variance of the k-nearest neighbor estimator for the Hellinger-Pinsker divergence is bounded above by a term on the order of one over N. This bound holds for sample size N.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.2

returned_results.slogan: The variance of the nearest neighbor ratio estimator is bounded above by a term of order one over N plus a term of order one over M.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.2

returned_results.slogan: The bias of the marginal entropy estimator is bounded by a term of order log N raised to the power of one plus delta times one plus one over d, divided by N to the power of one over d. This holds under specific rate assumptions and when the nearest neighbor distance is bounded by a sequence a_N. The result applies for k greater than or equal to the ratio of d_x to d_y. The expectation is taken over the indicator event that the nearest neighbor distance is at most a_N.
returned_results.name: Lemma 13

returned_results.slogan: For k at least 3, the expected value of the k-local nearest neighbor entropy estimator converges to the true entropy as the sample size goes to infinity. This holds for independent and identically distributed samples from a twice continuously differentiable probability density function. The variance of the estimator is bounded by the square of the log of n divided by n, provided the second moment of the log density is finite. The constant in the bias expression depends only on k and the dimension.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1

returned_results.slogan: The k-nearest neighbor entropy estimator's expected absolute error is bounded by a term involving k over M raised to one over d, plus a term involving one over k, plus a higher-order remainder. The estimator's variance is bounded by a term involving one over N, plus a term involving one over M, plus a higher-order remainder. The constants in these bounds depend only on the underlying reward distribution and the true entropy. The random variables are independent and identically distributed with bounded support.
returned_results.name: Theorem 16

returned_results.slogan: The variance of the entropy estimator is bounded by a term of order log N raised to the power of three plus delta, divided by N. This bound holds under the stated rate assumption. The result shows how the estimator's variance decreases as the sample size increases. The logarithmic factor indicates a slow convergence rate.
returned_results.name: Lemma 14

returned_results.slogan: The expected squared error between the entropy estimator and true entropy is bounded by a sum of two terms. The first term depends on the Holder continuity exponent beta and dimension D. The second term depends inversely on the sample size n and the number of neighbors k. Choosing k proportional to a specific power of n optimizes the convergence rate. The overall bound combines bias and variance contributions.
returned_results.name: Corollary 20

returned_results.slogan: The variance of a function based on nearest neighbor distances is bounded above. The bound depends on the sample size and the dimension of the space. It involves expected values of squared distance-based functions. The constant in the bound depends only on the dimensionality.
returned_results.name: Lemma B.24

returned_results.slogan: The fixed k-nearest neighbor estimator for differential entropy has a bounded mean squared error. This bound holds for independent and identically distributed samples from a density function. The error is at most a constant times the sum of two terms involving the sample size. The constant depends on the smoothness, dimension, and other parameters.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1

trajectory.query: heat trace asymptotic expansion on orbifolds coefficient c_k equals manifold coefficient plus singular stratum contributions

returned_results.slogan: The heat trace of a closed two-dimensional Riemannian orbifold has an asymptotic expansion as time approaches zero. This expansion consists of a main term from the regular part and contributions from each singular stratum. The contribution from each singular stratum is weighted by the reciprocal of the order of its isotropy group. The coefficients in the expansion are defined via integrals and series involving geometric invariants.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.11

returned_results.slogan: The trace of the heat kernel on a Riemannian orbifold integrated over the orbifold has an asymptotic expansion as time approaches zero. This expansion consists of a main term from the regular part and contributions from each singular stratum. The main term scales with the negative half power of the orbifold dimension, while each singular contribution scales with the negative half power of the stratum dimension. The singular contributions are weighted by the inverse of the isotropy group order at points in the stratum.
returned_results.name: Lemma

returned_results.slogan: The heat trace for the Hodge Laplacian on a closed orbifold has an asymptotic expansion as time approaches zero. This expansion includes contributions from the regular part and from each primary singular stratum. The coefficients involve integrals over these strata and depend on the isotropy groups. The leading coefficient for each stratum is expressed as a sum over maximal isotropy elements.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.6

returned_results.slogan: The heat trace of a Riemannian orbifold has an asymptotic expansion as time approaches zero from the positive side. This expansion involves contributions from all singular strata of the orbifold, weighted by the order of their isotropy groups. The expansion takes the form of a power series in the square root of time, multiplied by an inverse power of time related to the orbifold's dimension. The coefficients in this series are constants determined by the geometry and singular structure of the orbifold.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.2

returned_results.slogan: The heat trace of a Riemannian orbifold has an asymptotic expansion as time approaches zero from the positive side. This expansion is expressed as a sum over all strata of the orbifold, each term divided by the order of the isotropy group of points in that stratum. The expansion takes the form of a power series in the square root of time, multiplied by an inverse power of time related to the dimension of the orbifold. The coefficients in this series are constants that depend on the geometry of the orbifold.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.8

returned_results.slogan: The heat trace of a Riemannian orbifold has an asymptotic expansion as time approaches zero from the positive side. This expansion involves contributions from all strata of the orbifold, weighted by the order of the isotropy at each point. The expansion takes the form of a power series in the square root of time, multiplied by an inverse power of time related to the dimension. The coefficients in this series are constants determined by the geometry and isotropy of the orbifold.
returned_results.name: Theorem 6.4

returned_results.slogan: The heat trace on a Riemannian orbifold has an asymptotic expansion as time approaches zero from the positive side. The expansion involves contributions from the regular part and from isolated singularities. Each isolated singularity contributes a term divided by the order of its local group. The expansion takes the form of a power series in the square root of time, multiplied by a factor involving the dimension and pi.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.1

returned_results.slogan: The asymptotic expansion of the heat trace for the orbifold M over Z_k is approximately twice A plus twice C as t approaches zero. For the orbifold M over D_k, the expansion is approximately A plus B plus C. The difference between these expansions gives the asymptotic expansion for Z_Omega, which is approximately A minus B plus C. These relations are derived from given equations and a lemma.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.13

returned_results.slogan: The trace of the heat kernel for an isometry on an orbifold has an asymptotic expansion as time approaches zero. The expansion sums over all strata of the orbifold, weighted by the order of the isotropy group. Each term involves an integral over the fixed point set of the isometry intersected with the stratum. The coefficients are local invariants depending on the isometry and the geometry.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.2

returned_results.slogan: The heat trace for the Hodge Laplacian on smooth p-forms of a closed Riemannian orbifold has an asymptotic expansion as time approaches zero. This expansion includes contributions from both the regular part and all singular strata of the orbifold. Each singular stratum contributes a term divided by the order of its isotropy group. The expansion takes the form of a power series in the square root of time, multiplied by an inverse power of time.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.15

trajectory.query: for finite Riemannian covering heat invariants scale by degree a_j(base)=1/r a_j(cover)

returned_results.slogan: A finite k-sheeted Riemannian cover relates the spectral properties of two manifolds. The heat trace coefficients of the first manifold equal k times those of the second. Similarly, the Minakshisundaram-Pleijel coefficients of the first are k times those of the second. This holds for every positive integer n.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.1

returned_results.slogan: The heat kernel on a regular covering space corresponds to the heat kernel on the base manifold.
returned_results.name: Proposition 5.4

returned_results.slogan: Given a covering of weighted graphs, the sum of heat kernels over the fiber of a vertex equals a scaled version of the base heat kernel. The scaling factor involves the square root of the ratio of fiber sizes. For a strong regular covering with a singleton fiber at a chosen vertex, the heat kernel on the cover simplifies to the base heat kernel divided by the square root of the fiber size at the target. This relation holds for any vertex in the base and any lift in the cover.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.1

returned_results.slogan: The heat kernel on the base manifold is bounded below by the heat kernel on the covering space. This inequality holds for all positive times and all points on the base manifold. The result applies to regular coverings of Riemannian manifolds.
returned_results.name: Proposition 5.2 (Proposition~ 2.4 in \cite{Bor00})

returned_results.slogan: For a regular covering map between manifolds, the heat kernel on the base equals the sum over the covering group of heat kernels on the cover. The covering group is the quotient of the fundamental groups. The sum involves any lifts of the base points to the covering space. This relation holds for all points and time.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2 (\mbox{\rm \cite[p. 826]{Brooks}})

returned_results.slogan: A Riemannian covering of finite degree preserves the bottom of the spectrum and the bottom of the essential spectrum. The bottom of the spectrum of the covering space equals that of the base space. Similarly, the bottom of the essential spectrum of the covering space equals that of the base space. This holds for any finite-degree Riemannian covering.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.1

returned_results.slogan: On a stochastically complete Riemannian manifold S with a normal covering space, the heat kernel of the operator Δ minus a bounded potential V is given. The heat kernel on the base manifold equals a sum over deck transformations of the heat kernel on the covering space. This sum involves the lifted potential and holds for all points in the covering space and all positive times.
returned_results.name: Corollary 6.6

returned_results.slogan: For a tower of coverings converging to an infinite Galois covering of a compact Riemannian manifold, the integral of the trace of the heat kernel over the fundamental domain of the infinite covering equals the limit of the corresponding integrals over the finite coverings. This limit also equals the limit of the average integrals over the finite covering spaces. The result holds for each positive integer power of the heat kernel.
returned_results.name: Corollary 3.5

returned_results.slogan: A k-fold Riemannian covering between closed oriented manifolds implies an inequality for conformal covering invariants. The invariant on the base manifold is bounded above by that on the covering space. It is also bounded below by the covering invariant scaled by k to the negative two over n. Consequently, the conformal volume of the base is at most that of the cover.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.3.5

returned_results.slogan: The heat kernel on the base manifold equals the heat kernel on its regular covering space for all positive times and all pairs of points.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.3

trajectory.query: isospectral manifolds have equal volume heat coefficient a_0 determines volume

returned_results.slogan: The volumes of two manifolds are equal. Therefore, the zeroth order coefficients of their heat kernels are also equal.
returned_results.name: Lemma 7.1

returned_results.slogan: Two manifolds without boundary and with equal volume are isoheat.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1

returned_results.slogan: The leading heat kernel coefficient equals the volume function.
returned_results.name: Lemma 6.1

returned_results.slogan: The zeroth heat kernel coefficient equals a constant times the volume of the manifold. The first coefficient is proportional to the volume of the boundary. The second coefficient involves integrals of the scalar curvature over the manifold and the mean curvature over the boundary. Higher coefficients include more complex curvature invariants and their derivatives.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1

returned_results.slogan: The zeroth heat kernel coefficient equals the volume of the manifold. The first coefficient is proportional to the volume of the boundary. The second coefficient involves an integral of the mean curvature over the boundary. Higher coefficients include integrals of curvature tensors and second fundamental form components on the boundary.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.2

returned_results.slogan: The volume of a compact Riemannian manifold can be recovered from its heat kernel trace. The volume equals the limit as time approaches zero of a specific expression involving the trace. This expression is scaled by a power of time and a constant factor. The result connects spectral data to geometric volume.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.5

returned_results.slogan: Two flat tori are isospectral if and only if they have identical heat traces. They are also isospectral if and only if they have identical theta series. Another equivalent condition is that they have identical length spectra. If any of these conditions hold, the tori must have the same dimension and volume.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2.15

returned_results.slogan: The zeroth heat kernel coefficient is a volume integral over the manifold of the trace of the identity. The first coefficient is a boundary integral of the trace of the identity. The second coefficient involves integrals over both the manifold and boundary, including terms with E, the scalar curvature, and S. Higher coefficients a3 and a4 are more complex, combining volume and boundary integrals with additional curvature and boundary operator terms.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.2

returned_results.slogan: Two locally homogeneous three-manifolds have equal heat trace coefficients up to order three. If one manifold is modeled on the Nil geometry, then the other is locally isometric to it. This result holds under the given spectral condition.
returned_results.name: Theorem 73

returned_results.slogan: A smooth diffeomorphism between closed Riemannian manifolds implies that equality of one Dirichlet series coefficient for all parameters makes two conditions equivalent to isospectrality. If either manifold has a simple spectrum, then one of these conditions alone is equivalent to isospectrality.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2

trajectory.query: locality and universality of heat invariants U_j are constant on locally homogeneous spaces and equal for quotients with common homogeneous cover

returned_results.slogan: For locally homogeneous three-manifolds, the heat trace invariants a_j equal the curvature invariants b_j for j=0,1,2 if and only if the b_j values are equal. If both manifolds are modeled on unimodular Lie groups with left-invariant metrics and satisfy a nonzero polynomial condition, then a_j equals b_j for j=0,1,2,3 if and only if the b_j values are equal.
returned_results.name: Corollary 60

returned_results.slogan: For a locally homogeneous three-manifold, the first two heat invariants are expressed in terms of the Ricci tensor eigenvalues. The first invariant equals the volume times a linear combination of the eigenvalues divided by six. The second invariant equals the volume times a quadratic combination of the eigenvalues divided by three hundred sixty. If the manifold is covered by a unimodular Lie group with non-zero Ricci eigenvalues, the third invariant is given by a more complex rational function of the eigenvalues.
returned_results.name: Theorem 54

returned_results.slogan: For each nonnegative integer j, there is a universal polynomial P_j depending on the curvature tensor and its covariant derivatives up to order j. The j-th heat invariant a_j equals the integral of P_j over the manifold with respect to the volume form. On a fixed compact Riemannian manifold, the absolute value of a_j is bounded by a constant C_j that depends on the manifold and its metric.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.2 (Bounds for heat coefficients)

returned_results.slogan: A compact three-manifold with a universal cover that is a symmetric space, Nil, or R-squared semidirect R, each with a left-invariant metric, is considered. Among compact locally homogeneous three-manifolds, such a manifold is determined up to local isometry by its first four heat invariants. The heat invariants are spectral quantities derived from the Laplace-Beltrami operator. This result characterizes the manifold's local isometry type using only these four invariants.
returned_results.name: Corollary 75

returned_results.slogan: Two locally homogeneous three-manifolds with equal heat invariants up to order three are either both modeled on the Sol geometry or both modeled on the universal cover of SL2R. The converse also holds: if both manifolds are modeled on one of these geometries, then their heat invariants match. This establishes a necessary and sufficient condition for isospectrality within these two model geometries.
returned_results.name: Corollary 82

returned_results.slogan: Two locally homogeneous three-manifolds with equal heat invariants up to order three are locally isometric to a product of a two-sphere and a Euclidean line if and only if the other is also locally isometric to that product. The same holds for the product of a hyperbolic plane and a Euclidean line. The result applies for any non-zero real constant k. The theorem establishes a necessary and sufficient condition for such local isometries based on heat invariants.
returned_results.name: Theorem 71

returned_results.slogan: If every invariant geodesic orbit metric on the universal cover is normal, then every such metric on the original space is also normal. The same holds for standard metrics. This result applies to homogeneous spaces and their universal covers. It establishes a correspondence between metric properties on the cover and the base space.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2.9

returned_results.slogan: A compact locally homogeneous three-manifold with universal cover isometric to a symmetric space, R2 semidirect R, Nil, or a nearly round left-invariant metric on S3 is determined up to local isometry by its first four heat invariants. If such a manifold shares the first four heat invariants with one modeled on the metrically maximal geometry of the universal cover of SL2(R) with its maximal isometry group, then it must be modeled on the universal cover of SL2(R) itself.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2

returned_results.slogan: For compact locally homogeneous three-manifolds with specific Ricci tensor properties, if the first four heat invariants match, then the third invariant polynomial of the metric's volume-normalized eigenvalues must be equal. Alternatively, it may equal a constant expression defined in terms of the first three invariant polynomials of the original metric. This constant involves squares and cubes of these polynomials combined in a rational formula.
returned_results.name: Theorem 61

returned_results.slogan: The theorem provides formulas for the heat invariants e sub q,0, e sub q,2, and e sub q,4 on a manifold. These invariants are expressed as integrals involving the volume form, scalar curvature, Ricci curvature norm squared, and full curvature norm squared. Each term includes combinatorial coefficients depending on the dimension m and the parameter q. The constants involve powers of pi and numerical factors.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.1

trajectory.query: heat invariants are integrals of universal local densities U_j on orbifolds and manifolds

returned_results.slogan: For each nonnegative integer j, there is a universal polynomial P_j depending on the curvature tensor and its covariant derivatives up to order j. The j-th heat invariant a_j equals the integral of P_j over the manifold with respect to the volume form. On a fixed compact Riemannian manifold, the absolute value of a_j is bounded by a constant C_j that depends on the manifold and its metric.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.2 (Bounds for heat coefficients)

returned_results.slogan: The theorem provides formulas for the heat invariants e sub q,0, e sub q,2, and e sub q,4 on a manifold. These invariants are expressed as integrals involving the volume form, scalar curvature, Ricci curvature norm squared, and full curvature norm squared. Each term includes combinatorial coefficients depending on the dimension m and the parameter q. The constants involve powers of pi and numerical factors.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.1

returned_results.slogan: For any integer omega greater than or equal to three times n, the local heat invariants of a d-dimensional closed Riemannian manifold are given by a specific formula. This formula involves a sum over j from zero to omega, with binomial coefficients and factorials in the denominator. The expression also includes the application of the Laplacian operator raised to the power j plus n to a function f of the squared distance from x. The function f must be smooth near x and satisfy f of s equals s plus terms of order s squared for small s.
returned_results.name: Theorem 14

returned_results.slogan: The heat invariants are integrals over Euclidean space of functions a_j(x). Each a_j(x) is defined using a sum involving binomial coefficients and derivatives of the distance function raised to a power. The binomial coefficients are expressed in terms of the Gamma function when the dimension n is odd. The derivatives are evaluated at the point where x equals y.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.1

returned_results.slogan: For a locally homogeneous three-manifold, the first two heat invariants are expressed in terms of the Ricci tensor eigenvalues. The first invariant equals the volume times a linear combination of the eigenvalues divided by six. The second invariant equals the volume times a quadratic combination of the eigenvalues divided by three hundred sixty. If the manifold is covered by a unimodular Lie group with non-zero Ricci eigenvalues, the third invariant is given by a more complex rational function of the eigenvalues.
returned_results.name: Theorem 54

returned_results.slogan: The fixed point set of gamma is a union of submanifolds with given dimensions. Certain invariants exist that depend functorially on gamma and a finite number of jets of the symbol of H. An asymptotic expansion relates an integral involving the heat kernel to a sum over these submanifolds. The expansion involves powers of t and integrals of the invariants over each submanifold.
returned_results.name: Theorem

returned_results.slogan: For each k between 1 and n-1, the local Steklov heat invariant a_k(x) is expressible as a universal polynomial. This polynomial depends on the covariant derivatives of the Riemann curvature tensor of the domain, up to order k-2. It also depends on the covariant derivatives of the mean curvature of the boundary, up to order k-1. The coefficients of this polynomial are universal constants.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.2.1

returned_results.slogan: Each heat invariant is a universal linear combination of Weyl Riemannian invariants. The weight of these invariants is twice the index of the heat invariant.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.6 (Atiyah-Bott-Patodi~ \cite{ABP:OHEIT})

returned_results.slogan: For any O(2)-invariant subset U of M, the integral of the heat kernel over the intersection of U and Omega equals a defined function G(t). This leads to a relation between integrals of heat kernels on quotient spaces of M by cyclic and dihedral groups over projected regions. Specifically, the difference of these integrals equals the heat kernel integral over U intersect Omega. When U is the entire manifold M, this simplifies to the difference of the heat traces on the quotient spaces equaling the heat trace on Omega.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.10

returned_results.slogan: The first heat invariant for the Laplacian on differential forms equals a binomial coefficient. The second invariant is a linear combination of binomial coefficients multiplied by the scalar curvature. The fourth invariant involves binomial coefficients and terms including the Laplacian of the scalar curvature, the square of the scalar curvature, and the squared norms of the Ricci and Riemann curvature tensors. The coefficients for these terms are given by specific combinations of binomials in the dimension and form degree.
returned_results.name: Theorem 6.1

trajectory.query: Caffarelli Silvestre extension theorem fractional Laplacian Dirichlet-to-Neumann map

returned_results.slogan: For n at least 1 and s between 0 and 1, there exists a map E_s from the union of Sobolev spaces to smooth functions on the upper half-space. This extension, called the Caffarelli-Silvestre extension, sends a function f to a function u that solves a weighted Laplace equation and converges to f at the boundary. The extension can be expressed as a convolution with a Poisson kernel or via its Fourier transform. The normal derivative of u at the boundary converges to a constant multiple of the fractional Laplacian of f.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.1

returned_results.slogan: For a smooth and bounded function u, the Caffarelli-Silvestre extension U is the unique bounded solution to a degenerate elliptic equation in the upper half-space with boundary condition u. The extension is smooth in the interior and continuous up to the boundary. The fractional Laplacian of u equals a constant multiple of the limit involving the normal derivative of U as the vertical coordinate approaches zero. This result connects the fractional Laplacian to a local problem in one higher dimension.
returned_results.name: Lemma 7.4

returned_results.slogan: The fractional Laplacian operator is characterized as a Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for an extension problem in a higher-dimensional half-space. For a given function, the solution to a specific Dirichlet problem in this extended space is considered. The fractional Laplacian applied to the function equals a constant multiple of the normal derivative limit of this solution at the boundary. This provides an alternative interpretation of the fractional operator through a local boundary condition.
returned_results.name: Proposition 11.2

returned_results.slogan: The fractional Laplacian operator for any exponent between zero and one corresponds to a Dirichlet-to-Neumann map in a higher-dimensional half-space. This map arises from an extension problem involving a specific degenerate elliptic operator. The exponent of the fractional Laplacian determines the parameter of the extension operator. This connection provides a way to study nonlocal operators using local methods in an extended setting.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.1

returned_results.slogan: The eigenfunctions and eigenvalues of the fractional Laplacian with Dirichlet boundary conditions are given by pairs of functions and their powers. An extension operator maps functions from a fractional Sobolev space to an extended space using a series involving these eigenfunctions and a special function solving an ordinary differential equation. The fractional Laplacian of such a function is represented as a series with coefficients multiplied by fractional powers of eigenvalues. Norms of the fractional Laplacian, its square root, the original function, and its extension are all equal up to a constant.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.3

returned_results.slogan: For n at least 3 and s between 0 and 1, consider two disjoint bounded Lipschitz sets and a uniformly elliptic matrix function. The theorem establishes a bounded linear operator mapping a fractional Dirichlet-to-Neumann data set to a classical one. This operator is defined via a Caffarelli-Silvestre extension and a boundary trace. The closure of the image of this operator equals the full classical data set.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.2

returned_results.slogan: The fractional Laplacian of a function in the Sobolev space H(M) is obtained using the Dirichlet-to-Neumann map. It equals the negative limit of the outward normal derivative of the harmonic extension as the extension variable approaches zero from above. This limit is taken in the dual space of H(M).
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.6

returned_results.slogan: The Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for the fractional Laplacian is expressed in terms of a nonlocal Neumann operator and an extension by zero. The nonlocal Neumann operator maps functions from a global Sobolev space to local Sobolev spaces outside the domain. It involves a smooth multiplier function defined by an integral over the domain. The formula holds almost everywhere for functions in L2.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.2

returned_results.slogan: A function in a fractional Sobolev space has a unique extension to a higher-dimensional space satisfying a weighted Laplace equation and matching boundary values. This extension is given by an integral formula involving a specific kernel or a Fourier multiplier. The fractional Laplacian of the original function equals a constant times a limit involving the normal derivative of the extension. The extension minimizes a weighted Dirichlet energy among all extensions and satisfies an energy identity relating the fractional Laplacian norm to the weighted gradient norm.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.1 (Caffarelli–Silvestre \cite{CS})

returned_results.slogan: For any bounded open set in the plane with a twice continuously differentiable boundary, and for any function in a fractional Sobolev space, the square integral of the fractional Laplacian of its extension is bounded by the square integral of its fractional Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator over the domain. This inequality holds for all fractional orders between zero and one. The fractional Laplacian is defined via the Fourier transform.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.3

trajectory.query: equivalence of stability definitions for fractional Allen-Cahn extension energy and nonlocal energy

returned_results.slogan: A sequence of solutions to a fractional Allen-Cahn equation with bounded energy converges to a function taking values plus or minus one. The limit corresponds to a set with finite nonlocal perimeter whose boundary satisfies a nonlocal mean curvature equation. The solutions converge locally uniformly away from the boundary, and their energy converges to a nonlocal perimeter functional. The level sets of the solutions and the boundary of the limit set are mutually close in Hausdorff distance.
returned_results.name: Proposition 5.1

returned_results.slogan: A sequence of solutions to a fractional Allen-Cahn equation with bounded energy and convergent exterior data has a subsequence converging to a nonlocal minimal partition. The limit partition consists of essentially open sets with finite nonlocal perimeter. The convergence is locally smooth away from the partition boundaries. The energy of the solutions converges to a constant multiple of the nonlocal area functional of the limit partition.
returned_results.name: Proposition 7.1

returned_results.slogan: For an open set Omega in d-dimensional space satisfying certain extension domain conditions, the nonlocal energy forms for functions u and v in the Sobolev space converge to a constant multiple of the local energy form as epsilon approaches zero. This holds for three different types of nonlocal energy forms: the minimal, maximal, and plus forms. The convergence is to the same limit in each case, scaled by a constant K_{d,p}. The result applies when Omega is a W^{1,p}-extension domain or when its boundary equals the boundary of its closure and the complement is also an extension domain.
returned_results.name: Theorem 9.15

returned_results.slogan: A function on the circle and its harmonic extension to the disk are related. The function is a stationary point of a fractional energy if and only if its extension is weakly conformal. This equivalence connects a half-order energy condition to a conformality condition.
returned_results.name: Theorem \thesection .4

returned_results.slogan: A function u solves a fractional Laplacian equation and is monotone in one variable. The limits of u at positive and negative infinity define two functions. If a smooth perturbation of the extension of u stays between the extensions of these limit functions, then the energy of u in a ball is less than or equal to the energy of the perturbed extension.
returned_results.name: Lemma 5.1

returned_results.slogan: For n at least 2 and s in (0,1), every stable solution u to a fractional equation converges along some subsequence to a function that takes only the values 1 and -1. The limit is the characteristic function of a nontrivial cone, which is weakly stable for the fractional perimeter. The localized Sobolev energies converge to those of the limit function. The potential energy terms vanish in the limit along the subsequence.
returned_results.name: Proposition 6.1

returned_results.slogan: The energy functional E superscript N of t is defined as a sum of energies E sub k of t plus the squared L2 norm of a fractional derivative of u. This total energy is equivalent to the squared norm of u in the Sobolev space H to the power of N plus alpha over 2 on the real line. The equivalence holds uniformly for all functions u whose norm in that Sobolev space is less than epsilon.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.1

returned_results.slogan: The energy form is equivalent to the squared norm in the fractional Sobolev space with zero mean. Adding the square of the mean value to the energy form gives an equivalent squared norm in the full fractional Sobolev space. These equivalences hold for functions in the respective spaces.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2.5

returned_results.slogan: For a function in the fractional Sobolev space on the circle with its harmonic extension, four conditions are equivalent. These include the equality of the angular and radial derivative magnitudes and their orthogonality. The conditions also state that the half-Laplacian of the function is zero and that the function is a stationary point of the energy. The harmonic extension is conformal on the disk if and only if the function is an energy stationary point.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.26

returned_results.slogan: The two definitions of the fractional Laplacian are equivalent. Both formulations describe the same mathematical operator.
returned_results.name: Proposition A.1

trajectory.query: second variation formula stability for fractional semilinear equation extension problem

returned_results.slogan: A stable solution to a fractional Laplacian equation with a convex nonlinearity has a harmonic extension. The theorem defines a quantity involving second derivatives of this extension. An inequality bounds the integral of this quantity squared times a test function squared.
