returned_results.slogan: The Dynamical Mordell-Lang conjecture holds for birational endomorphisms of the affine plane with first dynamical degree greater than one. It also holds for automorphisms of projective surfaces with first dynamical degree exceeding one. Additionally, it is valid for totally inseparable endomorphisms of projective space over certain positive characteristic fields that lift the Frobenius. These maps are defined by raising coordinates to a power of the characteristic and adding homogeneous polynomials from the maximal ideal.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.2

returned_results.slogan: For a dominant rational self-map f on a smooth projective surface S, if the first dynamical degree exceeds the second, and the dynamical Mordell-Lang conjecture holds, then for a point P with a Zariski dense forward orbit, the arithmetic degree exists and equals the first dynamical degree.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.3

returned_results.slogan: An automorphism with positive entropy on a projective surface has only finitely many periodic irreducible curves. The set of periodic points is the union of these curves and the periodic points not on any curve. For any positive integer d, the intersection of degree d points with the periodic points off the curves is finite. This confirms a conjecture about the structure of periodic points for such automorphisms.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.1 (cf.~ \cite{Kaw08})

returned_results.slogan: A unirational projective variety with a surjective morphism whose dynamical degree exceeds one satisfies a specific dynamical property.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.2

returned_results.slogan: A surface automorphism pair satisfies the DML property if and only if some positive iterate of the automorphism also satisfies it. The property holds precisely when every dense two-sided orbit intersects any irreducible closed subcurve in only finitely many points. If there is a dominant morphism between surfaces that commutes with their automorphisms, then one pair satisfies DML if and only if the other does. These three statements characterize the dynamical Mordell-Lang property for surfaces.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.9

returned_results.slogan: A dominant polynomial endomorphism on the affine plane over the algebraic closure of the rationals satisfies the dynamical Mordell-Lang property when the square of its first dynamical degree exceeds the second dynamical degree.
returned_results.name: Theorem

returned_results.slogan: The theorem applies to a projective surface with an ample line bundle and a birational map. If a specific ratio involving degrees of the map and its square exceeds one, then the first dynamical degree is bounded below by a function of that ratio. This lower bound is always at least one. The result provides a condition under which the dynamical degree is strictly greater than one.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.1

returned_results.slogan: A smooth projective surface over the algebraic numbers with an automorphism of dynamical degree greater than one has only finitely many periodic curves. There exist two real divisors and associated canonical height functions that transform by the dynamical degree under the automorphism and its inverse. The sum of these heights gives a Weil height for a nef and big divisor, and both heights are non-negative. For a point not on a periodic curve, these heights vanish precisely when the point is periodic.
returned_results.name: Theorem 9

returned_results.slogan: A birational map on a projective surface with a first dynamical degree greater than one has a Zariski dense set of non-critical periodic points.
returned_results.name: Theorem 6.8

returned_results.slogan: The first dynamical degree of a rational self-map on a surface is defined as a limit involving pullbacks of ample divisors and is independent of the divisor choices. This value is always at least the square root of the topological degree. Under a birational map, the first dynamical degree remains invariant. The result holds for surfaces and involves properties of rational maps and divisors.

returned_results.slogan: The first dynamical degree of a dominating rational map on a smooth projective surface exists. The first dynamical degree is invariant under birational changes of coordinates and does not depend on the choice of norm.

returned_results.slogan: For a dominant rational self-map f on X, the first dynamical degree equals the first arithmetic degree.

returned_results.slogan: The first dynamical degree of a birational map on a smooth projective surface is at least one and is invariant under birational conjugation. If the degree equals one, then the map is birationally conjugate to an automorphism with a power in the connected component of the identity. Alternatively, the map is not primitive and equivariantly maps to a curve with rational or elliptic general fibers.

returned_results.slogan: For a projective surface over a field with a dominant rational self-map and a big and nef line bundle, the first dynamical degree is at least the square of the first degree divided by four times the first degree.

returned_results.slogan: The clutter of minimal vertex covers of an unmixed bipartite graph is 2-partitionable. The rank of its incidence matrix is at most the independence number of the graph plus one. If the graph is Cohen-Macaulay, the rank equals the independence number plus one.

returned_results.slogan: A graph is unmixed if all its minimal vertex covers have the same size.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.4

returned_results.slogan: A simplicial complex on two disjoint vertex sets of equal size has a bipartite graph formed by faces intersecting both sets. If this graph is Cohen-Macaulay and has no isolated vertex, then two conditions are equivalent. The complex is unmixed with all minimal vertex covers having size equal to one vertex set. There also exists a lattice segment whose ideal equals the Stanley-Reisner ideal of the complex.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.4

returned_results.slogan: For a clutter, the ideal generated by its minimal vertex covers is unmixed if and only if every minimal vertex cover has size equal to its covering number minus one.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.8

returned_results.slogan: A bijection exists between minimal set covers on a set of n vertices and bipartite posets with n elements. This bijection preserves the balance property.
returned_results.name: Theorem 24

returned_results.slogan: A bipartite graph has minimal vertex covers of equal size. This implies that the vertex cover polytope admits a quadratic triangulation. The triangulation is a specific geometric decomposition of the polytope. The result holds under the stated condition on vertex covers.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.27 (Herzog, Hibi, Ohsugi ’09 \cite{Herzog2009})

returned_results.slogan: For an unmixed graph with two distinct minimal vertex covers C1 and C2, any vertex cover C' of the symmetric difference graph G' yields that C' union the intersection of C1 and C2 is a vertex cover of the original graph. The symmetric difference graph is bipartite with a perfect matching and a bipartition into two sets of equal size, which are the set differences of C1 and C2. The size of each part equals the matching number and the independence number of G'.
returned_results.name: Lemma 5.11

returned_results.slogan: The union of alpha x and alpha y forms a minimal vertex cover of the graph G P. Every minimal vertex cover of G P can be expressed as the union of beta x and beta y. This structure holds for some poset ideal beta of P. The result characterizes all minimal vertex covers in terms of poset ideals.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.1

trajectory.query: associated directed graph of unmixed bipartite graph acyclic reduction Cohen-Macaulay subgraph unique up to isomorphism

returned_results.slogan: An unmixed bipartite graph without isolated vertices contains a unique Cohen-Macaulay bipartite subgraph up to isomorphism. This subgraph has a poset isomorphic to that of the original graph. As a result, all maximal chains in the poset have equal length.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.4

returned_results.slogan: A bipartite graph is unmixed if and only if it has a perfect matching and its associated directed graph is transitively closed. The graph is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if it is perfectly matched and the associated directed graph is acyclic and transitively closed. An acyclic and transitively closed directed graph is equivalent to a poset.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.\@arabic \c@thm

returned_results.slogan: An unmixed bipartite graph is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if it has a unique perfect matching. This is also equivalent to the condition that for any two edges in the perfect matching, the complement of the subgraph induced by their vertices is connected. These three conditions are all equivalent for such graphs.
returned_results.name: Corollary 9

returned_results.slogan: A bipartite graph G satisfying conditions (1) and (2) is Cohen-Macaulay exactly when the directed graph D is both acyclic and transitive.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.6

returned_results.slogan: If a graph is Cohen-Macaulay, then it is also unmixed.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.1

returned_results.slogan: An unmixed bipartite graph G is an aCM graph if and only if two specific subgraphs H and K are also aCM graphs. The subgraph H is formed by removing the closed neighborhood of vertex x_n from G. The subgraph K is formed by removing the closed neighborhood of vertex y_n from G. This result holds under the condition that the only neighbor of x_n in G is y_n.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.9

returned_results.slogan: A bipartite graph G that meets two conditions and is sequentially Cohen-Macaulay implies its associated directed graph D has no cycles.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.4

returned_results.slogan: A Cohen-Macaulay bipartite graph contains exactly one perfect matching. This matching is unique and no other perfect matching exists in such a graph.
returned_results.name: Corollary 8

returned_results.slogan: An unmixed bipartite graph is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if it contains no induced complete bipartite subgraph on two sets of m vertices each, where the vertex indices match. This condition is equivalent to forbidding any induced matching of a two-by-two complete bipartite subgraph with corresponding indices. Specifically, the graph must avoid any induced subgraph isomorphic to K_{m,m} with vertices x_i1 through x_im and y_i1 through y_im for any subset of indices of size m at least two. The same holds when restricting to the case where m equals two.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.1

returned_results.slogan: An unmixed bipartite graph from a poset is a complete Cohen-Macaulay bipartite graph exactly when the poset is a chain.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.5

trajectory.query: minimal vertex covers of bipartite graph from poset ideals every minimal vertex cover corresponds to poset ideal

returned_results.slogan: The union of alpha x and alpha y forms a minimal vertex cover of the graph G P. Every minimal vertex cover of G P can be expressed as the union of beta x and beta y. This structure holds for some poset ideal beta of P. The result characterizes all minimal vertex covers in terms of poset ideals.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.1

returned_results.slogan: A bijection exists between minimal set covers on a set of n vertices and bipartite posets with n elements. This bijection preserves the balance property.
returned_results.name: Theorem 24

returned_results.slogan: A minimal prime ideal containing the edge ideal of a graph corresponds to a minimal vertex cover of the graph. The ideal is generated by a set of variables in a polynomial ring over a field. This set of variables forms a minimal vertex cover. The result establishes a one-to-one relationship between these algebraic and combinatorial structures.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1

returned_results.slogan: Given an unmixed graph ideal, if two sets of equal size differ by one element and their associated primes form a dominant pair, then their intersection is also a minimal vertex cover. If the graph is bipartite and the union of the sets is a minimal vertex cover, then their intersection is also a minimal vertex cover.
returned_results.name: Lemma 5.5

returned_results.slogan: A maximal matching in a bipartite graph produces a vertex cover derived from that matching. This vertex cover is minimal in size. The construction uses vertices from both parts of the graph based on the matching edges. The result holds for any bipartite graph with a maximal matching.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.2

returned_results.slogan: A subset C of vertices in a graph G is a vertex cover if and only if the prime ideal generated by the variables corresponding to C contains the edge ideal of G. Moreover, C is a minimal vertex cover exactly when that prime ideal is a minimal prime ideal of the edge ideal.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.3

returned_results.slogan: A prime ideal is a minimal prime of the ideal I_G if and only if it is generated by a minimal vertex cover for the graph G.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.2

returned_results.slogan: Minimal generators of first syzygies correspond to cover relations in an intersection-closed poset. The poset is a subset of the power set of n elements. This bijection holds for the ideal associated with the poset's comparability graph.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.5

returned_results.slogan: The minimal primes of the ideal I_G correspond exactly to the minimal vertex covers of the graph G.
returned_results.name: Lemma 5.2

returned_results.slogan: For a graph G with vertices labeled 1 to n, let P be the ideal generated by a set of variables. Then P is a minimal prime ideal of the edge ideal I(G) exactly when the corresponding set of vertices is a minimal vertex cover of G.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.5

trajectory.query: comparison principle for the p-Laplacian torsion function domain monotonicity if B subset Omega then w_Omega >= w_B

returned_results.slogan: If a bounded smooth domain has two functions in a Sobolev space, and the p-Laplacian of one is at least that of the other in the distribution sense, and the first function is less than or equal to the second on the boundary, then the first function is also less than or equal to the second throughout the entire domain.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.5

returned_results.slogan: The p-Laplacian comparison principle states that for two functions in a Sobolev space over a bounded smooth domain, if the p-Laplacian of one is less than or equal to that of the other in the weak sense, and the first function is less than or equal to the second on the boundary, then the same inequality holds throughout the entire domain.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.4

returned_results.slogan: The p-Laplacian comparison principle states that if two functions in a Sobolev space satisfy a weak inequality of their p-Laplacians, and one function is less than or equal to the other on the boundary, then this inequality holds throughout the entire domain.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.2

returned_results.slogan: If u and v are functions defined on a domain and its boundary, and the p-Laplacian of u is at least that of v inside the domain, while both functions are zero on the boundary, then u is less than or equal to v throughout the domain.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.2 (\cite{Kim-Chung10, Park-Chung11}, Theorem A in \cite{Park11})

returned_results.slogan: The weak comparison principle applies to functions in a Sobolev space over a bounded domain. If the p-Laplacian of u is less than or equal to that of v inside the domain, and u is less than or equal to v on the boundary, then u is less than or equal to v throughout the entire domain. This holds for any exponent p strictly between 1 and infinity. The result follows from an integral inequality involving test functions.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.2

returned_results.slogan: For a bounded open set in R^n and a set A in a specific class, the function w_A defined as the p-torsion function of A is a subsolution to the negative p-Laplacian of u equals 1. This means that for all nonnegative test functions in the Sobolev space, the integral inequality involving the gradient of w_A and the test function holds. Additionally, if another subsolution w in the same Sobolev space satisfies the inequality and is nonpositive outside A almost everywhere, then w_A is greater than or equal to w almost everywhere in the domain.
returned_results.name: Lemma 5.2 ((Comparison principle))

returned_results.slogan: Let omega be a bounded domain in R^N with N at least 2, and let a be a non-negative bounded function. Suppose u and v are in the Sobolev space W^1,p of omega and satisfy a weak differential inequality involving the p-Laplacian and the function a. If u is less than or equal to v on the boundary of omega, then u is less than or equal to v throughout omega.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.2

returned_results.slogan: Given open bounded sets Omega contained in U, and a bounded function c, assume c is bounded above by a specific sum involving the p-Laplacian eigenvalue and the torsion function. For functions u and v in a certain space with boundary conditions, if the difference of their p-Laplacian operators minus c times a function g of u and v satisfies an inequality, and one of u or v is bounded, then either u equals v everywhere in Omega or u is strictly greater than v on every compact subset.
returned_results.name: Proposition 6.15 (Strong comparison principle)

returned_results.slogan: If two smooth domains satisfy one contained in the other, and for each domain a p-Laplacian equation is solved with given boundary conditions, then under certain conditions the solutions are ordered. Specifically, if the right-hand side function in the smaller domain is nonnegative and bounded above by that in the larger domain, and the boundary values of the solution on the smaller domain are also bounded above, then the solution in the smaller domain is everywhere less than or equal to the solution from the larger domain restricted to the smaller domain.
returned_results.name: Lemma 5

returned_results.slogan: Let p be greater than 1, and let f be a non-negative continuous function on the reals such that f(t) divided by t to the p minus 1 is non-increasing for small positive t. Suppose u and v are positive, bounded, continuously differentiable functions in a Sobolev space on a domain. If the p-Laplacian of u is at most f(u) and the p-Laplacian of v is at least f(v) in the domain, then u is less than or equal to v everywhere in the domain.
returned_results.name: Lemma 7.3

trajectory.query: explicit formula for the p-torsion function of a ball solution of -Delta_p w = 1 in a ball

returned_results.slogan: For a given positive R, define a radial function u_p on the ball of radius R. The p-norm of the gradient of u_p equals a specific constant involving N, p, R, and the volume of the unit ball. This constant is exactly the p-torsional rigidity of the ball B_R.
returned_results.name: Theorem

returned_results.slogan: A smooth positive function u solves a given equation on a punctured ball. The exponent p is defined by a specific formula. The function u is bounded above by a constant times the absolute value of x raised to the negative p. This bound holds for all x in a smaller punctured ball centered at the origin.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.1

returned_results.slogan: A function whose p-th Laplacian is zero on a ball can be uniquely represented as a sum of p terms. Each term involves a harmonic function multiplied by a specific rational factor. The rational factors depend on the distance from the origin and complex p-th roots of unity. The representation holds for all points inside the ball.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2

returned_results.slogan: An open, bounded, Lipschitz set in R^n contains a positive function f and a weak solution w to a p-Laplace equation with zero boundary conditions. The distribution function of w satisfies a specific differential equation involving f and its decreasing rearrangement. Under this condition, the domain is a ball centered at some point x_0. The solution w and the function f are spherically symmetric and decreasing about x_0.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.2

returned_results.slogan: The solution to a Dirichlet problem involving the p-Laplacian in a bounded open set satisfies an integral identity over balls. This identity relates the integral of the p-power of the gradient to a boundary term and a term involving the source function. The boundary term includes the outward normal and the solution itself. The result holds for almost every radius and center in the space.
returned_results.name: Lemma A.1

returned_results.slogan: On a Riemannian manifold with an isoparametric distance function from a point, the solution to the p-Laplace equation with specified boundary conditions depends only on the distance from that point. The solution is expressed as an integral involving the geometry of geodesic balls and their boundaries. The normal derivative of this solution is constant on the boundary of the geodesic ball. This constant is given by a simple expression involving the volume and surface area of the ball.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.1

returned_results.slogan: The Dirichlet problem for the p-Laplacian on a ball has a unique solution. The solution is expressed as an integral formula involving a sum over p terms. Each term integrates the boundary data f over a rotated segment of the sphere. The kernel in the integral depends on the distance from the point x to the center and the rotation angles.
returned_results.name: Corollary 1

returned_results.slogan: A solution to the p-Laplace equation in a domain G satisfies an integral identity. The p-Dirichlet integral over a ball equals a boundary integral over the sphere. The boundary term involves the gradient magnitude to the power p minus two, multiplied by the function and its normal derivative. This holds for every closed ball contained within the domain.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.11

returned_results.slogan: The function u(x) equals the ratio of |x| to R raised to the power (p-n)/(p-1), where R is (n-p)/(p-1) times C inverse. This function is the only solution to the given problem within the ball of radius R centered at the origin.
returned_results.name: Proposition 1.1 (Model)

returned_results.slogan: The first eigenvalue of the p-Laplacian operator in a ball of radius R in N-dimensional space is given by a formula involving a constant nu sub one of p and theta, divided by R, all raised to the power p. The corresponding eigenfunction depends on the radial distance from the center and is expressed using the same constant.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.1

trajectory.query: torsion function and first Dirichlet eigenvalue rightmost inequality lambda_p and w_Omega

returned_results.slogan: The inequality relates the first eigenvalue, the p-torsion, and the volume of a domain in d-dimensional space. It holds for any domain with finite positive volume and for p between one and infinity. The expression is bounded above by one.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.2

returned_results.slogan: For a bounded smooth domain with nonnegative anisotropic mean curvature, a lower bound is established for the first eigenvalue of the anisotropic p-Laplacian. The bound involves a constant depending on p and the maximum value of the torsion function. The inequality relates these quantities through a specific multiplicative constant. This result holds in dimensions two and higher.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.3

returned_results.slogan: For a non-empty, open, simply connected set in the plane with positive first Dirichlet eigenvalue, the torsion function is bounded above by an expression involving the distance to the boundary, the eigenvalue, and a positive constant. The maximum of the torsion function occurs at a point whose distance to the boundary is at least a constant multiple of the inverse square root of the eigenvalue. This lower bound is optimized over a range of the constant. Under a specified condition, the maximum of the first Dirichlet eigenfunction also occurs at a point with a similar lower bound on the distance to the boundary.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2

returned_results.slogan: The (s,p)-torsion function is bounded and belongs to L-infinity. Its ratio of infinity norm to L1 norm is bounded below by the reciprocal of the domain's measure. The upper bound involves constants, the domain's first eigenvalue, and the eigenvalue of the unit ball. This inequality relates the function's norms to geometric and spectral properties.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2.3

returned_results.slogan: For every open set with finite measure, the torsion function is bounded. An integral inequality holds involving the measure of the set and its symmetric rearrangement. The inequality relates the L-infinity norm of the torsion function to the first eigenvalue. Constants appear in the exponents and denominators of the expression.
returned_results.name: Theorem 12

returned_results.slogan: A bounded open set Omega has a first eigenvalue lambda_1. If a positive function v satisfies an integral inequality for all nonnegative test functions, then lambda_1 is at least lambda. Furthermore, the p-Dirichlet energy of any function u in the Sobolev space is bounded below by lambda times the p-norm of u. This provides a lower bound for the eigenvalue and a Poincare-type inequality.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.2

returned_results.slogan: For a real number theta and p at least 2, an inequality holds for smooth functions with compact support in a domain. The inequality involves integrals of the horizontal gradient and a weight function based on a distance-like function. The constant lambda one is the first eigenvalue of a referenced eigenvalue problem, and it is sharp. The eigenfunction associated with this eigenvalue serves as the maximizing function.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.26

returned_results.slogan: For a real parameter theta and smooth functions with compact support on a domain, an integral inequality holds involving the p-th power of a directional derivative. The left side is bounded below by a constant times another integral of the function weighted by a power of a distance function. The constant lambda one is the first eigenvalue of a referenced eigenvalue problem. The inequality is sharp and the eigenfunction associated with lambda one achieves the optimal constant.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.19

returned_results.slogan: The torsion function is bounded exactly when the principal eigenvalue is positive. The supremum norm of the torsion function is at least the reciprocal of the eigenvalue. It is also at most a constant multiple of the reciprocal of the eigenvalue, multiplied by the logarithm of an expression involving the eigenvalue and a parameter. The constant depends on the dimension and the parameter.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1

returned_results.slogan: For a bounded smooth domain in N-dimensional space, the first eigenvalue of the p-Laplacian is bounded above and below by expressions involving the p-torsion function and the domain's volume. The lower bound depends on a constant related to the volume of the unit ball and the dimension. The upper bound involves the L1 norm of the p-torsion function. These inequalities relate the eigenvalue to the geometry of the domain.
returned_results.name: Proposition 6

trajectory.query: Theorem 1.2 convex sets torsion function bounded above by inradius p-Laplacian convex domain

returned_results.slogan: For a convex domain, an integral inequality holds with an upper bound of one. The p-Laplacian eigenvalue is bounded above and below by expressions involving the infinity norm of the eigenfunction. The eigenvalue is also bounded by terms involving the L1 norm of the eigenfunction and the domain's measure. As p approaches one from above, these bounds converge to the Cheeger constant.
returned_results.name: Theorem 13

returned_results.slogan: For a bounded convex domain in R^d, the gradient of the torsion function is bounded by a constant times a geometric factor involving the domain's inradius and diameter, raised to an exponent, multiplied by powers of the domain's volume and boundary measure. The constant depends only on the dimension and a parameter alpha less than or equal to d. The exponent involving the ratio of inradius to diameter is optimal.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.4

returned_results.slogan: For an open bounded convex set in N-dimensional space and a given p between 1 and infinity, the p-torsional rigidity is bounded below. The lower bound is expressed as a constant divided by the diameter of the set raised to the power p. The constant involves a factor of 2 raised to the power of (p-1)/p. This inequality provides a quantitative estimate for the torsional rigidity.
returned_results.name: Corollary 4.5 (Payne-Weinberger type estimate)

returned_results.slogan: The (s,p)-torsion function is bounded and belongs to L-infinity. Its ratio of infinity norm to L1 norm is bounded below by the reciprocal of the domain's measure. The upper bound involves constants, the domain's first eigenvalue, and the eigenvalue of the unit ball. This inequality relates the function's norms to geometric and spectral properties.
returned_results.name: Corollary 2.3

returned_results.slogan: For any dimension d and exponent p greater than d, there exists a constant depending on p and d such that for every bounded open set, the p-Laplacian eigenvalue raised to the power of one over p is at least that constant divided by the inradius of the set.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.7

returned_results.slogan: For a bounded domain in R2 with boundary in a certain Sobolev-Lorentz space, the infinity norm of the gradient of a solution to the p-Laplacian problem is bounded by a constant times the Lq norm of f, with the constant depending on p and theta. The bound takes one form for p between 1 and 2 and another for p greater than or equal to 2. If the domain is convex instead, the bound simplifies and no longer depends on theta. The constant depends only on q and the domain.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.3

returned_results.slogan: For a bounded, open, convex set in the plane with non-empty interior and constant function f equal to one, the p-torsional rigidity deficit is at least a positive constant K of p multiplied by the ratio of the minimum width to the diameter. The constant K of p is given explicitly in terms of p. The exponent of the width-to-diameter ratio is sharp.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.2

returned_results.slogan: For an open bounded convex set in N-dimensional space and an exponent p between 1 and infinity, the p-Laplacian eigenvalue is bounded below by a constant times the reciprocal of the p-th power of the set's inradius. The constant is given by ((p-1)/p) raised to the power p. This inequality provides a lower estimate for the eigenvalue.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.1

returned_results.slogan: The distance from any maximum point of the torsion function to the boundary is at least the inradius divided by the square root of the dimension. This holds for bounded domains with mean convex boundaries. The result provides a lower bound on how far interior maxima must lie from the boundary.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1

returned_results.slogan: For an open bounded convex set, the torsional rigidity is bounded above by a product involving the set's inradius and diameter. The bound also includes a ratio of modified Bessel functions evaluated at these geometric parameters. The inequality relates the torsional rigidity of the set to that of a ball with the same diameter. Equality occurs exactly when the set is a ball.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.11

trajectory.query: planar multiply connected sets lower bound on first Dirichlet eigenvalue by inradius theorem 3.4 inradius planar multiply connected

returned_results.slogan: For a domain in the plane with connectivity at least two, the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of the Laplacian is bounded below. The bound depends on the connectivity and the inradius of the domain. Specifically, the eigenvalue is at least one divided by the square of the connectivity times the square of the inradius.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1 (Osserman, \cite{Oss})

returned_results.slogan: A simply connected domain in the complex plane has a first Dirichlet eigenvalue for the Laplacian. This eigenvalue is bounded below by a universal constant divided by the square of the domain's inradius. The inradius is the radius of the largest disc contained within the domain. The inequality holds for all such domains.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4

returned_results.slogan: A connected compact set in the plane has a first eigenvalue bounded by a constant times its inradius. The constant is positive and universal, independent of the set. This inequality relates geometric and spectral properties of the set.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.1

returned_results.slogan: The first Dirichlet eigenvalue of the Laplacian on an open convex set in R^d is bounded below. The bound is expressed in terms of the set's inradius. Specifically, the eigenvalue is at least pi squared divided by four times the square of the inradius.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.4 (Hersch-Payne-Stakgold \cite{Hersch1960, Payne1973, Avkhadiev2007})

returned_results.slogan: The theorem provides a lower bound for the first eigenvalue of the magnetic Laplacian on a planar domain with multiple holes. The domain is formed by removing convex sets from a larger convex set. The bound depends on the geometry of the domain and the fluxes of a given closed potential around its inner boundaries. The result is expressed in terms of the minimal and maximal widths of the domain and the distance of the fluxes to the integers.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2

returned_results.slogan: For every open multiply connected set of order k in the plane with finite inradius, the Cheeger constant is at least a constant divided by the square root of k and the inradius. The constant is the same as in a referenced theorem. This lower bound depends on the connectivity order and the inradius. The result applies to sets with positive finite inradius.
returned_results.name: Corollary 5.2

returned_results.slogan: The first eigenvalue of a bounded, finitely connected planar domain is bounded below by the first eigenvalue of a disk with equal area. The bound improves based on how much the domain's inradius falls short of the disk's radius. It also depends on the square root of the minimum area among the complement's components. The improvement factor scales with the cube of the smaller of two geometric ratios.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.1

returned_results.slogan: There exists a constant at least one nine-hundredth such that for any simply connected planar domain with inradius rho, the first eigenvalue of the Dirichlet Laplacian is at least c divided by rho squared.
returned_results.name: Theorem (Hayman, \cite{hay})

returned_results.slogan: An open multiply connected set of order k in the plane satisfies an upper bound on its first Dirichlet eigenvalue. The bound is proportional to k times the square of the Cheeger constant. The constant of proportionality involves the first zero of the Bessel function J_0 and a fixed constant from a referenced theorem.
returned_results.name: Theorem 5.4 (Buser's inequality for planar sets)

returned_results.slogan: The first eigenvalue of the Laplacian on a simply connected planar domain is at least the reciprocal of its conformal radius.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.4

trajectory.query: Proposition 5.1 no reduction generated by two homogeneous polynomials symbolic power ideal I_H^(n) reduction generated by two elements

returned_results.slogan: Given homogeneous polynomials f and g such that the quotient ring by their ideal is one-dimensional and reduced, with f and g having degrees m and n respectively. Assume f is in the m-th power of the ideal of point A, and g is in the n-th power of the ideal of point B, but neither is contained in the ideal of the other point. Define H as the set containing points A and B, plus all points where the ideal generated by f and g is contained in their local ideals. Then the symbolic Rees algebra of the ideal of H is finitely generated.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.5

returned_results.slogan: For n at least 4, the n-th symbolic power of the ideal I has no homogeneous reduction with two generators. A homogeneous minimal reduction is given explicitly, with three generators for n at least 4 and two generators for n equals 3. The reduction number of I with respect to this reduction is always 1.
returned_results.name: Proposition 5.1

returned_results.slogan: The regularity of the n-th symbolic power of a homogeneous ideal I in a ring A is bounded above by n times the regularity of I, assuming the quotient ring A by I has dimension two.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.7

returned_results.slogan: For each n greater than or equal to one, the ideal generated by the n-th powers of h1 through hn equals the ideal generated by h1 to the n and h2 to the n minus one through hn to the n minus one.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.2

returned_results.slogan: For n at least 1, the ideal I_n R is contained in the n-th symbolic power of p. The ideal formed by I_n and x_1 in T is homogeneous. This ideal is also m-primary.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.13

returned_results.slogan: For a homogeneous ideal in a polynomial ring, the symbolic power with exponent equal to the big height times n is contained in the ordinary n-th power. The big height is the maximum height among the associated primes of the ideal. This containment holds for all positive integers n. In particular, the symbolic power with exponent d minus one times n is always contained in the ordinary n-th power.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.1 (Hochster–Huneke, Ein–Lazarsfeld–Smith {\cite{ELS01, HH02}})

returned_results.slogan: For a homogeneous ideal I in a ring A with dimension at most two, let d(I) be the maximum degree of its generators. There exists a constant e such that the regularity of the n-th symbolic power of I is bounded by n times d(I) plus e for all positive integers n.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.8

returned_results.slogan: In a noetherian ring, let an ideal have generation type d. If the symbolic powers of the ideal are contained in certain ordinary powers for indices up to d, then for all positive integers n, the symbolic power with exponent hn minus h plus 1 is contained in the ordinary n-th power.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.10

returned_results.slogan: Let F be a field. Consider an ideal I generated by homogeneous polynomials of degree n in a polynomial ring over F. If the radical of I equals the maximal ideal generated by the variables, then each variable raised to the n-th power lies in I.
returned_results.name: Lemma 6.9

returned_results.slogan: Given a polynomial ring in two variables over a field, consider two homogeneous ideals where one is contained in the other. If the asymptotic growth functions of their powers are equal for all nonnegative real numbers, then the smaller ideal is a reduction of the larger one.
returned_results.name: Lemma 6.3

trajectory.query: Theorem 2.5 argument proving (xi1, xi2)R is a reduction of symbolic power ideal after localization Rees algebra reduction criterion

returned_results.slogan: Let S be a localization of a polynomial ring in finitely many variables over a field K, and let I be an ideal of S. If the quotient ring R equals S divided by I is reduced and generically separable over K, then the kernel of the map from I modulo I squared to the tensor product of R with the module of Kaehler differentials of S over K is the second symbolic power of I modulo I squared.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.31 (Eisenbud-Mazur \cite [Theorem 3]{EM})

returned_results.slogan: In a regular ring R, consider a localization P of a polynomial ring in finitely many variables over R. For an ideal I such that P/I is reduced and generically separable over R, every evolution of P/I is trivial exactly when the second symbolic power of I is contained in the product of the maximal ideal and I.
returned_results.name: Theorem 1.4

returned_results.slogan: Let R be a local domain with maximal ideal m and residue field k, and let I be an ideal without embedded components. If the extended Rees algebra tensored with R localized at P is Noetherian for every prime ideal P not equal to m, then there exists a natural number N. For all natural numbers i, the symbolic power I raised to N times i is contained in the ordinary power I raised to N i. This containment holds after localizing at any prime ideal other than m.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.8

returned_results.slogan: Let R be a Noetherian local ring and E a finite R-module of rank at least two. Given a reduction U of E and certain conditions on depth, the natural map from the Rees algebra of E tensor S modulo x to the Rees algebra of the quotient module is an isomorphism. The element x is also regular on the Rees algebra of E tensor S.
returned_results.name: Theorem 3.1

returned_results.slogan: The symbolic Rees algebra of an ideal in a Noetherian ring localizes compatibly with respect to a multiplicatively closed subset. Localizing the symbolic Rees algebra of the ideal equals the symbolic Rees algebra of the localized ideal. This holds when the ring is Noetherian and the subset is multiplicative. The result expresses an equality of localized algebras.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.1

returned_results.slogan: The Fitting ideal and the ideal generated by certain powers of variables and their products with T become equal after localizing at any element of the form x_r raised to a power times T, for indices between s and n. This holds in the Rees ring of the ideal a with respect to T. The localization process makes these two ideals coincide. The indices s, l, and n are fixed with s less than or equal to l less than or equal to n.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.1

returned_results.slogan: Let R be a quasi-unmixed, analytically unramified local domain with infinite residue field and positive dimension, and let I be an ideal of R. If the S2-ification of the extended Rees algebra S is considered, then the intersection of the nth symbolic power of I with R equals the first symbolic power of I to the n. In particular, if R satisfies the S2 property, then the nth symbolic power of I is exactly the first symbolic power of I to the n for all positive integers n.
returned_results.name: Theorem 6.2

returned_results.slogan: Given positive integers k and l, and elements xi and eta in the k-th and l-th symbolic powers of an ideal I over the integers. If the rational versions of xi and eta satisfy Huneke's condition on the rational ideal, then for all sufficiently large primes p, the reductions modulo p of xi and eta lie in the symbolic powers over the finite field. These reduced elements also satisfy Huneke's condition on the ideal modulo p.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.12

returned_results.slogan: In a two-dimensional Cohen-Macaulay local ring with infinite residue field, let I be an m-primary ideal such that the Ratliff-Rush closure of I to the power r equals I to the power r, where r is the reduction number of I. Suppose x is a regular element in m but not in I, and its initial form in the associated graded ring is regular. If the ideal formed by I and x modulo x is Ratliff-Rush closed, then the regularity of the Rees algebra modulo x equals the regularity of the Rees algebra itself.
returned_results.name: Corollary 5.2

returned_results.slogan: The second symbolic power of I equals the saturation of I squared with respect to Q. The quotient of the second symbolic power by the square of I is isomorphic to R modulo Q.
returned_results.name: Theorem 4.4

trajectory.query: reduction of ideal after localization if maximal ideal of associated graded ring is radical generated by initial forms criterion

returned_results.slogan: Given a reduction ideal generated by monomials for the maximal ideal, several conditions are equivalent. The associated graded ring is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if the initial forms of the monomials form a regular sequence. This is also equivalent to the ring being Cohen-Macaulay and the reduction ideal intersecting powers of the maximal ideal in a specific way. Finally, it is equivalent to the ring being Cohen-Macaulay and each initial form being a non-zero-divisor.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.2

returned_results.slogan: The initial ideal of I with respect to the reverse lexicographic order is used. If a certain ideal formed from I and variables is a minimal reduction of the maximal ideal, then the corresponding ideal formed from the initial ideal and variables is also a minimal reduction of the maximal graded ideal. The reduction numbers of the original ring modulo I and the ring modulo the initial ideal are equal. This equality holds under the stated conditions.
returned_results.name: Lemma

returned_results.slogan: An ideal generated by nonzero elements in a polynomial ring has a certain property if and only if the initial forms of those generators generate the associated graded ideal. This property relates the generators of the ideal to the generators of its graded counterpart. The result holds over a polynomial ring in several variables.
returned_results.name: Lemma 1

returned_results.slogan: The associated graded ring of a Noetherian excellent local ring is assumed to be Cohen-Macaulay. An ideal generated by initial forms of a full system of parameters equals the maximal homogeneous ideal. The corresponding ideal in the original ring then equals the maximal ideal. This holds under the given conditions on the ring and its residue field.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.7

returned_results.slogan: The associated graded ring of a semigroup ring with respect to the maximal ideal is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if the initial forms of the generators of a reduction ideal form a regular sequence. This is also equivalent to the ring being Cohen-Macaulay and each initial form being a non-zero divisor in the associated graded ring.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.3

returned_results.slogan: The ideal a in the localization of a polynomial ring at the maximal ideal generated by the variables is finitely generated if its initial ideal in the polynomial ring is finitely generated. This holds when the polynomial ring is over an arbitrary ring and the set of variables is arbitrary. The result connects finite generation in the localization to finite generation of the initial ideal.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.10

returned_results.slogan: A finitely generated connected graded algebra with a unique maximal graded ideal is reduced if and only if its completion at that maximal ideal is reduced. This is also equivalent to the completion at every maximal ideal being reduced. Additionally, if the associated graded ring with respect to the maximal graded ideal is reduced, then these conditions are satisfied.
returned_results.name: Lemma 5.4

returned_results.slogan: The associated graded ring of the maximal ideal in a quotient ring is isomorphic to a polynomial ring modulo an ideal generated by initial forms. This holds when the generators of the original ideal have no constant terms. The isomorphism preserves the standard grading structure. The result connects the local ring structure to a simpler graded algebra.
returned_results.name: Lemma

returned_results.slogan: A set of elements in the maximal ideal forms a minimal reduction of that ideal if and only if their initial forms constitute a homogeneous system of parameters in the associated graded ring.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.1

returned_results.slogan: For an excellent Noetherian local ring with infinite residue field, if the associated graded ring is Cohen-Macaulay, then the initial ideal of a parameter ideal in the ring equals the ideal generated by the initial forms of those parameters in the graded ring.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.8

trajectory.query: set of elements forms a reduction of an ideal iff their initial forms generate irrelevant ideal associated graded ring local ring

returned_results.slogan: Given a reduction ideal generated by monomials for the maximal ideal, several conditions are equivalent. The associated graded ring is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if the initial forms of the monomials form a regular sequence. This is also equivalent to the ring being Cohen-Macaulay and the reduction ideal intersecting powers of the maximal ideal in a specific way. Finally, it is equivalent to the ring being Cohen-Macaulay and each initial form being a non-zero-divisor.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.2

returned_results.slogan: A set of elements in the maximal ideal forms a minimal reduction of that ideal if and only if their initial forms constitute a homogeneous system of parameters in the associated graded ring.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.1

returned_results.slogan: Let A be a local ring with maximal ideal M and residue field k, and let J be a proper ideal. For elements a1 through as in J, the ideal they generate is a reduction of J if and only if the graded k-algebra formed from the associated graded ring of J modulo the classes of these elements is zero-dimensional.
returned_results.name: Theorem

returned_results.slogan: An ideal generated by nonzero elements in a polynomial ring has a certain property if and only if the initial forms of those generators generate the associated graded ideal. This property relates the generators of the ideal to the generators of its graded counterpart. The result holds over a polynomial ring in several variables.
returned_results.name: Lemma 1

returned_results.slogan: In a noetherian local ring with maximal ideal M, elements x1 through xm in M generate a reduction of M if and only if the associated graded ring modulo the classes of these elements in M over M squared has dimension zero. This equivalence relates the reduction property to a condition on the graded ring structure. The result holds without assuming the ring is regular.
returned_results.name: Theorem

returned_results.slogan: The associated graded ring of a semigroup ring with respect to the maximal ideal is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if the initial forms of the generators of a reduction ideal form a regular sequence. This is also equivalent to the ring being Cohen-Macaulay and each initial form being a non-zero divisor in the associated graded ring.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.3

returned_results.slogan: The initial ideal of I with respect to the reverse lexicographic order is used. If a certain ideal formed from I and variables is a minimal reduction of the maximal ideal, then the corresponding ideal formed from the initial ideal and variables is also a minimal reduction of the maximal graded ideal. The reduction numbers of the original ring modulo I and the ring modulo the initial ideal are equal. This equality holds under the stated conditions.
returned_results.name: Lemma

returned_results.slogan: The ideal generated by the given powers of the elements is a minimal reduction of the specified ideal. There exists an integer such that the ideal raised to any power beyond that integer equals a sum of products involving the elements and lower powers of the ideal. The initial forms of the elements form a system of parameters for the associated graded ring. These three conditions are equivalent.
returned_results.name: Theorem 2.1

returned_results.slogan: The length of the quotient of the associated graded ring by the ideal generated by the images of certain elements is finite if and only if those elements form a reduction of a specific power of the module. This equivalence holds under the condition that the module is finitely generated and the quotient of the free module by the module has finite length. The elements are taken from a fixed positive power of the module. Their images are considered modulo the product of the initial form ideal and that same power.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.1

returned_results.slogan: A local ring with an infinite residue field has an ideal I and elements a_i in I. The ideal generated by these elements is a minimal reduction of I if and only if their initial forms form a homogeneous system of parameters for the fiber cone of I.
returned_results.name: Proposition 3.8

trajectory.query: symbolic Rees algebra localizes compatibly localized symbolic Rees algebra equals symbolic Rees algebra of localized ideal

returned_results.slogan: The symbolic Rees algebra of an ideal in a Noetherian ring localizes compatibly with respect to a multiplicatively closed subset. Localizing the symbolic Rees algebra of the ideal equals the symbolic Rees algebra of the localized ideal. This holds when the ring is Noetherian and the subset is multiplicative. The result expresses an equality of localized algebras.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.1

returned_results.slogan: The localization of the Rees algebra of an ideal in a commutative ring equals the Rees algebra of the localized ideal. This holds when localizing with respect to a multiplicative subset. The result connects the behavior of the Rees algebra under localization. It shows that forming the Rees algebra commutes with the localization process.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.1

returned_results.slogan: Given a ring S essentially of finite type over a subring B, with a multiplicatively closed subset W of S, let V be the intersection of W and B, and I an ideal of S such that localizing I at W and intersecting with S gives I back. Then the n-th symbolic power of the localization of I at W with respect to B equals that with respect to the localization of B at V. The n-th symbolic power of I with respect to B equals the intersection with S of the n-th symbolic power of the localized ideal with respect to B. Also, localizing the n-th symbolic power of I with respect to B at W gives the n-th symbolic power of the localized ideal with respect to B.
returned_results.name: Lemma 3.4 (\cite{DiffSig})

returned_results.slogan: For a Noetherian ring and an ideal, the localization of a power of the ideal equals the power of its localization at any prime ideal. The same holds for symbolic powers. If the symbolic power is not contained in the regular power in a local or graded ring, this noncontainment also holds after localizing at the maximal ideal. Conversely, if a noncontainment occurs at some prime ideal after localization, then it holds globally. If containment holds at all associated primes of the regular power, then the symbolic power is contained in the regular power.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.6

returned_results.slogan: A normal excellent domain R with a flag of prime ideals Delta and a prime ideal p containing Delta has an inclusion of its symbolic Rees algebra. This inclusion maps into the symbolic Rees algebra with respect to the join of p and Delta. The latter algebra equals the symbolic Rees algebra of the localization of the original algebra at p.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.1.8

returned_results.slogan: If J is an ideal of A, then for any integer e, the e-th symbolic power of the localization of J at W exists. This symbolic power equals the localization at W of the e-th symbolic power of the contraction of the localized ideal back to A.
returned_results.name: Lemma 8

returned_results.slogan: Let R be a local domain with maximal ideal m and residue field k, and let I be an ideal without embedded components. If the extended Rees algebra tensored with R localized at P is Noetherian for every prime ideal P not equal to m, then there exists a natural number N. For all natural numbers i, the symbolic power I raised to N times i is contained in the ordinary power I raised to N i. This containment holds after localizing at any prime ideal other than m.
returned_results.name: Proposition 2.8

returned_results.slogan: If the extended Rees algebra of the ideal I over the ring S is Cohen-Macaulay, then the Rees algebra of I over R is also Cohen-Macaulay. Under the assumption that both R and S are localized at their irrelevant maximal ideals, the converse holds. In that case, if the Rees algebra of I over R is Cohen-Macaulay, then the extended Rees algebra over S is Cohen-Macaulay. This establishes an equivalence under specific localization conditions.
returned_results.name: Proposition 4.7

returned_results.slogan: For each index j in an index set J, the s-th symbolic power of the localization of a ring R at j equals the localization at j of the s-th symbolic power of R.
returned_results.name: Lemma 4.1

returned_results.slogan: The first symbolic power ring modulo its first symbolic power ideal is isomorphic to the integral closure of the first symbolic power ring. The localization at a prime ideal equals the localization of the first symbolic power ring at its corresponding prime ideal.
returned_results.name: Lemma 2.15
